1.pq: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.

p: Faith is not a feeling. It is a decision to trust God before you can see the outcome.
Today, think about a place in your life where you're being asked to move forward without yet knowing how things will turn out.
Before we begin, ask God to help you trust Him with what you cannot yet see.

pages.q: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.

pages.prompt: Where in your life right now do you need to trust God more than you currently do?

o.l: I can trust Him with a decision I keep putting off
o.r:
Putting off a decision often feels safer than actually deciding. But delay is still a choice. It just postpones the moment you finally trust God with the outcome.

Bring this decision to Him today, honestly, and ask for the courage to move forward, even before every answer feels certain.

o.l: I can trust Him with a relationship I can't control
o.r:
You cannot control another person's heart, their choices, or their timing. What you can control is your own faith in the middle of that uncertainty.

Bring this relationship to God, and trust that He is working in ways you cannot yet see, even in what feels most out of your hands.

o.l: I can trust Him with a fear I haven't spoken out loud
o.r:
A fear kept silent tends to grow heavier the longer it stays unspoken. Naming it, even just to God, is often the first real step toward trusting Him with it.

Speak it honestly in prayer today. He already knows. He is simply waiting for you to bring it to Him.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r:
Whatever is on your heart today, God already knows it fully, even before you find the words for it.

Bring it to Him honestly, in your own way, and trust that He is listening closely, exactly where you are.

p: Faith rarely feels certain. It feels like taking one step forward without seeing the whole staircase.
That is not weakness. That is exactly what faith is for.

Alma taught that “faith is not to have a perfect knowledge of things.” If you have faith, you hope “for things which are not seen, which are true.” Faith rests on what is real, even before you can see it.
God is not asking you to have all the answers. He is asking you to trust the One who does.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Alma 32:21
Write down one thing you are trusting God with this week.

pages.q: Faith in Jesus Christ is the foundation of all belief and the conduit of divine power.

2.pq: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.

p: God does not need your prayers to know what you need. He wants your prayers because that is how a relationship works.
Today, think about whether your prayers feel like a conversation or a routine.
Before we begin, pray simply, and mean every word of it.

pages.q: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.

pages.prompt: What would change if you prayed today the way you'd talk to someone you trust completely?

o.l: I can stop reciting and start speaking honestly
o.r: Prayers filled with memorized words can start to feel hollow. Try speaking today's prayer exactly the way you'd talk to someone who already loves you completely.

o.l: I can ask for something specific instead of something vague
o.r: A vague prayer is easy to forget you ever prayed. Name the actual thing you need, clearly, and watch how differently it feels to bring it to God.

o.l: I can make space to actually listen after I pray
o.r: Prayer isn't only talking. Try staying quiet for a moment after you finish, and see what settles in the silence.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Whatever today's prayer needs to be, bring it honestly. God is far more interested in your sincerity than your wording.

p: God is not distant. He is not waiting for perfect words.
Jesus Christ told the Nephites, “ye must always pray unto the Father in my name.” So you speak to Heavenly Father, and you close in the name of Jesus Christ.
He is waiting for you, exactly as you are, with whatever is actually on your mind.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 3 Nephi 18:19-21
Pray tonight in your own words and close in the name of Jesus Christ.

pages.q: Prayer is the key to the heart of God.

3.pq: In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.

p: It is easy to notice what is missing from your life. It takes real effort to notice what is already there.
Today, think about the last time you truly paused to thank God, not out of habit, but because you meant it.
Before we begin, name one specific thing you are grateful for right now.

pages.q: In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.

pages.prompt: What is one thing you have been overlooking that actually deserves your gratitude today?

o.l: I can thank God for a person I've taken for granted
o.r: Take a moment today to actually name that person to God, and thank Him specifically for what they've given you.

o.l: I can thank God for a trial that taught me something
o.r: Even hard seasons can carry a hidden gift. Thank God today for what that trial ended up teaching you.

o.l: I can thank God for something so ordinary I never think to mention it
o.r: The most overlooked blessings are often the most constant ones. Notice one today, and simply say thank you.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However gratitude shows up for you today, let it be specific and sincere, not just a passing thought.

p: Gratitude does not wait for everything to be perfect. It notices what is good even in the middle of what is hard.
The Lord taught that “he who receiveth all things with thankfulness shall be made glorious.” Thankfulness is more than good manners. The Lord ties a promise to it.
A grateful heart is not naive. It is simply paying attention.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 78:19
Write down three blessings from your day and thank God for each one out loud.

pages.q: A grateful heart notices what an anxious heart overlooks.

4.pq: Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows.

p: There is no version of your pain, your mistakes, or your loneliness that Christ has not already carried.
Today, think about a burden you've been carrying alone that you were never meant to carry alone.
Before we begin, bring that burden to Him, honestly, without pretending it's lighter than it is.

pages.q: Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows.

pages.prompt: What is one thing you are currently trying to carry by yourself that Christ has already offered to carry with you?

o.l: I can bring Him a sin I haven't fully let go of
o.r: Christ already knows. Bring it to Him honestly today, and let yourself actually receive the forgiveness He's offering.

o.l: I can bring Him a grief I haven't processed
o.r: Grief carried alone grows heavier. Bring this grief to Him today, and let Him help carry what you've been holding by yourself.

o.l: I can bring Him a fear I keep pushing down
o.r: A fear you keep pushing away doesn't disappear. It just waits. Bring it into the light today, honestly, in prayer.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Whatever weight you're carrying today, Christ has already offered to carry it with you. Let Him.

p: The Atonement is not just for the moment you die. It is for this Tuesday, this ordinary hard day, this exact weight you are carrying right now.

Alma taught that the Savior would “take upon him the pains and the sicknesses of his people.” He did this “that he may know according to the flesh how to succor his people.” To succor is to help. He knows how to help you because He has felt what you feel.
He already knows. He is already willing. The only question is whether you will let Him.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Alma 7:11-13
Name one burden in prayer and ask the Savior to help you carry it.

pages.q: There is no burden Christ has not already offered to carry with you.

5.pq: And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone.

p: No family is perfect. But every family is a place where God intended real love to be practiced, even imperfectly.
Today, think about one relationship in your family that could use a little more patience from you.
Before we begin, pray for the people in your family by name.

pages.q: And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone.

pages.prompt: What is one small way you could strengthen a family relationship this week?

o.l: I can reach out to someone I haven't spoken to in a while
o.r: A short message today could mean more than you expect. Reach out to that person you've been meaning to reconnect with.

o.l: I can forgive something I've been holding onto
o.r: Family relationships often carry old wounds. Choose today to release one you've been holding onto longer than it deserves.

o.l: I can simply spend unhurried time with someone I love
o.r: Put away distractions today and give someone in your family your full, unhurried attention, even briefly.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However you strengthen family today, let it be intentional. These relationships are worth the effort they ask of you.

p: Family was never meant to be easy. It was meant to be eternal.
God created man and woman in His own image. Then He blessed them and said, “Be fruitful, and multiply.” Family has been part of His plan from the beginning.
That is exactly why it is worth the patience, the forgiveness, and the effort it asks of you.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Moses 2:27-28
Call or message one family member today, just to ask how they are.

pages.q: Family was never meant to be easy. It was meant to be eternal.

6.pq: Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.

p: You do not need a title, a calling, or a plan to serve someone today. You only need to notice them.
Today, think of someone near you who is carrying something you could help lighten.
Before we begin, ask God to show you who needs you today.

pages.q: Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.

pages.prompt: Who is someone you could quietly serve today, without being asked?

o.l: I can help someone with something practical, no explanation needed
o.r: Notice a practical need today and simply meet it, without waiting to be asked or needing to explain why.

o.l: I can simply listen to someone who needs to be heard
o.r: Sometimes the most valuable service is simply listening, fully, without rushing to fix or respond.

o.l: I can forgive someone before they even ask for it
o.r: Real service sometimes looks like forgiving first, before an apology ever comes.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However service shows up for you today, let it be quiet and genuine, not performed for notice.

p: Service rarely looks dramatic. Most of the time, it looks like showing up for someone in a small, unnoticed way.
King Benjamin taught his people, “when ye are in the service of your fellow beings ye are only in the service of your God.” Every act of help counts as service to Him.
That is exactly the kind of service Christ noticed most.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Mosiah 2:17
Do one quiet act of service today and tell no one about it.

pages.q: Service rarely looks dramatic. Most of the time, it looks like showing up.

7.pq: And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three.

p: Hope is not pretending things are fine. Hope is trusting that God is still working, even when things are not fine yet.
Today, think about a situation in your life that feels unfinished or unresolved.
Before we begin, ask God to help you hold onto hope, even without a timeline.

pages.q: And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three.

pages.prompt: Where do you most need to hold onto hope right now?

o.l: I can hold onto hope for a relationship that feels strained
o.r: A strained relationship doesn't have to stay that way forever. Hold onto hope for it today, even without knowing exactly how it heals.

o.l: I can hold onto hope for a situation I can't control
o.r: Some situations are simply out of your hands. Choose today to hold onto hope anyway, trusting God is still working.

o.l: I can hold onto hope for a version of myself I'm still becoming
o.r: You are not finished growing. Hold onto hope for who you're still becoming, even on days that feel like setbacks.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Wherever you need hope today, choose to hold onto it, not naively, but as an act of real trust in God.

p: God is not finished with your story. What feels unresolved today is not necessarily unresolved forever.
Moroni wrote that hope “cometh of faith” and “maketh an anchor to the souls of men.” Hope holds you steady when the water is rough.
Hope is simply choosing to keep walking, even before you can see how it ends.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Ether 12:4
Write down one thing you are hoping for, then pray for the patience to wait for it.

pages.q: Hope is simply choosing to keep walking, even before you can see how it ends.

8.pq: Though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow.

p: Repentance is not a punishment. It is the way back to who you were always meant to become.
Today, think about something you've been avoiding bringing to God, not because He doesn't already know, but because you haven't yet let yourself be honest about it.
Before we begin, ask God for the courage to be honest with Him today.

pages.q: Though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow.

pages.prompt: What is one thing you've been carrying that you could finally bring to God today?

o.l: I can confess something I've been avoiding
o.r: Avoidance doesn't make it lighter. Bring this honestly to God today, and let the weight actually start to lift.

o.l: I can forgive myself for something I've already repented of
o.r: If you've genuinely repented, God has already forgiven you. Today, practice forgiving yourself too.

o.l: I can start changing a pattern I know isn't right
o.r: Real repentance shows up in changed action. Start today, even imperfectly, on the pattern you already know needs to shift.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Whatever repentance looks like for you today, take the honest step. God meets you exactly there.

p: Repentance is not about proving you're sorry enough. It is about turning, actually turning, toward the person God knows you can be.
Amulek urged the people, “now is the time and the day of your salvation.” He promised that if we repent and do not harden our hearts, the great plan of redemption begins to work for us right away.
He is not keeping score. He is holding the door open.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Alma 34:31-34
Pray tonight and tell Heavenly Father honestly what you want to change.

pages.q: Repentance is not a punishment. It is the way back to who you were always meant to become.

9.pq: Ye ought to forgive one another: for he that forgiveth not his brother his trespasses standeth condemned before the Lord.

p: Forgiveness is not saying what happened was okay. It is deciding not to let it own you anymore.
Today, think about someone you've been holding something against, even if they never apologized, even if they never will.
Before we begin, ask God to help you release what you've been holding onto.

pages.q: Ye ought to forgive one another: for he that forgiveth not his brother his trespasses standeth condemned before the Lord.

pages.prompt: Who is someone you might need to begin forgiving today?

o.l: I can forgive someone who never said sorry
o.r: Forgiveness was never meant to depend on an apology. Choose today to release this, for your own sake as much as theirs.

o.l: I can forgive myself for something I keep replaying
o.r: You've relived this enough times. Let today be the day you finally let yourself off the hook.

o.l: I can let go of something small before it becomes something big
o.r: Small resentments grow quietly if left alone. Release this one today, before it becomes something heavier.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However forgiveness looks today, choose it deliberately. It is a gift you give yourself as much as anyone else.

p: Unforgiveness feels like protection. It is actually a weight you keep choosing to carry.

Peter asked how often he should forgive his brother: “till seven times?” Jesus Christ answered, “Until seventy times seven.” In our day the Lord said, “of you it is required to forgive all men.” Forgiveness is not something to count.
Letting go does not mean what happened didn't matter. It means you refuse to let it define what happens next.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Matthew 18:21-22
Pray for the person you need to forgive. Ask God to help you want good for them.

pages.q: Unforgiveness feels like protection. It is actually a weight you keep choosing to carry.

10.pq: The Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things.

p: You were never meant to figure out this life entirely on your own.
Today, think about a decision in front of you where you haven't yet stopped to actually listen for guidance.
Before we begin, sit in silence for a moment and simply ask.

pages.q: The Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things.

pages.prompt: Where in your life could you use more spiritual guidance right now?

o.l: I can ask for direction on a decision I've been putting off
o.r: Bring that decision to God today and genuinely ask for direction, then take time to actually listen.

o.l: I can ask for comfort in something that's been weighing on me
o.r: Ask God today for comfort in this specific burden, and trust He can reach exactly where you are.

o.l: I can simply ask to feel closer to God today
o.r: Sometimes the simplest prayer is the most honest one: just ask to feel closer to Him today.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However you seek the Spirit today, come with real openness. He responds to sincerity, not perfect words.

p: The Holy Ghost does not shout. He speaks in impressions, in peace, in quiet certainty.
The Lord told Oliver Cowdery that He would speak “in your mind and in your heart, by the Holy Ghost.” That is how the Spirit speaks: through your thoughts and your feelings.
If you've never noticed Him before, that does not mean He hasn't been speaking. It may simply mean you haven't yet learned to listen.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 8:2-3
Sit quietly for two minutes, ask God one question, and write down any thought that comes.

pages.q: The Holy Ghost speaks quietly. Learning to listen is a lifelong practice.

11.pq: Lying lips are abomination to the Lord: but they that deal truly are his delight.

p: Small dishonesties feel harmless until you realize how much they cost you in trust, with others and with yourself.
Today, think about one place in your life where a small compromise has become a habit.
Before we begin, ask God to help you see yourself clearly.

pages.q: Lying lips are abomination to the Lord: but they that deal truly are his delight.

pages.prompt: Where could a little more honesty change something in your life today?

o.l: I can stop a small dishonesty I've let become normal
o.r: Notice the small dishonesty you've grown used to, and choose today to stop it, even if no one else would ever know.

o.l: I can be honest with someone about how I actually feel
o.r: Say the honest thing today, even if it's uncomfortable. Clarity is usually kinder than a comfortable half-truth.

o.l: I can be honest with myself about something I've been avoiding
o.r: Stop avoiding it. Be honest with yourself today about what you already know is true.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Whatever honesty asks of you today, choose it. Trust, once broken by small dishonesties, is hard to rebuild.

p: Honesty is not just about avoiding lies. It is about becoming someone whose word can actually be trusted, starting with yourself.
The thirteenth article of faith says, “We believe in being honest, true, chaste, benevolent, virtuous.” Honesty comes first in that list.
Integrity is who you are when explaining yourself would be easier than telling the truth.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Articles of Faith 1:13
Choose one small place to tell the whole truth today, even when it is easier not to.

pages.q: Integrity is who you are when no one else would ever know the difference.

12.pq: Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time.

p: Humility is not thinking less of yourself. It is thinking of yourself less, and of God more.
Today, think about a moment recently when you were more focused on being right than being teachable.
Before we begin, ask God to soften whatever in you resists correction.

pages.q: Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time.

pages.prompt: Where in your life could a little more humility open a door?

o.l: I can admit I was wrong about something instead of defending it
o.r: Let go of the need to be right today, and simply admit where you were wrong.

o.l: I can listen to feedback instead of resisting it
o.r: The next time feedback comes today, resist the urge to defend yourself first, just listen.

o.l: I can let go of needing to be seen as capable all the time
o.r: You don't have to have it all together today. Let go of that pressure, even briefly.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However humility shows up today, let it open a door instead of closing one.

p: Pride closes doors. It cannot receive counsel, cannot admit fault, cannot grow.
The Lord said, “I give unto men weakness that they may be humble.” He added, “my grace is sufficient for all men that humble themselves before me.” Humility is where His grace begins to help you.
Humility is what makes room for God to actually work in you, not because you are small, but because you are willing.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Ether 12:27
Ask someone for advice today, and listen without defending yourself.

pages.q: Humility is thinking of yourself less, and of God more.

13.pq: Let us run with patience the race that is set before us.

p: Some answers come immediately. Most of what matters comes slowly, on God's timeline, not yours.
Today, think about something you've been praying for that hasn't resolved yet.
Before we begin, ask God for peace, not just for an answer.

pages.q: Let us run with patience the race that is set before us.

pages.prompt: Where do you most need patience with God's timing right now?

o.l: I can wait for an answer instead of forcing my own solution
o.r: Resist the urge to force a solution today, and instead wait, trusting God's timing over your own.

o.l: I can be patient with someone else's process of growth
o.r: Someone in your life is growing more slowly than you'd like. Be patient with their process today.

o.l: I can be patient with my own slow progress
o.r: Your own growth may feel slower than you want. Practice patience with yourself today, exactly where you are.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Wherever patience is tested today, choose it deliberately. Most things worth having take longer than we'd prefer.

p: Patience is not passive waiting. It is active trust, believing God is still working, even when nothing visible seems to be happening.
Alma and his people learned that the Lord “trieth their patience and their faith.” Then came the promise: “whosoever putteth his trust in him the same shall be lifted up at the last day.”
The timeline is His. The trust is yours to choose.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Mosiah 23:21-22
Name one thing you are waiting on. Pray, then do one thing to move it forward.

pages.q: Patience is active trust, not passive waiting.

14.pq: Charity suffereth long, and is kind.

p: Charity is not a feeling you have. It is a decision you make, over and over, especially when it's inconvenient.
Today, think about someone difficult to love, and choose to love them anyway, today.
Before we begin, ask God for His love for someone you find hard to love.

pages.q: Charity suffereth long, and is kind.

pages.prompt: Who in your life could use a little more patience and kindness from you today?

o.l: I can be patient with someone who frustrates me
o.r: The next time that person frustrates you today, choose patience instead of an immediate reaction.

o.l: I can show kindness without expecting anything back
o.r: Offer kindness today to someone who can't repay it, and let that be enough.

o.l: I can choose love even when I don't feel like it
o.r: You won't always feel loving. Choose it anyway today, as an act of will, not just emotion.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However charity shows up today, let it cost you something real. That's what makes it genuine.

p: Mormon taught that “charity is the pure love of Christ, and it endureth forever.” He also said how to receive it: “pray unto the Father with all the energy of heart, that ye may be filled with this love.”
It is not a feeling that arrives. It is a choice you keep making until it becomes who you are.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Moroni 7:45-48
Do one kind thing today for someone who is hard to love.

pages.q: Charity is love that costs you something and gives anyway.

15.pq: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally.

p: God does not only speak through prophets to the world. He speaks personally, to you, about your life.
Today, think about a question you've never actually taken to God directly.
Before we begin, ask Him that exact question, and wait for an answer.

pages.q: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally.

pages.prompt: What is a question you could bring directly to God today?

o.l: I can ask Him about a decision I've been unsure of
o.r: Bring that uncertain decision directly to God today, and ask Him plainly for guidance.

o.l: I can ask Him to help me understand something I've struggled with
o.r: Ask God today to help you understand the thing that's been confusing you, and stay open to how the answer comes.

o.l: I can simply ask Him what He wants me to know right now
o.r: Sometimes the best prayer is simple: ask God today what He wants you to know right now.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However you seek personal revelation today, ask sincerely and expect that God is willing to answer.

p: You do not need someone else to receive answers meant for you. God is willing to speak directly, personally, to anyone who genuinely asks.
The Lord told Oliver Cowdery how revelation comes: “you must study it out in your mind; then you must ask me if it be right.” Then comes the answer: “you shall feel that it is right.”
The question is not whether He will answer. The question is whether you're truly listening.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 9:7-9
Write one question to God. Read Doctrine and Covenants 9:8, then pray about it and listen.

pages.q: God is willing to speak directly, personally, to anyone who genuinely asks.

16.pq: To obey is better than sacrifice.

p: Obedience is not about proving yourself to God. It is about trusting that His way leads somewhere good.
Today, think about a commandment you understand the reason for, and one you don't, and choose to trust Him with both.
Before we begin, ask God to help you trust Him even where you don't yet see why.

pages.q: To obey is better than sacrifice.

pages.prompt: Where could a little more obedience change your life for the better right now?

o.l: I can follow a commandment I've been putting off
o.r: There's a commandment you've been delaying. Take one honest step toward it today.

o.l: I can trust a counsel I've been resisting
o.r: Some counsel is hard to accept. Choose today to trust it, even without fully understanding every reason yet.

o.l: I can obey even without fully understanding why yet
o.r: You don't need every answer before you obey. Trust today, and let understanding come later.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However obedience shows up today, remember it is trust in action, not blind rule-following.

p: Obedience is not blind. It is trust, choosing to follow a Father who has never once led you wrong.
Joseph Smith taught, “when we obtain any blessing from God, it is by obedience to that law upon which it is predicated.” Blessings and obedience belong together.
The blessings He promises are not bribes. They are simply what naturally follows a life aligned with truth.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 130:20-21
Pick one commandment and keep it fully today. Notice how it feels.

pages.q: Obedience is not blind. It is trust in a Father who has never once led you wrong.

17.pq: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.

p: The Sabbath is not a restriction. It is a gift. One day set apart to remember what actually matters most.
Today, think about how your Sundays actually feel, and whether they draw you closer to God or just feel like rules.
Before we begin, ask God to help you see the Sabbath as rest, not obligation.

pages.q: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.

pages.prompt: What is one thing you could do this Sunday to make it feel more like a gift than a rule?

o.l: I can spend unhurried time in scripture or prayer
o.r: Set aside unhurried time this Sunday for scripture or prayer. Let it be rest, not another task.

o.l: I can reach out to someone who needs connection
o.r: Use part of your Sabbath today to reach out to someone who could use connection.

o.l: I can simply rest, without guilt, from the noise of the week
o.r: Give yourself permission today to genuinely rest, without guilt, from the noise of the week.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However you keep the Sabbath today, let it feel like a gift, not one more obligation.

p: The Sabbath was made to give you something, not to take something away.
The Lord calls His holy day “a day appointed unto you to rest from your labors, and to pay thy devotions unto the Most High.” Rest and worship are part of the same gift.
One day, set apart, to remember whose you are. That is not a burden. That is rest for a soul that needs it.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 59:9-13
Choose one thing to do this Sunday that helps you feel close to God.

pages.q: The Sabbath was made to give you something, not take something away.

18.pq: I saw two Personages, whose brightness and glory defy all description.

p: In 1820, fourteen-year-old Joseph Smith went into the woods to pray. God the Father and His Son Jesus Christ appeared to him.
Today, think about what it means that God is still willing to answer sincere questions, exactly as He did then.
Before we begin, ask God a real question of your own, and expect a real answer.

pages.q: I saw two Personages, whose brightness and glory defy all description.

pages.prompt: What does the Restoration mean to you personally, beyond just history?

o.l: It means God still speaks through living prophets today
o.r: Let that truth settle in today: the same God who spoke to prophets anciently is still speaking, now, through a living prophet.

o.l: It means my questions matter enough for God to answer
o.r: Your honest questions were never too small for God. Bring one to Him today, and expect a real answer.

o.l: It means the fullness of the gospel is available to me right now
o.r: The fullness of the gospel isn't locked away in history. It's available to you, fully, today.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However the Restoration speaks to you today, let it remind you that God's work with His children is not finished.

p: The Restoration was not a single event that ended in a grove of trees. It continues every time God answers an honest question with an honest heart.
Joseph wrote that he saw “two Personages, whose brightness and glory defy all description.” One of them said, pointing to the other, “This is My Beloved Son. Hear Him!”
That includes yours.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Joseph Smith—History 1:15-20
Pray with a real question today and write down what you feel afterward.

pages.q: The Restoration continues every time God answers an honest question with an honest heart.

19.pq: And if ye shall ask with a sincere heart, with real intent, having faith in Christ, he will manifest the truth of it unto you…

p: The Book of Mormon was not written to be admired. It was written to bring people to Christ.
Today, think about whether you've actually tested its promise, or just heard about it secondhand.
Before we begin, ask God directly whether it is true.

pages.q: And if ye shall ask with a sincere heart, with real intent, having faith in Christ, he will manifest the truth of it unto you, by the power of the Holy Ghost.

pages.prompt: Have you personally asked God about the Book of Mormon's truth?

o.l: I can read a portion of it with real intent this week
o.r: Choose a portion to read this week with genuine, real intent, not just to finish, but to actually seek truth.

o.l: I can pray about it sincerely, expecting an answer
o.r: Pray about the Book of Mormon today, sincerely, and actually expect that God will answer.

o.l: I can revisit a part of it I've read before with fresh eyes
o.r: Return today to a passage you've read before, and see what it says to you now, at this point in your life.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However you engage with the Book of Mormon today, come with an open heart. That is what the promise requires.

p: The invitation was never to simply believe what others say about this book. It was to find out for yourself.
Moroni promised that “by the power of the Holy Ghost ye may know the truth of all things.” The way to know is to ask God.
That promise still stands, for anyone willing to ask.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Moroni 10:3-5
Read one page of the Book of Mormon, then pray and ask if it is true.

pages.q: The invitation was never to believe what others say about this book. It was to find out for yourself.

20.pq: Organize yourselves; prepare every needful thing; and establish a house, even a house of prayer, a house of fasting…

p: Temples are not just beautiful buildings. They are where heaven and earth meet, and where families become eternal.
Today, think about your own connection to the temple, whether you've been, or whether it still feels distant.
Before we begin, ask God to help you understand why this sacred place matters.

pages.q: Organize yourselves; prepare every needful thing; and establish a house, even a house of prayer, a house of fasting, a house of faith, a house of learning, a house of glory, a house of order, a house of God.

pages.prompt: What is one step you could take toward the temple, wherever you currently are on that path?

o.l: I can learn more about what happens inside
o.r: Take a step today to learn more about what actually happens inside the temple, and why it matters.

o.l: I can work toward a temple recommend
o.r: If a temple recommend still feels distant, take one honest step toward it today.

o.l: I can do family history work that connects me to it
o.r: Family history work is part of what connects you to temple worship. Spend a little time on it today.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However you draw closer to the temple today, remember it's a process of becoming willing, not becoming perfect.

p: The temple is not reserved for the perfect. It is prepared for the willing.
When His people build a house to Him in His name, the Lord promised, “my glory shall rest upon it.” And “all the pure in heart that shall come into it shall see God.”
Whatever your relationship with it looks like today, God is patient, and the door remains open.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 97:15-16
If you can, plan a visit to the temple. If not yet, write down one step toward it.

pages.q: The temple is not reserved for the perfect. It is prepared for the willing.

21.pq: Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature.

p: Sharing the gospel is not about being pushy. It is about caring enough to let someone know what has mattered so much to you.
Today, think of one person in your life who might be open to a genuine conversation about faith.
Before we begin, ask God to give you courage, not a script.

pages.q: Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature.

pages.prompt: Who is someone you could have a genuine conversation about faith with this week?

o.l: I can invite someone to an activity or event
o.r: Think of someone today you could invite to an activity or event. A simple, low-pressure first step.

o.l: I can simply share something meaningful that's helped me
o.r: Share with someone today something meaningful that has genuinely helped your own faith.

o.l: I can just listen to where someone else is in their own journey
o.r: Instead of talking today, simply listen to where someone else actually is in their own journey of faith.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However missionary work shows up today, let it come from care, not obligation.

p: You do not need all the answers to share what you know. You only need to care enough to say something real.
The Lord told the early Saints, “it becometh every man who hath been warned to warn his neighbor.” Sharing what you know is part of that duty.
The rest, timing, readiness, the outcome, belongs to God.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 88:81
Pray for one person by name, then ask God what you could say to them.

pages.q: Sharing the gospel is an act of love, not a sales pitch.

22.pq: All these things shall give thee experience, and shall be for thy good.

p: Trials are not evidence that God has abandoned you. Often, they are the very place He is shaping you most.
Today, think about a hard season you're in, and consider what it might be teaching you.
Before we begin, ask God to help you see purpose, even in pain.

pages.q: All these things shall give thee experience, and shall be for thy good.

pages.prompt: What is a current trial you could ask God to help you find meaning in?

o.l: I can ask what this trial is teaching me
o.r: Instead of only asking why, ask God today what this trial might be teaching you.

o.l: I can ask for strength to get through today, not the whole future
o.r: You don't need strength for the whole future right now. Only for today. Ask for that.

o.l: I can ask to see God's hand, even in something hard
o.r: Ask God today to help you see His hand, even in the middle of something genuinely hard.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However you carry this trial today, trust that God has not left you to carry it alone.

p: Not every trial makes sense in the moment. Some only make sense looking back, once you see what they built in you.

When Joseph Smith was in Liberty Jail, the Lord told him, “The Son of Man hath descended below them all. Art thou greater than he?” Jesus Christ understands the lowest places. And “God shall be with you forever and ever.”
God does not waste pain. He redeems it.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 122:5-9
Write down one thing a hard season has already taught you.

pages.q: Trials are often the very place God is shaping you most.

23.pq: We will make an earth whereon these may dwell.

p: You did not begin at birth, and you will not end at death. There is a plan, and you were part of it before you ever arrived here.
Today, think about how differently life feels when you remember it has an eternal shape.
Before we begin, ask God to help you see your life as part of something larger.

pages.q: We will make an earth whereon these may dwell.

pages.prompt: How does knowing your life has eternal purpose change how you see today?

o.l: It helps me care less about things that don't actually matter
o.r: Let this eternal view shrink, just a little, the things today that don't actually matter in the long run.

o.l: It gives me hope for people and situations that feel unresolved
o.r: Hold onto hope today for someone or something that still feels unresolved. The story isn't finished yet.

o.l: It reminds me my choices here carry real, lasting weight
o.r: Remember today that your choices carry weight beyond this moment. Let that shape one decision you make.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However the Plan of Salvation speaks to you today, let it widen your view beyond just this one day.

p: This life is not the whole story. It is one meaningful chapter in something far bigger than any single day can hold.

In a vision, Abraham heard the Lord say of His children, “we will prove them herewith, to see if they will do all things whatsoever the Lord their God shall command them.” This life is a time of learning and choosing.
Knowing that does not make today less important. It makes it matter more.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Abraham 3:22-26
Write one sentence about how today looks different when you remember your life is eternal.

pages.q: This life is one meaningful chapter in something far bigger than any single day can hold.

24.pq: I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their God, and they shall be my people.

p: A covenant is not just a promise. It is a two-way relationship. God offers something sacred, and you commit something real in return.
Today, think about a covenant you've already made, and whether you've been living up to your part of it.
Before we begin, ask God to help you understand what your covenants truly mean.

pages.q: I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their God, and they shall be my people.

pages.prompt: What is one covenant in your life you could recommit to more fully today?

o.l: I can live my baptismal covenant more intentionally
o.r: Choose one specific way today to live your baptismal covenant more intentionally, not just habitually.

o.l: I can honor a covenant I made that I've let slip
o.r: There's a covenant you've let slip. Take one honest step back toward it today.

o.l: I can prepare more seriously for a covenant still ahead of me
o.r: If a covenant is still ahead of you, take today seriously as part of your preparation for it.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However covenants show up in your life today, remember God always keeps His side completely.

p: Covenants are not chains. They are anchors, steady places to return to when life feels uncertain.
The Lord said, “I, the Lord, am bound when ye do what I say.” A covenant works both ways.
God always keeps His side. The invitation is simply to keep yours.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 82:10
Name one covenant you have made and write one way to keep it this week.

pages.q: Covenants are anchors, not chains.

25.pq: Men are free according to the flesh... to choose liberty and eternal life... or to choose captivity and death.

p: God could have made you incapable of choosing wrong. Instead, He gave you the dignity of a real choice.
Today, think about one choice in front of you, and remember it is genuinely yours to make.
Before we begin, ask God for wisdom to choose well.

pages.q: Men are free according to the flesh... to choose liberty and eternal life... or to choose captivity and death.

pages.prompt: What is one choice today where you could deliberately choose what leads you closer to God?

o.l: I can choose a habit that strengthens instead of weakens me
o.r: Notice one habit today, and deliberately choose the version that strengthens you instead of weakens you.

o.l: I can choose to respond with patience instead of frustration
o.r: The next frustrating moment today, choose patience instead of the automatic reaction.

o.l: I can choose to act instead of just intending to
o.r: Stop just intending, and actually act today on the thing you've been meaning to do.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However you exercise agency today, remember every choice is genuinely, meaningfully yours.

p: Your agency is sacred. It is proof that God trusts you enough to let your choices be truly your own.
Lehi taught that “men are, that they might have joy.” And that men “are free to choose liberty and eternal life, through the great Mediator of all men.”
Every day is another chance to choose well, not perfectly, just honestly.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 2 Nephi 2:25-27
Make one choice today because of who you want to become, not because of how you feel.

pages.q: Your agency is proof that God trusts you enough to let your choices be truly your own.

26.pq: A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you.

p: Christ never waited for people to become worthy of His attention. He simply loved them, exactly where they were.
Today, think about someone you've been withholding kindness from, waiting for them to earn it first.
Before we begin, ask God to help you love the way He does, first, and without condition.

pages.q: A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you.

pages.prompt: Who could you show unconditional love to today, without waiting for them to deserve it?

o.l: I can be kind to someone who hasn't been kind to me
o.r: Choose kindness today toward someone who hasn't shown you the same, without waiting for them to go first.

o.l: I can love someone even while we still disagree
o.r: You don't need agreement to offer love. Choose it today, even in the middle of a real disagreement.

o.l: I can love someone by simply not judging them today
o.r: Withhold judgment today toward someone, and let that restraint itself become an act of love.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However Christlike love shows up today, let it be first, not a response earned by someone else.

p: Christlike love does not ask what someone has done to deserve it. It simply gives, the way it was given to you first.
On the night before His Crucifixion, Jesus Christ told His disciples, “By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.” Love is the sign of a disciple.
That is the whole pattern. He loved first, so that you could learn to do the same.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 1 John 4:19
Show kindness today to someone who has not earned it.

pages.q: Christlike love does not ask what someone has done to deserve it.

27.pq: Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.

p: The scriptures were not written to be read once and set aside. They were written to be returned to, again and again, at every season of your life.
Today, think about whether your scripture study feels alive, or like a checklist.
Before we begin, ask God to help His word feel new to you today.

pages.q: Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.

pages.prompt: What could make your scripture study feel more meaningful this week?

o.l: I can read slower, and actually sit with what I read
o.r: Slow down today's scripture study, and actually sit with a single verse instead of rushing through many.

o.l: I can ask a real question before I open the scriptures
o.r: Before you open the scriptures today, bring a real, honest question you actually want answered.

o.l: I can write down what stands out, instead of just reading past it
o.r: When something stands out today, write it down instead of letting it pass by unnoticed.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However you approach scripture today, come expecting to actually hear something meant for you.

p: The scriptures do not change. But you do, and that is exactly why the same verse can speak differently to you at different times in your life.
Nephi taught, “feast upon the words of Christ; for behold, the words of Christ will tell you all things what ye should do.”
Come to them expecting to actually hear something.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 2 Nephi 32:3
Read for ten minutes and stop on one verse. Write what it asks of you.

pages.q: The scriptures do not change. But you do.

28.pq: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you.

p: The peace Christ offers is not the absence of hard things. It is calm confidence in the middle of them.
Today, think about what has been stealing your peace lately, and bring it honestly to God.
Before we begin, ask Him for peace that doesn't depend on your circumstances changing.

pages.q: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you.

pages.prompt: Where in your life do you most need Christ's peace right now?

o.l: I can ask for peace about something I can't control
o.r: Bring to God today the thing you cannot control, and ask specifically for peace about it, not a solution.

o.l: I can ask for peace in a relationship that feels unsettled
o.r: Ask God today for peace in that unsettled relationship, even before it's fully resolved.

o.l: I can ask for peace about my own future
o.r: Bring your uncertainty about the future to God today, and ask for peace in the not-yet-knowing.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However you seek peace today, remember it doesn't require your circumstances to change first.

p: The world's peace depends on everything going right. Christ's peace remains even when nothing does.

Paul wrote that “the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.” The way to it: “in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.”
That is the peace worth asking for, not the absence of storms, but stillness in the middle of them.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Philippians 4:6-7
Name what has taken your peace, pray about it, then do one small thing to calm your day.

pages.q: Christ's peace remains even when the storm does not.

29.pq: If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.

p: Following Christ is not a single decision made once. It is a direction chosen again, every single day.
Today, think about what following Him would look like specifically today, not in general.
Before we begin, ask God what discipleship looks like for you right now.

pages.q: If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.

pages.prompt: What would it look like to follow Christ more intentionally today?

o.l: I can make a choice today that reflects what I believe
o.r: Choose one decision today that genuinely reflects what you say you believe.

o.l: I can let go of something that's been pulling me away from Him
o.r: Identify the thing that's been quietly pulling you away, and let go of it today.

o.l: I can simply try to see today the way He would
o.r: Try today, even briefly, to see your circumstances the way Christ might see them.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However discipleship shows up today, let it be one deliberate step in His direction.

p: Discipleship is not measured by how far you've come. It is measured by which direction you're facing right now.
In Luke's account, Jesus Christ adds one word: “daily.” Following Him is a choice you make again each day.
Every day offers a fresh chance to take one more step toward Him.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Luke 9:23-24
Ask God, “What is one way I can follow Jesus Christ today?” Then do it.

pages.q: Discipleship is measured by which direction you're facing right now.

30.pq: For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory.

p: Some days feel enormous. In light of eternity, most of what worries you today will not matter in ten years.
Today, think about what you're carrying that might feel lighter with a longer view.
Before we begin, ask God to help you see your life the way He sees it.

pages.q: For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory.

pages.prompt: What is something weighing on you today that might feel different with an eternal perspective?

o.l: I can let go of worrying about something temporary
o.r: Notice something you've been worrying over that is genuinely temporary, and set that worry down today.

o.l: I can trust that a current struggle is not the end of the story
o.r: Whatever struggle you're in, trust today that it is not the final word on your story.

o.l: I can focus more on what will actually matter in eternity
o.r: Shift your focus today toward what will actually matter a hundred years from now.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However eternal perspective shapes your day, let it lighten something that's been feeling too heavy.

p: This moment is real, and so is its weight. But it is not the whole picture, and it is not the end of your story.
In Liberty Jail the Lord told Joseph Smith, “thine adversity and thine afflictions shall be but a small moment.” Then He added, “if thou endure it well, God shall exalt thee on high.”
Eternity is patient with you. So try, today, to be a little more patient with yourself.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 121:7-8
Write down one worry, then write how it may look in ten years.

pages.q: Eternity is patient with you. So try to be a little more patient with yourself.

31.pq: Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.

p: Baptism is not the finish line. It is the doorway. The first covenant on a lifelong path.
Today, think about your own baptism, or a baptism you've witnessed, and what it meant in that moment.
Before we begin, thank God for the gift of a fresh start.

pages.q: Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.

pages.prompt: What does a fresh start mean to you right now?

o.l: I can let go of something old to make room for something new
o.r: Let go today of something old that's been taking up space, and make room for what's new.

o.l: I can renew a commitment I made at my own baptism
o.r: Renew today, intentionally, a specific commitment you made at your own baptism.

o.l: I can help someone else prepare for this step
o.r: Think of someone preparing for baptism, and offer them real support today.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However renewal shows up today, let it be a genuine fresh start, not just a passing thought.

p: Baptism does not erase your history. It marks the beginning of a new one. Written together with Christ.
In Mosiah 18:8-10 we read: “As ye are desirous to come into the fold of God, and to be called his people, and are willing to bear one another's burdens, that they may be light.”
Every day since has been a chance to keep choosing that same fresh start.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Mosiah 18:8-10
Remember your baptism. Write one promise you made and one way to keep it.

pages.q: Baptism marks the beginning of a new story, written together with Christ.

32.pq: This do in remembrance of me.

p: Every week offers a reset. A quiet moment to remember, to repent, and to begin again.
Today, think about how present you actually are during the sacrament, versus how present you'd like to be.
Before we begin, ask God to help this week's sacrament feel less routine and more real.

pages.q: This do in remembrance of me.

pages.prompt: What is one thing you could remember more intentionally during the sacrament this week?

o.l: I can remember a specific way Christ has helped me
o.r: Bring that specific memory to mind during this week's sacrament, and let it deepen your gratitude.

o.l: I can use the moment to genuinely repent, not just reflect
o.r: Use this week's sacrament to genuinely repent of something specific, not just to reflect in general.

o.l: I can renew my baptismal covenant with real intention
o.r: Renew your baptismal covenant this week with real, deliberate intention, not out of habit.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However you approach the sacrament this week, let it be a real moment of remembering, not routine.

p: The sacrament is not a formality to sit through. It is a weekly invitation to remember who you've promised to become.
In 3 Nephi 18:7-11 we read: “And this shall ye do in remembrance of my body, which I have shown unto you.”
That promise is renewed every time you choose to mean it.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 3 Nephi 18:7-11
This Sunday, use the sacrament to think of one way to remember Him better.

pages.q: The sacrament is a weekly invitation to remember who you've promised to become.

33.pq: The powers of heaven cannot be controlled nor handled only upon the principles of righteousness.

p: The priesthood is not about position. It is God's power, made available to bless others.
Today, think about a blessing, a priesthood blessing, or simply an act of service, that has shaped your life.
Before we begin, thank God for the ways His power has reached you through others.

pages.q: The powers of heaven cannot be controlled nor handled only upon the principles of righteousness.

pages.prompt: How has priesthood power blessed your life, directly or through someone else?

o.l: I can remember a specific blessing that helped me through something hard
o.r: Take a moment to remember that specific blessing, and let gratitude for it deepen your faith.

o.l: I can ask for a blessing I've been needing but haven't yet requested
o.r: If you've been needing a blessing, take the step today to actually ask for it.

o.l: I can better appreciate those who serve quietly in this way
o.r: Notice today someone who serves quietly through the priesthood, and thank them.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However priesthood power touches your life today, let it deepen your gratitude for those who serve.

p: This power was never meant to be used for control. It works only through righteousness, love, and genuine service.

In Doctrine and Covenants 121:41-42 we read: “No power or influence can or ought to be maintained by virtue of the priesthood, only by persuasion, by long-suffering, by gentleness and meekness, and by love unfeigned.”
That is what makes it recognizable, not the words spoken, but the love behind them.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 121:41-42
Notice how you influence others today. Choose patience and gentleness over pressure.

pages.q: This power works only through righteousness, love, and genuine service.

34.pq: He that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.

p: Enduring to the end is not about gritting your teeth. It is about staying faithful, one ordinary day at a time.
Today, think about a commitment you made that has gotten harder to keep, and choose to keep it anyway.
Before we begin, ask God for strength to endure, not just to start.

pages.q: He that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.

pages.prompt: What is something you've started but need renewed strength to continue?

o.l: I can recommit to a habit I've let slip
o.r: Recommit today to the habit you've let slip, even if it's just one small step back toward it.

o.l: I can keep showing up, even without feeling motivated
o.r: Show up today even without feeling motivated. Motivation often follows action, not the other way around.

o.l: I can trust that consistency matters more than perfection
o.r: Trust today that consistency, even imperfect, matters more than any single perfect effort.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However endurance is tested today, remember faithfulness is built in ordinary, repeated choices.

p: Most of life is not decided in dramatic moments. It is decided in the quiet choice to keep going, especially when no one is watching.
In James 5:11 we read: “Behold, we count them happy which endure. Ye have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of the Lord.”
That is what endurance actually looks like. Ordinary faithfulness, repeated.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in James 5:11
Think of one thing you want to quit. Take one more small step today.

pages.q: Most of life is decided in the quiet choice to keep going.

35.pq: Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth.

p: Meekness is not weakness. It is strength that has learned to be gentle.
Today, think of a moment where restraint would serve you better than reaction.
Before we begin, ask God to help you respond instead of react today.

pages.q: Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth.

pages.prompt: Where could a gentler response change something today?

o.l: I can respond calmly to something that would normally frustrate me
o.r: The next time frustration rises today, choose a calm response instead of a sharp one.

o.l: I can let go of needing to prove a point
o.r: Let go today of needing to prove you're right, even when you feel certain.

o.l: I can be strong without being harsh
o.r: Practice today being strong without being harsh. The two are not the same thing.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However meekness shows up today, remember it is strength that has learned restraint.

p: Meekness does not mean having no strength. It means having strength you choose not to misuse.
In Alma 13:28 we read: “But that ye would humble yourselves before the Lord, and call on his holy name, and watch and pray continually, that ye may not be tempted above that which ye can bear.”
Christ was the meekest of all, and also the strongest. Those two things were never in conflict.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Alma 13:28
Listen to someone today without correcting them. Say less than you planned.

pages.q: Meekness is strength that has learned to be gentle.

36.pq: Behold, the Lord requireth the heart and a willing mind…

p: Consecration means giving God not just your time, but your whole self. Talents, resources, everything.
Today, think about one part of your life you've been holding back from Him.
Before we begin, ask God what it would mean to give Him that part too.

pages.q: Behold, the Lord requireth the heart and a willing mind; and the willing and obedient shall eat the good of the land of Zion in these last days.

pages.prompt: What is one part of your life you could more fully dedicate to God?

o.l: I can offer my time more generously in His service
o.r: Offer your time today more generously than convenience would suggest.

o.l: I can use a specific talent for something meaningful
o.r: Use a specific talent today for something that genuinely matters, not just for yourself.

o.l: I can hold my resources more loosely, trusting Him with them
o.r: Hold your resources a little more loosely today, trusting God with what you're tempted to grip tightly.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However consecration shows up today, let it be a real, if small, loosening of your grip.

p: Consecration is not about giving everything away all at once. It is about slowly loosening your grip on what you've been holding too tightly.

In Doctrine and Covenants 42:30 we read: “And behold, thou wilt remember the poor, and consecrate of thy properties for their support that which thou hast to impart unto them, with a covenant and a deed which cannot be broken.”
Little by little, it becomes less about what you're giving up, and more about what you're becoming.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 42:30
Offer God one thing today: an hour, a talent, or a skill. Use it to bless someone.

pages.q: Consecration is slowly loosening your grip on what you've been holding too tightly.

37.pq: He that is slothful... shall not be counted worthy to stand.

p: Diligence is not about doing everything. It is about doing the right things, steadily, without giving up.
Today, think about a spiritual habit you've meant to build but haven't quite settled into yet.
Before we begin, ask God for the consistency you've been missing.

pages.q: He that is slothful... shall not be counted worthy to stand.

pages.prompt: What is one habit you could commit to more diligently this week?

o.l: I can pray at a consistent time each day
o.r: Choose a consistent time today to pray, and return to that same time again tomorrow.

o.l: I can read scripture even in small amounts, regularly
o.r: Read even a small amount of scripture today. Consistency matters more than quantity.

o.l: I can follow through on something I've kept postponing
o.r: Follow through today on the one thing you've kept postponing.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However diligence shows up today, remember it is steady effort, not dramatic bursts.

p: Diligence is rarely dramatic. It looks like small, steady effort, repeated long after the excitement of starting has faded.
In Doctrine and Covenants 58:26-28 we read: “For behold, it is not meet that I should command in all things.”
That quiet consistency is exactly what builds a life of real faith.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 58:26-28
Pick one good cause and give it thirty focused minutes today.

pages.q: Diligence looks like small, steady effort, repeated long after motivation fades.

38.pq: Let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit.

p: God gave you appetites and passions, not to control you, but for you to learn to govern.
Today, think of one area where discipline would serve you better than indulgence.
Before we begin, ask God for strength over whatever tends to master you instead.

pages.q: Let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit.

pages.prompt: What is one area where a little more self-discipline could bless your life?

o.l: I can set a boundary around something that controls me more than I'd like
o.r: Set a real boundary today around whatever has had too much control over you.

o.l: I can choose a healthier response to stress or frustration
o.r: Choose a healthier response today the next time stress or frustration rises.

o.l: I can practice restraint in a specific daily habit
o.r: Practice restraint today in one specific, ordinary daily habit.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However self-mastery is tested today, remember the goal is freedom, not restriction for its own sake.

p: Self-mastery is not about denying yourself joy. It is about making sure you are the one in charge, not your impulses.
In 1 Corinthians 9:25-27 we read: “And every man that striveth for the mastery is temperate in all things.”
That kind of freedom is worth the discipline it takes to get there.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 1 Corinthians 9:25-27
Choose one small habit to master today. Notice how it feels tonight.

pages.q: Self-mastery is making sure you are the one in charge, not your impulses.

39.pq: And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her.

p: Compassion notices pain before it's spoken. It moves toward hurting people instead of away from them.
Today, think of someone whose struggle you've noticed but haven't yet responded to.
Before we begin, ask God to help you see people the way He does.

pages.q: And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her.

pages.prompt: Who could use your compassion today, even in a small way?

o.l: I can check in on someone I know is struggling
o.r: Reach out today to someone you know is quietly struggling.

o.l: I can respond gently to someone who is having a hard day
o.r: Respond gently today to someone who is clearly having a hard day.

o.l: I can simply notice someone others might overlook
o.r: Notice today someone others tend to overlook, and see them.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However compassion shows up today, let it move you to actually respond, not just notice.

p: Christ never walked past suffering without responding to it. He saw people, and that seeing moved Him to act.
In Matthew 14:14 we read: “And Jesus went forth, and saw a great multitude, and was moved with compassion toward them, and he healed their sick.”
Compassion starts exactly there, with actually noticing.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Matthew 14:14
Ask someone how they are really doing, then listen. Do not rush to fix it.

pages.q: Compassion moves toward hurting people instead of away from them.

40.pq: I am the resurrection, and the life.

p: Death does not have the final word. Christ made certain of that.
Today, think about someone you've lost, and let yourself feel the hope the Resurrection offers.
Before we begin, thank God for the promise that separation is not forever.

pages.q: I am the resurrection, and the life.

pages.prompt: How does the promise of resurrection change the way you think about loss?

o.l: It gives me hope for someone I miss
o.r: Let this promise bring real hope today for someone you miss.

o.l: It helps me see death as temporary, not final
o.r: Let this truth today soften how heavily death weighs on your mind.

o.l: It changes how I think about my own mortality
o.r: Consider today how differently you see your own mortality in light of the Resurrection.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However the Resurrection speaks to you today, let it be a genuine source of hope, not just doctrine.

p: Every grave is temporary. Every goodbye is not truly the end.
In Alma 11:43-44 we read: “The spirit and the body shall be reunited again in its perfect form.”
Christ's empty tomb is the guarantee, not just that He lives, but that everyone you love who has passed will live again too.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Alma 11:43-44
Write the name of someone you miss. Thank God for the promise of the Resurrection.

pages.q: Christ's empty tomb is the guarantee that every goodbye is not truly the end.

41.pq: Neither is the man without the woman, neither the woman without the man, in the Lord.

p: Marriage sealed by God's authority is not just for this life. It is meant to last beyond it.
Today, think about what it means for a relationship to be built for eternity, not just for now.
Before we begin, ask God to help you love the way an eternal relationship deserves.

pages.q: Neither is the man without the woman, neither the woman without the man, in the Lord.

pages.prompt: What is one way you could strengthen an eternal relationship today?

o.l: I can be more patient with my spouse or future spouse
o.r: Practice patience today with your spouse or future spouse, even in something small.

o.l: I can express appreciation instead of assuming it's understood
o.r: Say the appreciation out loud today instead of assuming it's understood.

o.l: I can invest more intentionally in a relationship I want to last
o.r: Invest today, intentionally, in the relationship you want to last for eternity.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However eternal marriage shows up in your life today, remember it is built in daily, small choices.

p: An eternal marriage is not perfect from the start. It becomes eternal through the small, daily choices two people make to stay bound together.
In Doctrine and Covenants 131:1-4 we read: “In the celestial glory there are three heavens or degrees.”
That is what covenant love actually looks like, practiced one day at a time.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 131:1-4
Tell someone you love one thing you appreciate about them. Say it today.

pages.q: An eternal marriage becomes eternal through the small, daily choices two people make to stay bound together.

42.pq: Is not this the fast that I have chosen? to loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens…

p: Fasting is not about hunger. It is about making room, emptying something out so God can fill it instead.
Today, think about what fasting could add to your prayers this month.
Before we begin, ask God to help your next fast be more about seeking Him than simply following a routine.

pages.q: Is not this the fast that I have chosen? to loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, and to let the oppressed go free, and that ye break every yoke?

pages.prompt: What could you fast for with real purpose this month?

o.l: I can fast for someone else's need, not just my own
o.r: Let your next fast be for someone else's need, not only your own.

o.l: I can pair my fast with real service to someone in need
o.r: Pair your next fast with a real act of service to someone in need.

o.l: I can use the time for focused, uninterrupted prayer
o.r: Use fasting time today for focused, uninterrupted prayer, not just hunger.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However you approach fasting, let the hunger point you toward real seeking, not just ritual.

p: A fast without purpose is just an empty stomach. A fast with purpose becomes a genuine act of faith.
In Alma 5:46 we read: “Behold, I say unto you they are made known unto me by the Holy Spirit of God.”
The hunger is not the point. The seeking is.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Alma 5:46
Plan a fast with a clear purpose. Write the purpose down before you begin.

pages.q: A fast with purpose becomes a genuine act of faith.

43.pq: By the power of the Holy Ghost ye may know the truth of all things.

p: A testimony is not something you inherit. It is something you build, through personal experience with God.
Today, think about one experience that has personally confirmed something to you.
Before we begin, thank God for the moments He's already shown Himself real to you.

pages.q: By the power of the Holy Ghost ye may know the truth of all things.

pages.prompt: What is one truth you know because you personally experienced it, not just because you were taught it?

o.l: I can recognize a specific answer to prayer I've received
o.r: Recall today a specific answered prayer, and let it strengthen your testimony.

o.l: I can identify a moment I felt the Spirit clearly
o.r: Identify today a moment you clearly felt the Spirit, and hold onto that memory.

o.l: I can share this experience with someone who needs to hear it
o.r: Share today, with someone who needs it, an experience that built your own testimony.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However testimony shows up in your life today, remember it is built through personal experience with God.

p: A borrowed testimony can carry you for a while. A personal one can carry you through anything.
In Alma 32:26-27 we read: “Even if ye can no more than desire to believe, let this desire work in you.”
Every honest question you bring to God is another chance to make it truly your own.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Alma 32:26-27
Write your testimony in three sentences. Share it with one person this week.

pages.q: A personal testimony can carry you through anything a borrowed one cannot.

44.pq: When thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.

p: Conversion is not a single moment. It is a lifelong turning, again and again, toward Christ.
Today, think about how differently you see something now compared to a few years ago.
Before we begin, ask God to help you keep turning toward Him, not just once, but continually.

pages.q: When thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.

pages.prompt: Where do you sense God is still working to convert your heart?

o.l: I can let go of a belief that no longer serves my faith
o.r: Let go today of a belief that no longer reflects who you're becoming.

o.l: I can deepen a truth I already accept but haven't fully lived
o.r: Deepen today a truth you already accept, but haven't fully lived yet.

o.l: I can turn toward Him in an area I've been resistant in
o.r: Turn today toward the area where you've felt most resistant to God's direction.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However conversion shows up today, remember it is a lifelong turning, not a single moment.

p: Conversion never really finishes. It simply deepens, over years, as you keep choosing to let God change you.
In Alma 23:6 we read: “And as sure as the Lord liveth, so sure as many as believed, or as many as were brought to the knowledge of the truth, through the preaching of Ammon and his brethren.”
Every stage of that turning is real progress, even when it's slow.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Alma 23:6
Write one way you have changed because of Jesus Christ.

pages.q: Conversion never really finishes. It simply deepens, year after year.

45.pq: And shall run and not be weary, and shall walk and not faint.

p: Caring for your body is not just a physical matter. It is a spiritual one too.
Today, think about one way you could care better for the body God gave you.
Before we begin, thank God for the wisdom of this simple, practical law.

pages.q: And shall run and not be weary, and shall walk and not faint.

pages.prompt: What is one small, practical way you could honor your body today?

o.l: I can make a healthier choice in what I eat or drink
o.r: Make one healthier choice today in what you eat or drink.

o.l: I can prioritize rest instead of pushing through exhaustion
