o.r: Prioritize rest today instead of pushing through exhaustion.

o.l: I can treat my body as something sacred, not just useful
o.r: Treat your body today as something sacred, not merely useful.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However you honor your body today, remember this law was given as wisdom, not restriction.

p: This law was given with a promise attached, not to restrict you, but to strengthen you.

In Doctrine and Covenants 89:18-21 we read: “And all saints who remember to keep and do these sayings, walking in obedience to the commandments, shall receive health in their navel and marrow to their bones.”
Small, faithful choices about your body add up to real, lasting blessings.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 89:18-21
Choose one healthy habit today and thank God for the body He gave you.

pages.q: The Word of Wisdom is about honoring the body God gave you.

46.pq: Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse... and prove me now herewith.

p: Tithing is not really about money. It is about trust, whether you believe God will provide for the ninety percent.
Today, think about your own relationship with tithing, honestly.
Before we begin, ask God to help you trust Him more fully with what you have.

pages.q: Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse... and prove me now herewith.

pages.prompt: What would it look like to trust God more fully with your finances?

o.l: I can pay tithing consistently, even when it feels tight
o.r: Pay a full tithe today, even if it feels tight, and trust the promise attached to it.

o.l: I can give more generously beyond what's required
o.r: Give more generously today than what's strictly required.

o.l: I can stop worrying about the ninety percent and trust the pattern
o.r: Stop worrying today about the ninety percent, and trust the pattern God has promised.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However tithing shows up in your life today, remember it is a practice of trust, not just finance.

p: God does not need your money. He is offering you a chance to practice trust, in a way you can measure and see.
In 3 Nephi 24:10 we read: “Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in my house.”
Few commandments come with such a direct invitation to test them for yourself.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 3 Nephi 24:10
Write one blessing you have received. Thank God for His care.

pages.q: Tithing is one of the clearest ways to demonstrate whether you trust God as your provider.

47.pq: He shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers.

p: Somewhere in your family line is a name waiting to be remembered, and an ordinance waiting to be done.
Today, think about your ancestors. The people whose choices led, generation by generation, to you.
Before we begin, ask God to help you feel connected to those who came before you.

pages.q: He shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers.

pages.prompt: What is one small step you could take toward your family history this month?

o.l: I can look up one ancestor's name and story
o.r: Look up one ancestor's name and story today, even briefly.

o.l: I can ask an older relative about family history while I still can
o.r: Ask an older relative today about family history, while you still can.

o.l: I can help complete temple work for a name I already have
o.r: Take a step today toward completing temple work for a name you already have.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However family history work shows up today, remember it is reunion, not just record-keeping.

p: This work is not just genealogy. It is reunion, connecting generations who are still, in some real way, waiting for each other.
In Doctrine and Covenants 128:18 we read: “I might have rendered a plainer translation to this, but it is sufficiently plain to suit my purpose as it stands.”
Every name you find is a person who mattered, and still does.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 128:18
Write down one story about an ancestor, or ask a relative to tell you one.

pages.q: Family history work connects the living and the dead through sacred ordinances.

48.pq: Know ye not that ye are the temple of God?

p: Chastity is not a rule about restriction. It is about honoring the sacred power to create life.
Today, think about how you view your own body and relationships, with reverence, or with carelessness.
Before we begin, ask God to help you see intimacy the way He does. Sacred, not casual.

pages.q: Know ye not that ye are the temple of God?

pages.prompt: What is one way you could honor the law of chastity more fully in your life right now?

o.l: I can set clearer boundaries in a current relationship
o.r: Set a clearer boundary today in a current relationship.

o.l: I can be more careful about the media I consume
o.r: Be more careful today about the media you allow into your life.

o.l: I can treat this part of my life with more reverence
o.r: Treat this part of your life today with more reverence than casualness.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However chastity shows up in your choices today, remember it protects something sacred.

p: This standard is not about shame. It is about protecting something sacred. A power meant only to be used within the bounds God has set.
In Alma 39:5 we read: “Know ye not, my son, that these things are an abomination in the sight of the Lord.”
Living it well is not restriction. It is reverence.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Alma 39:5
Choose one wholesome thing to read, watch, or listen to today.

pages.q: This standard protects something sacred, not something shameful.

49.pq: It is required of the Lord, at the hand of every steward, to render an account of his stewardship.

p: Nothing you have is fully yours. It was entrusted to you, and one day you'll give an account of how you used it.
Today, think about what you've been given, time, talents, resources, and whether you're using them well.
Before we begin, ask God to help you see yourself as a steward, not just an owner.

pages.q: It is required of the Lord, at the hand of every steward, to render an account of his stewardship.

pages.prompt: What is one thing entrusted to you that you could steward more faithfully?

o.l: I can use my time more intentionally
o.r: Use your time today more intentionally than you have been.

o.l: I can use a talent I've been neglecting
o.r: Use a talent today you've been neglecting, even briefly.

o.l: I can be more careful with resources I've been given
o.r: Be more careful today with a resource entrusted to you.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However stewardship shows up today, remember everything you have is on loan, for a purpose.

p: A good steward does not hoard, and does not waste. They use what they've been given for a purpose beyond themselves.

In Doctrine and Covenants 104:13 we read: “For it is expedient that I, the Lord, should make every man accountable, as a steward over earthly blessings, which I have made and prepared for my creatures.”
Everything you have is on loan, for a season, for a reason.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 104:13
List what God has put in your care. Pick one to care for better this week.

pages.q: A good steward does not hoard, and does not waste.

50.pq: And the Lord called his people Zion, because they were of one heart and one mind.

p: Zion is not just a place. It is a people. Unified, pure in heart, caring for one another.
Today, think about what it would mean for your own community to be a little more like Zion.
Before we begin, ask God how you could help build it, starting today.

pages.q: And the Lord called his people Zion, because they were of one heart and one mind.

pages.prompt: What is one way you could help build Zion in your own community?

o.l: I can be more unified with someone I've had friction with
o.r: Take a step today toward unity with someone you've had friction with.

o.l: I can care for someone in need without being asked
o.r: Care today for someone in need, without waiting to be asked.

o.l: I can help create a sense of belonging for someone new
o.r: Help someone today feel a genuine sense of belonging.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However Zion shows up in your community today, remember it begins in small, unglamorous acts.

p: Zion begins in small, unglamorous acts of unity and care, not in grand gestures, but in ordinary people choosing to be one.
In Articles of Faith 1:4 we read: “We believe that the first principles and ordinances of the Gospel are.”
You do not need to wait for a perfect community. You can help build it, one relationship at a time.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Articles of Faith 1:4
Do one small thing today to make your home, ward or branch more peaceful.

pages.q: Zion begins in ordinary people choosing to be one.

51.pq: And it shall come to pass that he that feareth me shall be looking forth for the great day of the Lord to come…

p: Christ's return is not meant to bring fear. It is meant to bring hope. The promise that all will finally be made right.
Today, think about how differently you'd live if you were fully certain He was coming soon.
Before we begin, ask God to help you live today the way you would if He returned tomorrow.

pages.q: And it shall come to pass that he that feareth me shall be looking forth for the great day of the Lord to come, even for the signs of the coming of the Son of Man.

pages.prompt: How would today look different if you truly lived it in preparation for His return?

o.l: I would forgive something I've been holding onto
o.r: Forgive today something you've been holding onto, as if His return were imminent.

o.l: I would treat someone with more patience and love
o.r: Treat someone today with the patience and love you'd want to be found living.

o.l: I would spend less time on what doesn't ultimately matter
o.r: Spend less time today on what won't ultimately matter.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However you prepare for His return today, remember readiness is built in ordinary, faithful days.

p: No one knows the exact day. But everyone can be ready, not through fear, but through a life quietly and consistently aligned with Christ.
In Matthew 24:36 we read: “But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only.”
Readiness is not built in a single moment. It is built, day by day, in exactly the kind of life you are already living.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Matthew 24:36
Ask yourself what you would want to finish if He came soon. Do one thing from that list.

pages.q: Readiness for His return is built day by day, in the life you are already living.

52.pq: And because he hath done this, my beloved brethren, have miracles ceased? Behold I say unto you, Nay…

p: Heaven is closer than it seems. God sends help. Sometimes through angels, sometimes through the people right in front of you.
Today, think about a time someone showed up for you exactly when you needed it.
Before we begin, ask God to help you be that kind of help for someone else today.

pages.q: And because he hath done this, my beloved brethren, have miracles ceased? Behold I say unto you, Nay; neither have angels ceased to minister unto the children of men.

pages.prompt: Who could you minister to today, the way someone once ministered to you?

o.l: I can check on someone quietly struggling
o.r: Check on someone today who is quietly struggling, before they have to ask.

o.l: I can offer help before being asked
o.r: Offer help today before being asked, the way an angel might.

o.l: I can simply be present for someone who needs it
o.r: Simply be present today for someone who needs it, without needing to fix anything.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However ministering shows up in your life today, remember it is what any person does when they notice a need.

p: Ministering is not a formal calling reserved for a few. It is what any person does when they notice someone else's need and respond.
In Hebrews 1:14 we read: “Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?”
Sometimes, you are the angel someone else has been praying for.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Hebrews 1:14
Think of someone who helped you at the right time. Thank them, then do the same for another.

pages.q: Sometimes, you are the angel someone else has been praying for.

53.pq: For all have not every gift given unto them... that all may be profited thereby.

p: God gave you at least one spiritual gift, something specific and personal, meant to bless others, not just yourself.
Today, think about what comes naturally to you that might actually be a gift from God.
Before we begin, ask Him to help you recognize and use it.

pages.q: For all have not every gift given unto them... that all may be profited thereby.

pages.prompt: What is a gift you have that could bless someone else today?

o.l: I can use a gift of listening or comforting
o.r: Use your gift of listening or comforting today for someone who needs it.

Using it is not showing off. It is simply doing what you were equipped to do.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:

pages.q: Your gift was given so that someone else could be blessed by it.

54.pq: Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the Lord thy God is with thee.

p: Courage rarely feels brave in the moment. It usually just feels like doing the hard thing anyway.
Today, think about something you've been avoiding out of fear rather than genuine wisdom.
Before we begin, ask God for courage to take one small step forward.

pages.q: Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the Lord thy God is with thee.

o.r: However courage is tested today, remember it is not the absence of fear, but faith that outweighs it.

p: You are not asked to be fearless. You are asked to move forward anyway, trusting that God goes with you.
In Doctrine and Covenants 68:6 we read: “Wherefore, be of good cheer, and do not fear, for I the Lord am with you, and will stand by you.”
Courage is not the absence of fear. It is faith that outweighs it.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 68:6
Do one thing today that takes courage. Ask God to go with you.

pages.q: Courage is faith that outweighs fear.

55.pq: Men are, that they might have joy.

p: Joy is deeper than happiness. It can exist even in hard seasons, because it is rooted in something eternal.
Today, think about where your joy actually comes from. Circumstances, or something steadier.
Before we begin, ask God to help you find joy even in what's difficult right now.

o.r: However joy shows up today, remember it can exist even in hard seasons, because it is rooted in something eternal.

p: You were not created merely to endure this life. You were created to find real joy in it, even the parts that are hard.
In Mosiah 2:41 we read: “And moreover, I would desire that ye should consider on the blessed and happy state of those that keep the commandments of God.”
That joy is not naive. It is simply rooted somewhere deeper than your circumstances.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Mosiah 2:41
Notice three moments of joy today. Write them down tonight.

pages.q: You were created to find real joy in this life, even the hard parts of it.

56.pq: It is by grace that we are saved, after all we can do.

p: Grace is the gap between what you could ever earn and what Christ freely gives anyway.
Today, think about a place in your life where you've been trying to earn what was always meant to be a gift.
Before we begin, thank God for grace you did nothing to deserve.

pages.q: It is by grace that we are saved, after all we can do.

o.r: Stop punishing yourself today for something you've already repented of.

o.r: Accept help today instead of insisting on doing everything alone.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However grace shows up in your life today, remember it means your effort was never meant to be the whole story.

p: Grace does not mean your effort doesn't matter. It means your effort was never meant to be the whole story.
In Ephesians 2:8-9 we read: “For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves.”
Christ makes up the difference. More than enough, every single time.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:

pages.q: Christ makes up the difference. More than enough, every time.

57.pq: That which is of God is light; and he that receiveth light, and continueth in God, receiveth more light.

p: Before you ever learned about Him, something in you already recognized truth and goodness. That was the Light of Christ.
Today, think about a moment you sensed right from wrong, even before anyone taught you.
Before we begin, ask God to help that light in you grow brighter.

pages.q: That which is of God is light; and he that receiveth light, and continueth in God, receiveth more light.

o.r: Choose truth today over convenience, even in something small.

o.r: Pay attention today to a quiet prompting you've been ignoring.

o.l: I can surround myself with more of what uplifts, less of what doesn't
o.r: Surround yourself today with more of what uplifts, less of what doesn't.

o.r: However the Light of Christ moves in you today, remember it was placed in you before you ever went searching for it.

p: That inner sense of right and wrong was placed in you before you ever went searching for it. It is God's light, already present, waiting to grow.
In Moroni 7:16 we read: “For behold, the Spirit of Christ is given to every man, that he may know good from evil.”
Every good choice adds a little more brightness.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Moroni 7:16
Notice one moment today when you knew what was right. Follow it.

pages.q: Every good choice adds a little more brightness.

58.pq: That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee.

p: Christ prayed that His followers would be one, not identical, but unified in purpose and love.
Today, think about a relationship where division has crept in, even in something small.
Before we begin, ask God to help you be a peacemaker, not a divider, today.

pages.q: That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee.

pages.prompt: Where could you help build unity instead of division today?

o.l: I can let go of being right in favor of being kind
o.r: Let go today of being right, in favor of being kind.

o.l: I can reach out to someone I've drifted from
o.r: Reach out today to someone you've drifted from.

o.l: I can look for common ground instead of difference
o.r: Look today for common ground instead of focusing on difference.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However unity shows up in your relationships today, remember it doesn't require total agreement.

p: Unity does not mean everyone agrees on everything. It means choosing love and purpose even in the middle of real differences.
In 4 Nephi 1:15-17 we read: “And it came to pass that there was no contention in the land, because of the love of God which did dwell in the hearts of the people.”
That is exactly the kind of oneness Christ prayed for.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 4 Nephi 1:15-17
Do one thing today to bring two people closer, or to include someone.

pages.q: Unity means choosing love even in the middle of real differences.

59.pq: I will offer to thee the sacrifice of thanksgiving, and will call upon the name of the LORD.

p: Sacrifice is giving up something good for something greater. It is one of the clearest signs of real faith.
Today, think about something you've given up, or could give up, for the sake of something that matters more.
Before we begin, ask God to help you see sacrifice as an offering, not a loss.

pages.q: I will offer to thee the sacrifice of thanksgiving, and will call upon the name of the LORD.

pages.prompt: What is something you could sacrifice today for the sake of something that matters more?

o.l: I can give up comfort to help someone else
o.r: Give up some comfort today to genuinely help someone else.

o.l: I can give up time I'd rather spend elsewhere
o.r: Give up some time today you'd rather spend elsewhere.

o.l: I can give up pride to make peace with someone
o.r: Give up some pride today to make peace with someone.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However sacrifice shows up in your life today, remember it is never truly a loss.

p: Every sacrifice you make in faith is never truly a loss. It is an exchange, something temporary given up for something eternal gained.
In Doctrine and Covenants 97:8 we read: “All among them who know their hearts are honest, and are broken, and their spirits contrite, and are willing to observe their covenants by sacrifice.”
That is exactly the trade Christ Himself modeled, all the way to the cross.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 97:8
Give up one small comfort today and use the time to serve someone.

pages.q: Every sacrifice made in faith is an exchange, not a loss.

60.pq: For behold, this is my work and my glory.

p: God is not finished speaking. What He reveals today builds on everything He has revealed before.
Today, think about how your understanding of the gospel has grown, even in just the past year.
Before we begin, ask God to keep teaching you. You are not done learning yet.

pages.q: For behold, this is my work and my glory.

o.r: Stay open today to a truth you haven't fully understood yet.

o.r: Trust today that your honest questions will be answered in time.

o.r: Pay closer attention today to what a living prophet is currently teaching.

o.l: I can do something else

p: The canon of scripture may have closed for now, but the flow of revelation never has. God is still speaking. To prophets, and to you.

In Articles of Faith 1:9 we read: “We believe all that God has revealed, all that He does now reveal, and we believe that He will yet reveal many great and important things pertaining to the Kingdom of God.”
The work is not finished. And neither, it turns out, are you.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:

pages.q: God is still speaking. To prophets, and to you.

61.pq: Let your moderation be known unto all men.

p: Gentleness is strength expressed without force. It changes hearts that harshness never could.
Today, think about a moment a gentle word or action changed something for you.
Before we begin, ask God to help your words be gentle today, even when firm.

pages.q: Let your moderation be known unto all men.

pages.prompt: Where could gentleness serve you better than force today?

o.r: Soften today how you correct someone, even when correction is needed.

o.l: I can choose calm words over sharp ones
o.r: Choose calm words today over sharp ones, even under pressure.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However gentleness shows up today, remember it changes hearts that harshness never could.

p: Gentleness rarely makes headlines. But it quietly changes people in ways force never manages to.

It is one of the truest marks of a Christlike heart.

a: Study related verses in 2 Timothy 2:24

pages.q: Gentleness is one of the truest marks of a Christlike heart.

62.pq: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.

p: Wisdom is not just knowing facts. It is knowing how to apply truth in a way that actually helps.

o.r: Seek counsel today instead of deciding entirely alone.

o.r: Slow down today before reacting, and let a moment of pause guide your response.

p: Wisdom begins with humility, recognizing you don't have to figure everything out on your own.

pages.q: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.

63.pq: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much.

p: Faithfulness is not about perfection. It is about showing up, again and again, even imperfectly.

o.r: Be consistent today in a habit, even if it's imperfect.

o.r: Keep a promise today, even when it's inconvenient to do so.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However faithfulness shows up today, remember God notices consistency more than grand gestures.

p: Faithfulness in small things is what qualifies you for greater trust. God notices consistency more than grand gestures.
In Doctrine and Covenants 64:29 we read: “Wherefore, as ye are agents, ye are on the Lord's errand.”
Show up today. That is enough for today.

pages.q: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much.

64.pq: And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good.

p: The world was not an accident. Every detail reflects a Creator who values order, beauty, and purpose.

Before we begin, thank God for the world He made, and for your place in it.

That includes you.

pages.q: And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good.

65.pq: Be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another.

p: Kindness costs little and gives much. It is one of the simplest ways to reflect Christ to someone else.

pages.q: Be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another.

66.pq: Let integrity and uprightness preserve me.

p: Integrity is doing what is right even when no one else would ever know the difference.

pages.q: Let integrity and uprightness preserve me.

67.pq: Beloved, now are we the sons of God.

p: Before anything else defines you, this is true: you are a child of God.

o.r: Remember today the divine potential already placed within you.

pages.q: Beloved, now are we the sons of God.

68.pq: Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.

p: Grief is not a sign of weak faith. Even Christ wept.

o.r: Let yourself grieve today instead of pushing the sorrow aside.

pages.q: Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.

69.pq: Put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.

o.r: Be more reverent today during a moment of worship or prayer.

o.r: Treat a sacred space today with greater care and attention.

pages.q: Put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.

70.pq: Freely ye have received, freely give.

pages.q: Freely ye have received, freely give.

o.r: However steadfastness is tested today, remember being anchored doesn't mean nothing shakes you.

p: The storms of life move quickly, but a steadfast heart does not move with them.
In Helaman 5:12 we read: “And now, my sons, remember, remember that it is upon the rock of our Redeemer, who is Christ, the Son of God, that ye must build your foundation.”
Being anchored does not mean nothing shakes you. It means you do not drift from what actually matters.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Helaman 5:12
Do the same good thing today that you did yesterday. Do not skip it.

pages.q: Be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord.

73.pq: Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.

p: Selflessness notices someone else's need and responds, even when it costs you something.
Today, think about a moment you chose someone else's comfort over your own.
Before we begin, ask God to help you think of others before yourself today.

pages.q: Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.

pages.prompt: Where could you put someone else's need ahead of your own today?

o.l: I can give up something small for someone else's benefit
o.r: Give up something small today for someone else's benefit.

o.l: I can listen instead of talking about myself
o.r: Listen today instead of talking about yourself.

o.l: I can serve without needing recognition
o.r: Serve today without needing any recognition for it.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However selflessness shows up today, remember Christ modeled it perfectly, even in His hardest moments.

p: A selfless life is not a diminished one. It is one that finds meaning in something bigger than its own comfort.
In Philippians 2:3 we read: “Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.”
Christ modeled this perfectly. Always aware of others, even in His own hardest moments.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Philippians 2:3
Put someone else's needs first in one decision today.

pages.q: Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.

74.pq: Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.

p: Trusting God does not mean understanding everything He does. It means believing He is good, even when the path is unclear.
Today, think about a situation where you need to trust God more than you understand Him.
Before we begin, ask God to help your trust grow, even without complete answers.

pages.q: Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.

pages.prompt: Where do you need to trust God more than your own understanding right now?

o.l: I can trust Him with an outcome I can't control
o.r: Trust Him today with an outcome you genuinely cannot control.

o.l: I can trust His timing instead of forcing my own
o.r: Trust His timing today, instead of forcing your own.

o.l: I can trust He sees what I currently cannot
o.r: Trust today that He sees what you currently cannot.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However trust in God is tested today, remember you don't need to understand everything to trust Him.

p: You will not always understand why. But you can always choose to trust Who.

In Doctrine and Covenants 3:4 we read: “For although a man may have many revelations, and have power to do many mighty works, yet if he boasts in his own strength, and sets at naught the counsels of God.”
That distinction, trusting the Person, not just the plan, is where real faith lives.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 3:4
Write one thing you cannot control. Hand it to God in prayer.

pages.q: Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.

75.pq: If ye love me, keep my commandments.

p: Commandments are not obstacles to freedom. They are the boundaries that make real freedom possible.
Today, think about a commandment that has actually protected you from harm.
Before we begin, thank God for the wisdom behind His commandments.

pages.q: If ye love me, keep my commandments.

pages.prompt: What is one commandment you could keep more fully out of love, not obligation?

o.l: I can obey out of love rather than fear of consequence
o.r: Obey today out of love, not merely out of fear of consequence.

o.l: I can trust the wisdom behind a commandment I don't fully understand
o.r: Trust today the wisdom behind a commandment you don't fully understand.

o.l: I can keep a commandment I've been treating loosely
o.r: Keep a commandment today you've been treating loosely.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However God's commandments shape today, remember they are guardrails, not a cage.

p: Commandments were never meant as a cage. They are more like guardrails, protecting you from cliffs you may not even see coming.
In John 14:21 we read: “He that hath my commandments, and keepeth them, he it is that loveth me.”
Loving God naturally leads to trusting His commandments.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in John 14:21
Pick one commandment and write how it blesses or protects you.

pages.q: If ye love me, keep my commandments.

76.pq: Watch ye therefore, and pray always.

p: Watchfulness means staying spiritually alert, not letting small compromises quietly build into big ones.
Today, think about a small habit that has quietly drifted in the wrong direction.
Before we begin, ask God to help you notice what you've been overlooking.

pages.q: Watch ye therefore, and pray always.

pages.prompt: Where could a little more spiritual watchfulness protect you right now?

o.l: I can pay attention to a habit that's slowly drifting
o.r: Pay attention today to a habit that has been slowly drifting.

o.l: I can notice warning signs I've been ignoring
o.r: Notice today a warning sign you've been quietly ignoring.

o.l: I can stay alert instead of becoming spiritually complacent
o.r: Stay spiritually alert today instead of becoming complacent.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However watchfulness matters today, remember most drift happens quietly, one small compromise at a time.

p: Most spiritual drift does not happen suddenly. It happens quietly, one small compromise at a time.
In Doctrine and Covenants 61:38 we read: “Gird up your loins and be watchful and be sober, looking forth for the coming of the Son of Man, for he cometh in an hour you think not.”
Watchfulness simply means paying attention before drift becomes distance.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 61:38
Notice where you are most easily distracted. Make one change to guard against it.

pages.q: Watch ye therefore, and pray always.

77.pq: I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.

p: Contentment is not settling for less. It is finding peace with what you already have while still working toward what's next.
Today, think about a place in your life where comparison has stolen your peace.
Before we begin, ask God to help you feel at peace with where you are right now.

pages.q: I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.

pages.prompt: Where could contentment replace comparison in your life today?

o.l: I can appreciate what I have instead of focusing on what I lack
o.r: Appreciate today what you already have, instead of focusing on what you lack.

o.l: I can stop comparing my progress to someone else's
o.r: Stop comparing today your progress to someone else's.

o.l: I can find peace in an ordinary, unremarkable day
o.r: Find peace today in an ordinary, unremarkable moment.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However contentment shows up today, remember it does not require getting everything you want.

p: Contentment is not the absence of ambition. It is peace that does not depend on getting everything you want, right now.
In 1 Timothy 6:6-8 we read: “But godliness with contentment is great gain.”
That kind of peace can be learned. A little more, each day you practice it.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 1 Timothy 6:6-8
Write five things you have now that you once wished for.

pages.q: I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.

78.pq: Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.

p: God still speaks to the world through a living prophet. Someone called, just as anciently, to guide His people today.
Today, think about the last thing you heard a living prophet teach.
Before we begin, ask God to help you recognize and follow prophetic counsel.

pages.q: Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.

pages.prompt: What is one piece of prophetic counsel you could follow more fully?

o.l: I can revisit a recent message from a living prophet
o.r: Revisit today a recent message from a living prophet.

o.l: I can follow counsel I've been putting off
o.r: Follow today the counsel you've been putting off.

o.l: I can trust prophetic guidance even when I don't fully understand it yet
o.r: Trust prophetic guidance today, even without fully understanding every reason yet.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However the living prophet's voice reaches you today, remember he speaks for this specific moment in history.

p: A living prophet is not a relic of the past. He is God's voice for right now. For your specific moment in history.
In Doctrine and Covenants 1:38 we read: “What I the Lord have spoken, I have spoken, and I excuse not myself.”
Following that voice is one of the surest ways to stay close to God's will for your life.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 1:38
Read or listen to one message from the living prophet today.

pages.q: Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.

79.pq: Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.

p: Sanctification is the slow, patient process of becoming holy, not achieved all at once, but built over a lifetime.
Today, think about how you have grown spiritually, even slightly, this past year.
Before we begin, ask God to keep refining you, patiently and steadily.

pages.q: Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.

pages.prompt: Where do you sense God is currently refining you?

o.l: I can let go of a habit that no longer fits who I'm becoming
o.r: Let go today of a habit that no longer fits who you're becoming.

o.l: I can be patient with my own slow, ongoing growth
o.r: Be patient today with your own slow, ongoing growth.

o.l: I can trust the process, even when it's uncomfortable
o.r: Trust today the refining process, even when it's uncomfortable.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However sanctification shapes today, remember it is built slowly, over a lifetime.

p: You are not meant to be perfect today. You are meant to be a little more sanctified than you were yesterday.
In Moroni 10:32-33 we read: “Yea, come unto Christ, and be perfected in him, and deny yourselves of all ungodliness.”
That slow, steady refining is exactly how holiness is built.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Moroni 10:32-33
Choose one habit to leave behind. Ask the Savior for help to change.

pages.q: Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.

80.pq: Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you.

p: Loving those who have hurt you is one of the hardest, and most Christlike, things you will ever do.
Today, think of someone difficult in your life, and choose to pray for them rather than against them.
Before we begin, ask God to soften your heart toward someone who has wronged you.

pages.q: Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you.

pages.prompt: Who is someone difficult you could choose to love, even in a small way, today?

o.l: I can pray for someone who has hurt me
o.r: Pray today for someone who has hurt you.

o.l: I can respond with kindness instead of retaliation
o.r: Respond today with kindness instead of retaliation.

o.l: I can let go of resentment toward someone specific
o.r: Let go today of resentment toward someone specific.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However loving your enemies is tested today, remember it does not mean excusing what they've done.

p: Loving your enemies does not mean excusing what they've done. It means refusing to let their actions determine the condition of your own heart.
In 3 Nephi 12:44 we read: “But behold I say unto you, love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them who despitefully use you and persecute you.”
That kind of love is hard. It is also exactly the love Christ showed from the cross.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 3 Nephi 12:44
Pray for someone who has hurt you. Ask God to bless them.

pages.q: Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you.

81.pq: And to stand as witnesses of God at all times and in all things, and in all places that ye may be in, even until death…

p: You do not need a pulpit to be a witness of Christ. Your everyday choices are a witness too.
Today, think about what your life quietly says about what you believe.
Before we begin, ask God to help your actions match your testimony today.

pages.q: And to stand as witnesses of God at all times and in all things, and in all places that ye may be in, even until death, that ye may be redeemed of God.

pages.prompt: How could your actions be a stronger witness of Christ today?

o.l: I can act with integrity even when unseen
o.r: Act today with integrity, even when no one else would ever know.

o.l: I can respond to a hard moment the way Christ would
o.r: Respond today to a hard moment the way Christ would.

o.l: I can quietly reflect my beliefs in how I treat others
o.r: Let your treatment of others today quietly reflect your beliefs.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However standing as a witness shows up today, remember your life speaks louder than your words.

p: People notice how you live long before they ever hear what you say you believe.
In Acts 1:8 we read: “But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you.”
Standing as a witness is less about words, and more about a life that quietly confirms them.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Acts 1:8
Share something good about your faith with one person, simply and kindly.

pages.q: Ye are witnesses before God that ye have entered into a covenant with him.

82.pq: The worth of souls is great in the sight of God.

p: To God, every single soul matters, not as a number, but as someone infinitely precious.
Today, think about someone easy to overlook, and see them the way God does.
Before we begin, ask God to help you see people, not just faces in a crowd.

pages.q: The worth of souls is great in the sight of God.

pages.prompt: Who is someone you could treat with greater worth and dignity today?

o.l: I can see someone overlooked as truly valuable
o.r: See someone overlooked today as truly, deeply valuable.

o.l: I can treat a stranger with the same care I'd give a friend
o.r: Treat a stranger today with the same care you'd give a close friend.

o.l: I can remember my own worth is not measured by achievement
o.r: Remember today your own worth was never measured by achievement.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However the value of a soul shapes today, remember no one is a statistic to God.

p: No soul is a statistic to God, not yours, and not anyone else's.
In Doctrine and Covenants 18:11-13 we read: “For, behold, the Lord your Redeemer suffered death in the flesh.”
Seeing people the way He does changes how you treat every single one of them, including yourself.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 18:11-13
Think of someone who feels unseen. Tell them they matter.

pages.q: The worth of souls is great in the sight of God.

83.pq: For if there be no faith among the children of men God can do no miracle among them.

p: Miracles rarely come before faith. Usually, faith is the very thing that opens the door to them.
Today, think about a situation where you're waiting for proof before you're willing to believe.
Before we begin, ask God to help your faith come first, not last.

pages.q: For if there be no faith among the children of men God can do no miracle among them.

pages.prompt: Where could choosing faith first change how you approach a current situation?

o.l: I can trust God before I see the outcome
o.r: Trust God today before you see the outcome you're hoping for.

o.l: I can act in faith even without complete certainty
o.r: Act in faith today, even without complete certainty.

o.l: I can believe change is possible before I see any sign of it
o.r: Believe today that change is possible, before you see any sign of it.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However faith precedes the miracle today, remember belief is usually the condition, not the result.

p: Faith is rarely a response to already having your answer. It is usually the very condition that makes the answer possible.
In Ether 12:6 we read: “And now, I, Moroni, would speak somewhat concerning these things.”
Believe first. The miracle, in whatever form it takes, tends to follow.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Ether 12:6
Take one step of faith today before you see the result.

pages.q: If there be no faith among the children of men God can do no miracle among them.

84.pq: The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith.

p: You can tell what is good by what it produces. Love, joy, peace, patience. These are the fruits of a life close to God.
Today, think about which of these fruits feels strongest, and which feels weakest, in your own life.
Before we begin, ask God to help the weaker fruit grow.

pages.q: The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith.

pages.prompt: Which fruit of the Spirit could you nurture more intentionally today?

o.l: I can practice more patience in a specific situation
o.r: Practice patience today in one specific, difficult situation.

o.l: I can choose peace instead of anxiety
o.r: Choose peace today instead of letting anxiety take hold.

o.l: I can act with more gentleness toward someone
o.r: Act with gentleness today toward someone who tests your patience.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However the fruits of the Spirit show up today, remember you only need to keep tending the ones still forming.

p: You do not need to have every fruit fully grown today. You only need to keep tending the ones still forming.
In John 15:5 we read: “I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit.”
A life close to the Spirit naturally produces more of these. Slowly, and then all at once.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in John 15:5
Pick one fruit of the Spirit, like love or peace. Show it once today.

pages.q: The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith.

85.pq: Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.

p: When God is genuinely first, everything else tends to find its proper place.
Today, think about what has quietly been competing with God for first place in your life.
Before we begin, ask God to help you put Him first again today.

pages.q: Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.

pages.prompt: What is one way you could put God first more intentionally today?

o.l: I can pray before I start my day, not after
o.r: Pray today before your day begins, not after it's already underway.

o.l: I can make a decision based on what honors Him, not just convenience
o.r: Make a decision today based on what honors Him, not just what's convenient.

o.l: I can prioritize spiritual things over something less important
o.r: Prioritize something spiritual today over something less important.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However seeking God first shapes today, remember everything else tends to find its place around it.

p: This is not a promise that life becomes easy when God is first. It is a promise that everything else falls into better order.
In 3 Nephi 13:33 we read: “But seek ye first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things shall be added unto you.”
Seeking Him first is not one more task. It is the lens through which everything else comes into focus.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 3 Nephi 13:33
Start your day with prayer or scripture before you look at your phone.

pages.q: Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness.

86.pq: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven.

p: God's timing rarely matches your own. But it is never careless, and it is never late.
Today, think about something you've been waiting for that hasn't yet arrived.
Before we begin, ask God to help you trust His timing, even when it's hard to wait.

pages.q: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven.

pages.prompt: Where do you need to trust God's timing more than your own?

o.l: I can stop trying to force an outcome before it's ready
o.r: Stop trying today to force an outcome before it's ready.

o.l: I can trust that this waiting season has purpose
o.r: Trust today that this waiting season has real purpose.

o.l: I can be patient with a process that's taking longer than expected
o.r: Be patient today with a process taking longer than you expected.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However divine timing is tested today, remember what feels delayed to you is rarely delayed to God.

p: What feels delayed to you is rarely delayed to God. His timing accounts for things you cannot yet see.
In Habakkuk 2:3 we read: “For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie.”
Trusting that timing does not mean the waiting gets easier. It means the waiting becomes bearable.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Habakkuk 2:3
Write one thing you are waiting for. Thank God for what He is doing now.

pages.q: All these things shall give thee experience, and shall be for thy good.

87.theme: The Power of Small and Simple Things
87.pq: By small and simple things are great things brought to pass.

p: God rarely works only through the dramatic. Most of the time, He works through small, consistent, simple choices.
Today, think about a small habit that, over time, could quietly change everything.
Before we begin, ask God to help you take small steps faithfully, trusting they matter.

pages.q: By small and simple things are great things brought to pass.

pages.prompt: What small, consistent choice could you commit to today?

o.l: I can start a small habit that builds toward something bigger
o.r: Start today a small habit that builds toward something bigger.

o.l: I can trust that a tiny act of faith today matters
o.r: Trust today that a tiny act of faith genuinely matters.

o.l: I can stop waiting for a dramatic moment to finally begin
o.r: Stop waiting today for a dramatic moment, and simply begin.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However small and simple things shape today, remember great things are rarely built any other way.

p: You do not need a grand gesture to change your life. You need a small, faithful choice, repeated long enough to matter.
In Doctrine and Covenants 64:33 we read: “Wherefore, be not weary in well-doing, for ye are laying the foundation of a great work.”
Great things are rarely built any other way.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 64:33
Do one small good thing today that no one will notice.

pages.q: By small and simple things are great things brought to pass.

88.pq: Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.

p: Your neighbor is not just the person next door. It is anyone whose need crosses your path.
Today, think of someone nearby, literally or figuratively, who could use your care.
Before we begin, ask God to widen your definition of neighbor.

pages.q: Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.

pages.prompt: Who is a neighbor you could show more love to today?

o.l: I can check on a literal neighbor I haven't connected with in a while
o.r: Check on a literal neighbor today you haven't connected with in a while.

o.l: I can help someone whose path crosses mine, even briefly
o.r: Help someone today whose path crosses yours, even briefly.

o.l: I can extend the same care to a stranger that I would to a friend
o.r: Extend to a stranger today the same care you'd give a friend.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However loving your neighbor shows up today, remember Christ's definition was never limited by geography.

p: Christ's definition of neighbor was never limited by geography. It was defined by need, and by whoever was willing to respond to it.
In Luke 10:29-37 we read: “But he, willing to justify himself, said unto Jesus, And who is my neighbour?”
That widens the circle considerably, and it widens your opportunity to love, too.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Luke 10:29-37
Greet a neighbor by name, or offer help with something small.

pages.q: Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.

89.pq: Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.

p: Doubt is not the opposite of faith. It is often simply a part of the road faith travels through.
Today, think about a question you've been carrying, and bring it honestly to God instead of pushing it aside.
Before we begin, ask God to meet you exactly where your doubts currently are.

pages.q: Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.

pages.prompt: What is a doubt you could bring honestly to God today, rather than hiding it?

o.l: I can admit a question I've been avoiding
o.r: Admit today a question you've been quietly avoiding.

o.l: I can ask God directly instead of just wondering privately
o.r: Ask God today directly, instead of only wondering privately.

o.l: I can trust that doubt doesn't disqualify me from faith
o.r: Trust today that doubt doesn't disqualify you from real faith.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However doubt is present today, remember bringing it honestly to God may be the most honest faith you have.

p: Even a father in the Gospels who believed still admitted his unbelief, and Christ met him there, not with rejection, but with compassion.
In Jude 1:22 we read: “And of some have compassion, making a difference.”
Bringing your honest doubts to God is not weak faith. It may be the most honest faith you have.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Jude 1:22
Write your doubt, then write one thing you do know. Take both to God in prayer.

pages.q: Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.

90.pq: Strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life.

p: The path to God was never described as wide or crowded. It is narrow, and it takes real intention to stay on it.
Today, think about what has been quietly pulling you off course lately.
Before we begin, ask God to help you find your way back to the path, exactly where you currently are.

pages.q: Strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life.

pages.prompt: What is one thing pulling you off the path that you could correct today?

o.l: I can remove a distraction that's leading me astray
o.r: Remove today a distraction that's been leading you astray.

o.l: I can return to a habit that keeps me close to God
o.r: Return today to a habit that keeps you close to God.

o.l: I can make a small course correction before it becomes a bigger drift
o.r: Make a small course correction today before it becomes a bigger drift.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However the narrow path is tested today, remember every small correction back toward it is real progress.

p: The path was never meant to be easy or crowded. It was meant to lead somewhere worth the effort of staying on it.
In 2 Nephi 31:17-18 we read: “Wherefore, do the things which I have told you I have seen that your Lord and your Redeemer should do.”
Every small correction back toward it is real, meaningful progress.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 2 Nephi 31:17-18
Ask yourself if you are still on the path. Make one small correction today.

pages.q: Strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life.

91.pq: Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.

p: You are in a real, spiritual battle. God has provided armor, not to make you invincible, but to help you stand firm.
Today, think about which piece of that armor, truth, righteousness, faith, the word of God, you need most right now.
Before we begin, ask God to help you put on His armor today.

pages.q: Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.

pages.prompt: Which piece of God's armor do you need to strengthen today?

o.l: I can strengthen my shield of faith against doubt
o.r: Strengthen your shield of faith today against a specific doubt.

o.l: I can hold more firmly to the truth I know
o.r: Hold more firmly today to a truth you already know.

o.l: I can use scripture more actively against temptation
o.r: Use scripture more actively today against a specific temptation.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However God's armor is worn today, remember it was meant for the ordinary moments, not just dramatic ones.

p: This armor was never meant to sit unused. It was meant to be worn daily, in the ordinary moments where the real battle actually happens.
In Ephesians 6:13-17 we read: “Wherefore take unto you the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand.”
Put it on, one piece at a time, and you will find you can stand firm after all.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Ephesians 6:13-17
Choose one piece of the armor of God and use it today.

pages.q: Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.

92.pq: If the Son therefore shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed.

p: True freedom is not the absence of rules. It is liberation from whatever has been controlling you.
Today, think about what has quietly held power over you. A habit, a fear, a grudge.
Before we begin, ask Christ to help you walk in real freedom today.

pages.q: If the Son therefore shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed.

pages.prompt: What is something you could be freed from today, through Christ's help?

o.l: I can be freed from a habit that has controlled me
o.r: Bring that controlling habit to Christ today, and ask for real freedom from it.

o.l: I can be freed from fear that has held me back
o.r: Bring that fear to Christ today, and ask for freedom from what has held you back.

o.l: I can be freed from guilt over something already repented of
o.r: Release today the guilt over something you've already repented of.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However freedom in Christ shows up today, remember He offers release as often as you ask.

p: Real freedom is not doing whatever you want. It is being released from whatever has been quietly enslaving you.
In John 8:32 we read: “And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.”
Christ offers that release. Completely, and as often as you're willing to ask for it.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in John 8:32
Name one habit that holds you. Ask Jesus Christ to help you be free.

pages.q: If the Son therefore shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed.

93.pq: Men ought always to pray, and not to faint.

p: Some prayers are answered instantly. Others require asking again, and again, without giving up.
Today, think about a prayer you've stopped praying because the answer hasn't come yet.
Before we begin, ask God for the persistence to keep asking.

pages.q: Men ought always to pray, and not to faint.

pages.prompt: What is a prayer you could persist in, even without an immediate answer?

o.l: I can keep praying for something I've almost given up on
o.r: Keep praying today for the thing you've nearly given up on.

o.l: I can pray with more consistency, not just intensity
o.r: Pray today with more consistency, not just occasional intensity.

o.l: I can trust that continuing to ask is itself an act of faith
o.r: Trust today that continuing to ask is itself a genuine act of faith.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However perseverance in prayer is tested today, remember an unanswered prayer may simply still be unfolding.

p: An unanswered prayer is not necessarily an ignored one. Sometimes it is simply still unfolding.
In Luke 18:2-8 we read: “Saying, There was in a city a judge, which feared not God, neither regarded man.”
Keep asking. Persistence is not a lack of faith. It may be one of its clearest expressions.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Luke 18:2-8
Pray about the same need three times today. Do not give up.

pages.q: Men ought always to pray, and not to faint.

94.pq: She of her want did cast in all that she had.

p: A small gift given sacrificially can matter more to God than a large one given from abundance.
Today, think about what it would mean to give not from your excess, but from what actually costs you something.
Before we begin, ask God to help you give sacrificially, not just conveniently.

pages.q: She of her want did cast in all that she had.

pages.prompt: What is something you could give that would actually cost you something meaningful?

o.l: I can give time I don't feel like I have to spare
o.r: Give today the time you feel you don't have to spare.

o.l: I can give financially even when it stretches me
o.r: Give financially today, even if it genuinely stretches you.

o.l: I can give attention to someone when I'd rather be doing something else
o.r: Give your full attention today to someone, even when it's inconvenient.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However sacrificial giving shows up today, remember God measures the cost, not the size.

p: God does not measure your gift by its size. He measures it by what it cost you to give it.
In Mark 12:41-44 we read: “And Jesus sat over against the treasury, and beheld how the people cast money into the treasury.”
A small offering, given sacrificially, can matter more than a large one given easily.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Mark 12:41-44
Give something small that costs you something. Do it quietly.

pages.q: She of her want did cast in all that she had.

95.pq: I am the good shepherd, and know my sheep, and am known of mine.

p: Christ knows you individually, not as part of a crowd, but by name, the way a shepherd knows each sheep.
Today, think about what it means that He would leave the ninety-nine to come looking specifically for you.
Before we begin, thank God for being personally, individually known by Him.

pages.q: I am the good shepherd, and know my sheep, and am known of mine.

pages.prompt: How does it change things to know Christ is personally seeking you, specifically?

o.l: It helps me feel less alone in a hard season
o.r: Let this truth today ease the loneliness of a hard season.

o.l: It reminds me my struggles matter to Him personally
o.r: Remember today your struggles genuinely matter to Him, personally.

o.l: It gives me confidence that He knows exactly what I need
o.r: Take confidence today that He already knows exactly what you need.

o.r: However the Good Shepherd's care shows up today, remember He knows you individually, not as one of a crowd.

p: You are never just one of many to Christ. He knows your specific voice, your specific need, your specific story.
In Luke 15:4-6 we read: “What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it?”
That kind of personal attention is not common. It is, however, exactly how He loves you.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Luke 15:4-6
Reach out to one person who has been missing from your circle.

pages.q: I am the good shepherd, and know my sheep, and am known of mine.

96.pq: If any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away.

p: Becoming a new creature in Christ is not a metaphor. It is a real, spiritual transformation, available to anyone willing to change.
Today, think about which part of you feels most in need of that renewal.
Before we begin, ask God to help you become genuinely new, not just improved.

pages.q: If any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away.

pages.prompt: What is one old thing you're ready to let pass away in your life?

o.l: I can let go of an old pattern that no longer fits who I want to be
o.r: Let go today of an old pattern that no longer reflects who you want to become.

o.l: I can release an old wound instead of carrying it forward
o.r: Release today an old wound instead of carrying it forward.

o.l: I can trust that real change is genuinely possible for me
o.r: Trust today that real, lasting change is genuinely possible for you.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However spiritual rebirth shows up today, remember it starts exactly where you are, not where you wish you were.

p: This is not about becoming a slightly better version of your old self. It is about a real transformation, becoming someone genuinely new in Christ.
In Mosiah 27:25-26 we read: “And the Lord said unto me: Marvel not that all mankind, yea, men and women, all nations, kindreds, tongues and people, must be born again.”
That kind of change is available to you, starting exactly where you are today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Mosiah 27:25-26
Write one way you are different from who you used to be. Thank God.

pages.q: If any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away.

97.pq: For my soul delighteth in the song of the heart.

p: A hymn can reach your heart in ways a sermon sometimes cannot. Music has always been part of how God's people worship.
Today, think about a hymn that has quietly carried you through a hard moment.
Before we begin, ask God to let sacred music soften your heart today.

pages.q: For my soul delighteth in the song of the heart.

pages.prompt: What is a hymn or sacred song that has meant something to you personally?

o.l: I can listen to a hymn that has helped me before
o.r: Listen today to a hymn that has carried you through something hard before.

o.l: I can pay closer attention to hymn lyrics during worship
o.r: Pay closer attention today to the words of a hymn during worship.

o.l: I can use music intentionally to invite the Spirit
o.r: Use music today intentionally, to invite the Spirit into a quiet moment.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However sacred music moves you today, remember it can reach places words alone cannot.

p: Sacred music is not simply decoration around worship. It is itself a form of prayer. One that can reach places words alone sometimes cannot.
In Doctrine and Covenants 25:11-12 we read: “And it shall be given thee, also, to make a selection of sacred hymns, as it shall be given thee, which is pleasing unto me, to be had in my church.”
Let it do its quiet work in you today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 25:11-12
Listen to or sing a hymn today. Notice how it makes you feel.

pages.q: For my soul delighteth in the song of the heart.

98.pq: There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God... will... make a way to escape.

p: Christ Himself was tempted, in every way, and did not sin. He understands exactly what you're facing.
Today, think about a specific temptation you've been struggling against.
Before we begin, ask God for strength in that exact moment of weakness.

pages.q: There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God... will... make a way to escape.

pages.prompt: What is a way of escape you could take the next time this temptation arises?

o.l: I can remove myself from a situation before it becomes harder to resist
o.r: Remove yourself today from a situation before it becomes harder to resist.

o.l: I can reach out to someone for accountability
o.r: Reach out today to someone for real accountability.

o.l: I can replace the temptation with something that strengthens me instead
o.r: Replace today's temptation with something that genuinely strengthens you instead.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However temptation is faced today, remember God always provides a way through it.

p: God never promised you wouldn't be tempted. He promised a way through it, every single time, if you are willing to take it.
In Matthew 4:1-11 we read: “Then was Jesus led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil.”
That way of escape is always there. Sometimes it just takes courage to actually use it.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Matthew 4:1-11
Plan your way out of one temptation before it comes.

pages.q: There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man.

99.pq: He shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver.

p: Silver is not purified by being left alone. It is purified by fire, and by the refiner watching closely the entire time.
Today, think about a hard season that may actually be refining you, not just testing you.
Before we begin, ask God to help you trust the process, even while it's uncomfortable.

pages.q: He shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver.

pages.prompt: What is a current difficulty that might actually be refining something in you?

o.l: I can trust that this hard season has real purpose
o.r: Trust today that this hard season carries real, if hidden, purpose.

o.l: I can look for what this trial might be purifying in my character
o.r: Look today for what this trial might be purifying in your character.

o.l: I can believe God is watching closely, even in the heat of it
o.r: Believe today that God is watching closely, even in the heat of it.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However the refiner's fire shapes today, remember He never walks away during it.

p: The refiner never walks away during the fire. He watches closely, removing impurity, until he can see his own reflection in what remains.
In 1 Peter 1:6-7 we read: “Wherein ye greatly rejoice, though now for a season, if need be, ye are in heaviness through manifold temptations.”
That is exactly the kind of attention God gives you through your hardest seasons.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 1 Peter 1:6-7
Think of a hard time that made you stronger. Thank God for it.

pages.q: He shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver.

100.pq: Whatever principle of intelligence we attain unto in this life, it will rise with us in the resurrection.

p: You were not created to reach a finish line and stop. You were created to keep growing, forever.
Today, think about what it means that your growth does not end at death.
Before we begin, thank God for a plan that includes eternal progress, not a final stopping point.

pages.q: Whatever principle of intelligence we attain unto in this life, it will rise with us in the resurrection.

pages.prompt: How does eternal progression change how you see your growth today?

o.l: It helps me be patient with slow progress, since it's not the end
o.r: Let this truth today make you more patient with your own slow progress.

o.l: It reminds me effort now shapes who I become forever
o.r: Remember today your effort now shapes who you become forever.

o.l: It gives me hope that growth never truly stops
o.r: Take hope today that growth never truly stops, in this life or beyond it.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However eternal progression shapes today, remember this life is only the beginning of becoming.

p: This life is not the final exam. It is the beginning of a much longer journey of becoming.

In Doctrine and Covenants 130:19 we read: “And if a person gains more knowledge and intelligence in this life through his diligence and obedience than another, he will have so much the advantage in the world to come.”
Whatever progress you make today continues, in some form, into eternity.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 130:19
Set one small goal to grow this week. Write it down.

pages.q: For behold, this is my work and my glory, to bring to pass the immortality and eternal life of man.

101.pq: Whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord.

p: Honest work is not just a means to an income. It is a way of contributing, serving, and building something worthwhile.
Today, think about how you could bring more integrity and effort into your work today.
Before we begin, ask God to help you see your work as an offering, not just an obligation.

pages.q: Whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord.

pages.prompt: How could you bring more heart into your work today?

o.l: I can do a task fully instead of halfway
o.r: Do today's task fully today, instead of only halfway.

o.l: I can see my work as service, not just a job
o.r: See your work today as an offering, not merely a job.

o.l: I can be honest in my effort, even when no one is watching
o.r: Be honest in your effort today, even when no one else is watching.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However honest work shows up today, remember it can be done as an offering, not just an obligation.

p: Whatever your work looks like today, it can be done as an offering to God, not just a task to finish.
In Doctrine and Covenants 42:42 we read: “Thou shalt not be idle; for he that is idle shall not eat the bread nor wear the garments of the laborer.”
That shift, from obligation to offering, changes the entire feel of ordinary work.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 42:42
Do your work today as if the Lord were watching. Finish well.

pages.q: Whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord.

102.pq: That women adorn themselves in modest apparel.

p: Modesty is not about hiding who you are. It is about presenting yourself in a way that reflects self-respect and respect for others.
Today, think about what modesty means to you personally, beyond appearance alone.
Before we begin, ask God to help you see modesty as dignity, not restriction.

pages.q: That women adorn themselves in modest apparel.

pages.prompt: Where could modesty, in dress, speech, or behavior, reflect greater self-respect today?

o.l: I can present myself in a way that reflects who I truly value
o.r: Present yourself today in a way that reflects what you truly value.

o.l: I can speak in a way that reflects respect for myself and others
o.r: Speak today in a way that reflects respect for yourself and others.

o.l: I can avoid drawing attention in ways that don't reflect my values
o.r: Avoid today drawing attention in ways that don't reflect your real values.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However modesty shows up in your choices today, remember it is dignity, not restriction.

p: Modesty is less about covering up and more about what you choose to emphasize. Dignity over attention, substance over display.
In 1 Peter 3:3-4 we read: “Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel.”
Lived well, it is an expression of self-respect, not a restriction on it.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 1 Peter 3:3-4
Choose to dress and speak today in a way that shows respect for yourself and God.

pages.q: That women adorn themselves in modest apparel.

103.pq: Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.

p: Christ called His disciples friends, not just followers. Real friendship, loyal, honest, present, reflects His own example.
Today, think about a friendship that could use more of your attention.
Before we begin, ask God to help you be a better friend today.

pages.q: Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.

pages.prompt: Who is a friend you could invest in more intentionally today?

o.l: I can reach out to someone I've lost touch with
o.r: Reach out today to a friend you've lost touch with.

o.l: I can be more present with a friend who's going through something hard
o.r: Be more present today with a friend who's going through something hard.

o.l: I can be a more loyal friend, especially when it's inconvenient
o.r: Be a more loyal friend today, especially when it's inconvenient.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However friendship shows up today, remember Christ modeled it as loyal, sacrificial, and constant.

p: Christ modeled friendship at its highest. Loyal, sacrificial, and constant.
In John 15:14-15 we read: “Ye are my friends, if ye do whatsoever I command you.”
You do not need dramatic gestures to be that kind of friend. You simply need to show up, consistently, for the people who matter.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in John 15:14-15
Message a friend you have not spoken to lately. Say you are glad they are in your life.

pages.q: Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.

104.pq: Be thou an example of the believers.

p: People are shaped more by what they see modeled than by what they are told. Your example teaches, whether you intend it to or not.
