Before we begin, ask God to help your life reflect what you actually believe.

pages.q: Be thou an example of the believers.

pages.prompt: What is one way your example could better reflect your beliefs today?

o.l: I can act consistently with what I say I believe
o.r: Act today consistently with what you say you believe.

o.l: I can model patience for someone who's watching how I respond
o.r: Model patience today for someone who is watching how you respond.

o.l: I can let my life quietly teach, not just my words
o.r: Let your life today quietly teach, more than your words do.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However your example speaks today, remember someone is watching more closely than you realize.

p: You are someone's example, whether you've noticed it or not. A child, a friend, a coworker, someone watching more closely than you realize.
In Matthew 5:16 we read: “Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.”
Live today the way you'd want them to remember.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Matthew 5:16
Do one thing today that someone could copy and be better for it.

pages.q: Be thou an example of the believers.

105.pq: Whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven.

p: What is bound on earth through proper priesthood authority is bound in heaven too. This sealing power connects families beyond death.
Today, think about what it means that your family relationships can be made truly eternal.
Before we begin, thank God for the sealing power that makes eternal families possible.

pages.q: Whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven.

pages.prompt: How does the sealing power change the way you see your family relationships?

o.l: It gives me hope that my family bonds can last forever
o.r: Let this truth today give you real hope that your family bonds can last forever.

o.r: Let it motivate you today to nurture a relationship worth sealing.

o.r: Remember today these connections carry genuine eternal weight.

o.r: However the sealing power shapes today, remember it is real authority, not mere symbolism.

p: This power is not symbolic. It is real authority, given by God, to bind together what matters most. For time and for all eternity.
In Doctrine and Covenants 128:9 we read: “A power which records or binds on earth and binds in heaven.”
That is a promise worth building your family around.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:

Write the names of three family members. Pray for each by name.

pages.q: Whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven.

106.pq: For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ.

p: A calling is not about status. It is an opportunity to serve, stretch, and grow in ways you might not have chosen for yourself.
Today, think about a calling, past or present, that changed you more than you expected.
Before we begin, ask God to help you serve willingly in whatever you're asked to do.

pages.q: For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ.

pages.prompt: How could you serve more fully in your current calling or responsibility?

o.r: Approach your calling today with more genuine effort than routine.

o.l: I can trust that this calling is shaping me for a reason
o.r: Trust today that this calling is shaping you for a real reason.

o.l: I can serve without needing recognition
o.r: Serve today without needing recognition for it.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However your calling shapes today, remember it is often exactly the stretching experience you needed.

p: A calling rarely feels convenient at first. But it is often exactly the stretching experience God knew you needed.
In Doctrine and Covenants 107:99 we read: “Wherefore, now let every man learn his duty, and to act in the office in which he is appointed, in all diligence.”
Serve willingly, and watch what it quietly builds in you.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:

Thank someone who serves in a calling. Then do your own calling with care.

pages.q: And they were all called, and did labor diligently.

107.pq: Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness.

p: Righteousness is not about being flawless. It is about consistently choosing to align your life with God's will.
Today, think about one specific area where you could align your choices more closely with what you believe.
Before we begin, ask God to help you desire righteousness, not just avoid guilt.

pages.q: Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness.

o.l: I can make a choice today that reflects what I truly value
o.r: Make a choice today that genuinely reflects what you value.

o.l: I can be more consistent between my beliefs and my actions
o.r: Be more consistent today between your beliefs and your actions.

o.l: I can let go of a small compromise I've been allowing
o.r: Let go today of a small compromise you've been allowing.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However personal righteousness is tested today, remember it is a direction you keep choosing, not a status you achieve.

p: Righteousness is not a status you achieve once. It is a direction you keep choosing, one decision at a time.
In 3 Nephi 12:6 we read: “And blessed are all they who do hunger and thirst after righteousness, for they shall be filled with the Holy Ghost.”
Hungering after it, even imperfectly, is exactly what God asks of you.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 3 Nephi 12:6
Choose one right thing to hunger for today, like prayer or kindness.

pages.q: Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness.

108.pq: And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.

p: Your life is being written, choice by choice, into a record God keeps with perfect accuracy and perfect love.

Before we begin, ask God to help today be a page you'd be glad to have written.

pages.q: And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.

o.r: Make a choice today you'll be glad to look back on.

o.l: I can trust God's record is kept with both accuracy and mercy
o.r: Trust today that God's record of you is kept with both accuracy and mercy.

o.l: I can do something else

p: This is not a record kept to condemn you. It is kept to remember you. Every effort, every small victory, every honest attempt.
In Alma 5:58 we read: “For the names of the righteous shall be written in the book of life, and unto them will I grant an inheritance at my right hand.”
Write today's page with intention.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Alma 5:58
Write one thing you want to be remembered for. Do something toward it today.

pages.q: And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.

109.pq: Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls.

p: Sustaining a leader is more than agreeing with them. It is choosing to support and pray for those God has called to lead.

pages.q: Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls.

pages.prompt: How could you better support a leader in your life today?

That kind of support strengthens everyone, including you.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:

Thank a leader today, and pray for them by name.

pages.q: Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls.

110.pq: Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.

p: Time is one of the few things you cannot get back. How you spend it says a great deal about what you actually value.
Today, think about how much of your time has been consecrated to God, versus simply spent.
Before we begin, ask God to help you use today's time with more intention.

pages.q: Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.

pages.prompt: How could you use your time more intentionally today?

o.l: I can dedicate a specific portion of today to God
o.r: Dedicate a specific portion of today intentionally to God.

o.l: I can be more present instead of just busy
o.r: Be more present today, instead of simply busy.

o.l: I can spend less time on what doesn't actually matter to me
o.r: Spend less time today on what doesn't actually matter to you.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However consecrated time shows up today, remember it is never wasted time.

p: You cannot create more hours in a day. But you can choose, more carefully, what those hours are actually spent on.
In Doctrine and Covenants 88:124 we read: “Cease to be idle; cease to be unclean; cease to find fault one with another.”
Time given to God is never wasted time.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 88:124
Set aside one hour this week for a meaningful purpose. Put it on your calendar.

pages.q: Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.

111.pq: Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.

p: Pride convinces you that you don't need help, don't need correction, and don't need God. Humility is the cure.
Today, think about a place where pride might be quietly blocking your growth.
Before we begin, ask God to help you see yourself honestly.

pages.q: Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.

pages.prompt: Where could a little less pride open you up to real growth?

o.l: I can accept feedback instead of getting defensive
o.r: Accept feedback today instead of becoming defensive.

o.l: I can admit I need help with something
o.r: Admit today that you need help with something specific.

o.l: I can let go of needing to always be right
o.r: Let go today of needing to always be right.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However pride is tested today, remember humility opens exactly the growth pride was blocking.

p: Pride isolates. It convinces you that you're above correction, above help, above needing anyone else.
In Proverbs 11:2 we read: “When pride cometh, then cometh shame: but with the lowly is wisdom.”
Humility, by contrast, opens the door to exactly the growth pride was blocking.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Proverbs 11:2
Admit one mistake out loud today without making an excuse.

pages.q: Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.

112.pq: We know that all things work together for good to them that love God.

p: A mistake is not the end of the story. It is often the very thing that teaches you what nothing else could.
Today, think about a past mistake that ended up teaching you something valuable.
Before we begin, ask God to help you learn instead of just regretting.

pages.q: We know that all things work together for good to them that love God.

pages.prompt: What is a mistake you could reframe as a lesson instead of just a regret?

o.l: I can see a past failure as something that shaped who I am now
o.r: See today a past failure as something that genuinely shaped who you are now.

o.l: I can stop punishing myself for something already repented of
o.r: Stop punishing yourself today for something already repented of.

o.l: I can extract the lesson instead of just carrying the shame
o.r: Extract today's lesson instead of only carrying the shame.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However mistakes are reframed today, remember God can use even your missteps for good.

p: Mistakes are not proof you're failing. Often, they are simply proof you're trying, and trying is exactly how growth happens.

In Doctrine and Covenants 90:24 we read: “Search diligently, pray always, and be believing, and all things shall work together for your good, if ye walk uprightly and remember the covenant wherewith ye have covenanted one with another.”
God can use even your missteps for good, if you let Him.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 90:24
Write one mistake and the lesson it taught you. Thank God for the lesson.

pages.q: We know that all things work together for good to them that love God.

113.pq: Pure religion and undefiled before God... is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction.

p: How a person treats those who cannot repay them says everything about the condition of their heart.
Today, think about someone vulnerable, the poor, the lonely, the overlooked, you could care for today.
Before we begin, ask God to open your eyes to someone in need nearby.

pages.q: Pure religion and undefiled before God... is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction.

pages.prompt: Who is someone vulnerable you could care for today?

o.l: I can check on someone who is elderly or alone
o.r: Check on someone today who is elderly or alone.

o.l: I can help someone who has no way to repay me
o.r: Help someone today who has no way to repay you.

o.l: I can advocate for someone who has no voice in a situation
o.r: Advocate today for someone who has no voice in a situation.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However care for the vulnerable shows up today, remember love is proven most genuine there.

p: Real religion is not measured by ritual alone. It is measured, in part, by how gently you treat those who cannot repay your kindness.
In Mosiah 4:26 we read: “I would that ye should impart of your substance to the poor, every man according to that which he hath, such as feeding the hungry, clothing the naked.”
That is exactly where love is proven most genuine.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Mosiah 4:26
Look for someone who may be struggling alone. Offer one practical help.

pages.q: Pure religion and undefiled before God... is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction.

114.pq: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.

p: A parent's love offers a small glimpse of how completely God loves each of His children.
Today, think about a parent, your own, or yourself as a parent, and the sacrifices love like that requires.
Before we begin, thank God for parental love, wherever it has shown up in your life.

pages.q: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.

pages.prompt: How could you express parental love, given or received, more fully today?

o.l: I can express gratitude to a parent who shaped me
o.r: Express gratitude today to a parent who shaped who you are.

o.l: I can be more patient in my own role as a parent or mentor
o.r: Be more patient today in your own role as a parent or mentor.

o.l: I can trust that consistent love leaves a lasting mark
o.r: Trust today that consistent love leaves a lasting mark, even when it's unseen.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However a parent's love shows up in your life today, remember it reflects God's own patient love.

p: A parent's patient, sacrificial love is one of the clearest reflections of God's love available in mortal life.
In Enos 1:1 we read: “He taught me in his language, and also in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.”
If you've received it, be grateful. If you're giving it, keep going. It matters more than you may ever fully see.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Enos 1:1
Tell a child or young person you love them and why you are proud of them.

pages.q: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.

115.pq: Who shall ascend into the hill of the LORD? or who shall stand in his holy place? He that hath clean hands, and a pure heart…

p: Preparing for the temple is not about becoming perfect. It is about becoming willing, one honest step at a time.
Today, think about where you currently are on your own path toward the temple.
Before we begin, ask God to help you take the next honest step forward.

pages.q: Who shall ascend into the hill of the LORD? or who shall stand in his holy place? He that hath clean hands, and a pure heart; who hath not lifted up his soul unto vanity, nor sworn deceitfully.

pages.prompt: What is one step you could take toward temple preparation today?

o.l: I can learn more about what the temple represents
o.r: Learn today more about what the temple actually represents.

o.l: I can work on living a specific commandment more fully
o.r: Work today on living a specific commandment more fully.

o.l: I can talk with my bishop about my own path forward
o.r: Talk today with your bishop about your own path forward.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However temple preparation shows up today, remember it is about becoming willing, not becoming perfect.

p: In Isaiah 2:3 we read: “And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob.”
No one arrives at the temple door already perfect. They arrive willing, and willingness is exactly the step God asks of you today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Isaiah 2:3
Write one step toward the temple or toward greater worthiness. Do it this week.

pages.q: Establish a house, even a house of prayer, a house of fasting, a house of faith.

116.pq: Stand ye in holy places, and be not moved.

p: Truth does not change based on popularity. Standing for it, even when it's unpopular, takes real courage.
Today, think about a truth you believe that isn't always easy to stand for.
Before we begin, ask God for courage to stand firm today.

pages.q: Stand ye in holy places, and be not moved.

pages.prompt: Where could you stand more firmly for truth today, even if it's uncomfortable?

o.l: I can voice a belief I usually stay quiet about
o.r: Voice today a belief you usually stay quiet about.

o.l: I can avoid compromising something I know is true
o.r: Avoid today compromising something you know to be true.

o.l: I can stand firm even when it's not the popular choice
o.r: Stand firm today, even when it's not the popular choice.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However standing for truth is tested today, remember it does not bend to what is popular.

p: In Doctrine and Covenants 45:32 we read: “But my disciples shall stand in holy places, and shall not be moved.”
Truth was never meant to bend to trends. Standing for it, quietly and consistently, is one of the most Christlike things you can do.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 45:32
Stand up for what is right once today, kindly and without shame.

pages.q: Stand ye in holy places, and be not moved.

117.pq: The gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

p: Eternal life is not something you could ever fully earn. It is God's greatest gift, offered freely to those who come to Him.
Today, think about what it means that this greatest of all gifts is offered to you, personally.
Before we begin, thank God for a gift you could never fully deserve.

pages.q: The gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

pages.prompt: How does knowing eternal life is a gift, not a wage, change how you approach your faith?

o.l: It helps me rest instead of constantly striving for approval
o.r: Let this gift today help you rest instead of constantly striving for approval.

o.l: It reminds me grace matters more than perfect performance
o.r: Remember today grace matters more than perfect performance.

o.l: It fills me with gratitude rather than anxiety
o.r: Let gratitude today replace anxiety about what you haven't yet earned.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However eternal life as a gift shapes today, remember no effort could ever fully purchase it.

p: In Doctrine and Covenants 14:7 we read: “And, if you keep my commandments and endure to the end you shall have eternal life, which gift is the greatest of all the gifts of God.”
No effort could ever fully purchase eternal life. It is, and always will be, a gift. Offered freely by a God who loves you completely.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 14:7
Thank God for the gift of eternal life through Jesus Christ.

pages.q: The gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

118.pq: For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.

p: Fear can feel enormous in the moment. But it does not have the final say over your choices.
Today, think about a fear that has been quietly holding you back.
Before we begin, ask God for peace to replace that fear.

pages.q: For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.

pages.prompt: What is a fear you could take one small step past today?

o.l: I can do something despite feeling afraid of it
o.r: Do today, despite the fear, the thing you've been avoiding.

o.l: I can bring a specific fear honestly to God
o.r: Bring a specific fear today honestly to God.

o.l: I can trust His power more than my own anxiety
o.r: Trust today His power more than your own anxiety.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However fear is faced today, remember power, love, and a sound mind were given to you instead.

p: Fear will always try to convince you it's in charge. But it was never given to you by God. Power, love, and a sound mind were.
In Isaiah 41:10 we read: “Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed.”
Choose those instead, one small step at a time.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Isaiah 41:10
Name one fear. Pray for courage, then take one small step.

pages.q: For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.

119.theme: The Value of Silence and Solitude
119.pq: Be still, and know that I am God.

p: God often speaks in quiet moments, not in noise. Silence is not empty. It can be full of exactly what you need to hear.
Today, think about how much genuine silence you've allowed yourself lately.
Before we begin, find a quiet moment and simply listen.

pages.q: Be still, and know that I am God.

pages.prompt: Where could you make room for silence and stillness today?

o.l: I can spend a few quiet minutes without any distraction
o.r: Spend a few quiet minutes today without any distraction.

o.l: I can turn off noise and simply be present
o.r: Turn off the noise today and simply be present.

o.l: I can use silence to actually listen instead of just talk
o.r: Use silence today to actually listen, instead of only talking.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However stillness shows up today, remember sometimes the most important thing is simply to stop and listen.

p: In a world constantly filling every quiet moment with noise, choosing stillness is its own quiet act of faith.
In 1 Kings 19:11-12 we read: “And he said, Go forth, and stand upon the mount before the LORD.”
Sometimes, the most important thing you can do is simply stop, and listen.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 1 Kings 19:11-12
Find five quiet minutes today. Sit still and listen.

pages.q: Be still, and know that I am God.

120.pq: This is my doctrine, and it is the doctrine which the Father hath given unto me.

p: Faith, repentance, baptism, the Holy Ghost, and enduring to the end. This simple pattern is the doctrine of Christ.
Today, think about which part of this pattern you could apply more fully in your life right now.
Before we begin, ask God to help you walk this pattern faithfully today.

pages.q: This is my doctrine, and it is the doctrine which the Father hath given unto me.

pages.prompt: Which part of this pattern could you strengthen today?

o.l: I can deepen my faith in a specific way
o.r: Deepen your faith today in one specific, concrete way.

o.l: I can repent honestly of something specific
o.r: Repent honestly today of something specific, not just in general.

o.l: I can renew my commitment to my baptismal covenant
o.r: Renew today your commitment to your baptismal covenant.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However the doctrine of Christ shapes today, remember its simplicity is exactly what makes it something to return to for life.

p: This pattern is not complicated. It is simple, clear, and available to anyone willing to walk it. One honest step at a time.
In 2 Nephi 31:19-20 we read: “And now, my beloved brethren, after ye have gotten into this strait and narrow path, I would ask if all is done?”
That simplicity is exactly what makes it something you can return to, again and again, for the rest of your life.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 2 Nephi 31:19-20
List the steps of the doctrine of Christ. Choose the one you want to strengthen.

pages.q: This is my doctrine, and it is the doctrine which the Father hath given unto me.

121.pq: Give instruction to a wise man, and he will be yet wiser: teach a just man, and he will increase in learning.

p: No matter how much we know, there is always more to learn.
A teachable heart accepts correction, seeks understanding, and is willing to grow.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you learn before continuing.

pages.q: Give instruction to a wise man, and he will be yet wiser: teach a just man, and he will increase in learning.

pages.prompt: How will you respond when you have an opportunity to learn today?

o.l: I will listen with an open heart.
o.r: Listening with an open heart can help you notice truth you may have missed before. Ask God to help you understand and apply what you learn.

o.l: I will accept helpful correction.
o.r: Helpful correction can guide your growth when you receive it with humility. You do not have to be discouraged when you discover something you can improve.

o.l: I will seek to learn something new.
o.r: Choosing to learn something new can strengthen your mind and increase your understanding. Look for one truth today that can help you become better.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to show that you are willing to learn. Ask God to help you recognize opportunities for growth throughout the day.

p: Learning is part of becoming more like Jesus Christ. Growth continues when we remain willing to receive truth.
In Doctrine and Covenants 88:118 we read: “And as all have not faith, seek ye diligently and teach one another words of wisdom.”
You do not need to know everything today. A willing heart can take the next step.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 88:118
Ask someone for feedback today. Listen without defending yourself.

pages.q: A teachable heart is willing to learn, change, and grow.

122.pq: Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits:

p: Life can move quickly, and it is easy to focus only on what is still missing.
Remembering God's blessings helps us see His care more clearly. Even small blessings can remind us that we are not forgotten.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you remember His goodness before continuing.

pages.q: Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits:

pages.prompt: What will you do to remember God's blessings today?

o.l: I will write down one blessing.
o.r: Writing down one blessing can help you remember it later. Take time to notice why that blessing matters to you.

o.l: I will thank God for something specific.
o.r: Specific thanks can make prayer more personal and meaningful. Tell Heavenly Father exactly what you appreciate today.

o.l: I will remember a time God helped me.
o.r: Remembering past help can strengthen you in present challenges. Let that memory remind you that God has not changed.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Find another simple way to remember God's blessings. Choose something that helps you recognize His care in your life.

p: Remembering does not remove every difficulty, but it can strengthen our perspective. God's past blessings can give us confidence to continue.
In Alma 37:36-37 we read: “Yea, and cry unto God for all thy support; yea, let all thy doings be unto the Lord, and whithersoever thou goest let it be in the Lord.”
Take one moment today to pause and remember.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Alma 37:36-37
Write five blessings from this week. Thank God for each one.

pages.q: Remembering God's help can strengthen us for what comes next.

123.pq: Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.

p: Knowing information is useful, but understanding helps us know how truth applies to our lives.
God invites us to seek wisdom with effort, patience, and prayer.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you understand truth before continuing.

pages.q: Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.

pages.prompt: What will you do when you do not fully understand something important?

o.l: I will study it carefully.
o.r: Careful study can help you move beyond a quick answer. Give yourself time to read, think, and consider what is true.

o.l: I will ask God for understanding.
o.r: God can help you see truth more clearly. Pray honestly and remain willing to receive understanding over time.

o.l: I will ask a trustworthy person for help.
o.r: A trustworthy person may offer knowledge or experience that helps you learn. Listen carefully, then continue seeking your own understanding.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another good step toward greater understanding. Do not give up simply because the answer is not immediate.

p: Understanding often grows step by step. Some answers come quickly, while others require continued learning.
In James 1:5-6 we read: “If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not.”
Keep seeking truth with both your mind and your heart.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in James 1:5-6
Write one question you want answered. Study and pray about it today.

pages.q: Do not stop seeking simply because understanding takes time.

124.pq: Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin.

p: There are times when we know what is right but feel pressure to choose something else.
Doing what is right often begins with one clear decision. God can give us strength to act on the truth we already know.
Take a moment to pray and ask God for courage to choose what is right before continuing.

pages.q: Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin.

pages.prompt: When you know what is right, what will you do?

o.l: I will act on what I know.
o.r: Truth becomes part of our lives when we act on it. Take one clear step instead of waiting for the perfect moment.

o.l: I will ask God for strength first.
o.r: Asking God for strength can help when the right choice feels difficult. Then move forward with the help you receive.

o.l: I will encourage someone else to do what is right.
o.r: Your encouragement may help another person make a good choice. Speak with kindness and lead through your own actions.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another honest action that reflects what you know is right. Let your decision show that truth matters to you.

p: Knowing what is right is important, but choosing it gives that knowledge power in our lives.
In Joshua 24:15 we read: “And if it seem evil unto you to serve the LORD, choose you this day whom ye will serve.”
Today, let one good decision become an act of faith.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Joshua 24:15
Make one choice today because it is right, not because it is easy.

pages.q: When we know what is right, we can ask God for strength and act.

125.pq: Rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth;

p: Truth gives us a foundation we can trust.
We can learn to find joy in what is honest, good, and true, even when truth asks us to change.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you love truth before continuing.

pages.q: Rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth;

pages.prompt: How will you show that truth matters to you today?

o.l: I will be honest in my words.
o.r: Honest words build trust and reflect respect for truth. Speak clearly and avoid saying what you know is not true.

o.l: I will accept a truth that challenges me.
o.r: A challenging truth can become an opportunity to grow. Ask God to help you respond with willingness rather than resistance.

o.l: I will choose truth over approval.
o.r: Other people's approval can change, but truth does not depend on popularity. Let your choices be guided by what you know is right.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to show respect for truth. Let your actions match the principles you believe.

p: Truth does not become less valuable when it is difficult to accept. It can guide us toward greater freedom and growth.
In John 8:31-32 we read: “Then said Jesus to those Jews which believed on him, If ye continue in my word, then are ye my disciples indeed.”
Ask God to help you recognize truth and rejoice in it.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in John 8:31-32
Share one piece of good news about someone else today.

pages.q: A love for truth helps us remain honest when other choices seem easier.

126.pq: For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again:

p: Everyone has moments when things do not go as planned.
A setback does not have to become the end of your effort. Through Jesus Christ, we can learn, rise, and continue.
Take a moment to pray and ask God for strength to begin again before continuing.

pages.q: For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again:

pages.prompt: What will you do after a setback?

o.l: I will learn from what happened.
o.r: Learning from what happened can help you make a wiser choice next time. Be honest about the lesson without becoming harsh toward yourself.

o.l: I will try again.
o.r: Trying again is an act of courage. Take the next right step, even if it is small.

o.l: I will ask for help.
o.r: Asking for help can give you support and direction. You do not have to face every difficulty alone.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another good way to move forward after this setback. Do not let one difficult moment decide your whole future.

p: Falling short does not mean you cannot progress. What matters is your willingness to turn again toward what is good.
In Micah 7:8 we read: “Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy: when I fall, I shall arise.”
Today can be a new beginning.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Micah 7:8
Think of something you stopped trying. Take one small step to begin again.

pages.q: A setback can teach us, but it does not have to stop us.

127.pq: Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me.

p: The Lord invites us to hear His voice and respond.
His guidance may come through scripture, prayer, righteous thoughts, or quiet spiritual impressions.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you listen before continuing.

pages.q: Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me.

pages.prompt: How will you make room to listen for the Lord today?

o.l: I will spend a few quiet minutes listening.
o.r: Quiet time can help you notice thoughts and feelings that are easy to miss when you are distracted. Listen patiently without demanding an immediate answer.

o.l: I will read scripture slowly.
o.r: Reading slowly can give truth time to reach your heart and mind. Notice one phrase that speaks to your current needs.

o.l: I will remove one distraction.
o.r: Removing one distraction can create more room for spiritual attention. Choose something you can set aside for a little while today.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Find another way to become more attentive to the Lord. Come to Him with a sincere desire to hear and follow.

p: Listening is more than being silent. It includes being willing to notice and respond to what God teaches us.
In 1 Samuel 3:10 we read: “And the LORD came, and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel.”
Make room today for the Lord's voice.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 1 Samuel 3:10
Sit quietly for five minutes. Ask God what He wants you to hear.

pages.q: A willing heart makes room to hear the Lord.

128.pq: Thou shalt have no other gods before me.

p: Many things compete for our attention each day.
Putting God first helps us examine our priorities and make choices that bring us closer to Him.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you place Him first before continuing.

pages.q: Thou shalt have no other gods before me.

pages.prompt: What will you put first today?

o.l: I will begin my day with God.
o.r: Beginning your day with God can help set your direction. Offer a sincere prayer before the demands of the day take your attention.

o.l: I will make time for what matters most.
o.r: Important things often require intentional time. Look at your day and protect even a small period for spiritual priorities.

o.l: I will review one of my priorities.
o.r: Reviewing a priority can help you see whether your actions match what you value. Make one adjustment if you see a better way forward.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to give God a central place in your day. Let your decision be sincere and practical.

p: Putting God first does not mean ignoring our responsibilities. It means allowing His truth to guide how we meet them.
In Matthew 22:37 we read: “Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.”
One intentional choice today can show what matters most to you.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Matthew 22:37
Put God first in one decision today. Ask what He would have you do.

pages.q: When God guides our priorities, our choices can become clearer.

129.pq: Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God.

p: Our inner desires and thoughts influence the choices we make.
A pure heart seeks what is good and turns away from what weakens our relationship with God.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you develop a pure heart before continuing.

pages.q: Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God.

pages.prompt: What will help you keep your heart focused on what is good?

o.l: I will guard what I allow into my mind.
o.r: What you repeatedly watch, hear, and think about can shape your desires. Choose something today that helps your mind remain clean and focused.

o.l: I will replace an unhelpful thought with a good one.
o.r: You can choose not to continue feeding every thought that enters your mind. Turn your attention toward something true, worthy, and good.

o.l: I will ask God to change my desires.
o.r: God can help us want what is right more deeply. Pray honestly about the desires you want to strengthen or change.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another action that helps your heart move toward goodness. Small choices can shape your desires over time.

p: Purity begins within and affects how we live. God can help us change what needs to change.
In Alma 5:19 we read: “I say unto you, can ye look up to God at that day with a pure heart and clean hands?”
Choose one thing today that brings your heart closer to Him.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Alma 5:19
Choose one thing today that keeps your thoughts clean and your heart light.

pages.q: The things we welcome into our hearts can shape the people we become.

130.pq: He that is slow to wrath is of great understanding: but he that is hasty of spirit exalteth folly.

p: Anger can lead us to speak or act before we have thought clearly.
Being slow to anger does not mean ignoring problems. It means choosing a response with greater understanding and control.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you respond calmly before continuing.

pages.q: He that is slow to wrath is of great understanding: but he that is hasty of spirit exalteth folly.

pages.prompt: What will you do when you feel anger rising today?

o.l: I will pause before I speak.
o.r: A short pause can prevent words you may later regret. Give yourself time to choose a response that is honest and respectful.

o.l: I will try to understand the other person.
o.r: Understanding another person's situation may change how you respond. Listen before deciding what their actions mean.

o.l: I will step away until I am calmer.
o.r: Taking a short break can help you regain control. Return to the situation when you are better prepared to respond wisely.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another good way to prevent anger from controlling your actions. Ask God to help you respond with greater understanding.

p: We cannot always control what happens around us, but we can learn to control how we respond.
In James 1:19-20 we read: “Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath.”
Today, give yourself time to choose your words and actions carefully.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in James 1:19-20
When you feel anger rising today, pause and breathe before you speak.

pages.q: A pause can give wisdom time to guide our response.

131.pq: Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death: that like as Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Fathe…

p: Jesus Christ makes change possible.
Walking in newness of life means we do not have to remain the same when we choose to follow Him.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you move forward with a willing heart before continuing.

pages.q: Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death: that like as Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life.

pages.prompt: What new direction will you choose today?

o.l: I will leave one wrong habit behind.
o.r: Leaving a wrong habit may begin with one specific decision. Ask God for help and prepare a better action to take in its place.

o.l: I will begin one good habit.
o.r: A good habit can begin with a small action repeated consistently. Choose something realistic that brings you closer to God.

o.l: I will make one better choice than yesterday.
o.r: Progress does not require you to change everything at once. Look for one decision you can improve today.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another step that reflects your desire to move forward with Christ. Let today include a real change, even if it is small.

p: The gospel of Jesus Christ is a message of real change. Through Him, we can leave behind what is wrong and become better.
In Mosiah 5:2 we read: “And they all cried with one voice, saying: Yea, we believe all the words which thou hast spoken unto us.”
Do not wait for another day to take one new step.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Mosiah 5:2
Write one habit of your old life you are leaving. Choose one new habit to start.

pages.q: Because of Jesus Christ, we can choose a better direction and begin again.

132.pq: But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth:

p: Not every good action needs to be seen by other people.
Quiet goodness can help us focus on the person we are helping rather than the attention we may receive.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you do good with sincere motives before continuing.

pages.q: But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth:

pages.prompt: How will you do good without seeking attention today?

o.l: I will help someone privately.
o.r: Private help can protect another person's dignity and show sincere care. Look for a need you can meet without making yourself the focus.

o.l: I will do a good deed without telling anyone.
o.r: Doing good without announcing it can strengthen your motives. Let God know what you have done and be satisfied with that.

o.l: I will give credit to someone else.
o.r: Giving credit to someone else can show generosity and fairness. Notice the contribution another person has made and acknowledge it sincerely.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another quiet act of goodness. Let your focus remain on doing what is right rather than being noticed.

p: The value of a good act does not depend on how many people see it. God knows the desires behind our actions.
In Matthew 6:1-4 we read: “Take heed that ye do not your alms before men, to be seen of them.”
Choose goodness today because it is good.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Matthew 6:1-4
Do one good deed today and tell no one about it.

pages.q: Goodness does not need attention to have value.

133.pq: For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.

p: Every life is built on something.
When Jesus Christ is our foundation, His teachings can guide us through both calm and difficult times.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you build your life more firmly on Christ before continuing.

pages.q: For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.

pages.prompt: What will you do to strengthen your foundation in Jesus Christ?

o.l: I will follow one teaching of Jesus Christ more carefully.
o.r: Choose one teaching of the Savior and look for a clear way to live it today. Consistent action strengthens the foundation of faith.

o.l: I will turn to Christ when I feel uncertain.
o.r: Uncertainty can become a reason to seek the Savior more closely. Pray, study His words, and ask what He would have you do.

o.l: I will examine what guides my decisions.
o.r: Your decisions can reveal what has the strongest influence in your life. Consider whether your choices are becoming more centered on Christ.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another practical way to build your life on Jesus Christ. A strong foundation is built through repeated choices.

p: A foundation matters most when pressure comes. Christ offers truth and strength that do not depend on changing circumstances.
In Luke 6:48 we read: “He is like a man which built an house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock.”
Build on Him one choice at a time.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Luke 6:48
Write what your life is built on. Name one thing that makes it stronger.

pages.q: A life built on Jesus Christ has a foundation that can endure.

134.pq: A wholesome tongue is a tree of life: but perverseness therein is a breach in the spirit.

p: Our words can affect another person's day and sometimes much more.
We can choose words that are truthful, respectful, and helpful, even when we need to address a difficult matter.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you speak words that build before continuing.

pages.q: A wholesome tongue is a tree of life: but perverseness therein is a breach in the spirit.

pages.prompt: How will you use your words to help someone today?

o.l: I will give sincere encouragement.
o.r: Sincere encouragement can strengthen someone who feels tired or unnoticed. Make your words specific and honest.

o.l: I will speak more carefully.
o.r: Speaking more carefully can prevent unnecessary harm. Before you speak, consider whether your words are true and helpful.

o.l: I will apologize for hurtful words.
o.r: An honest apology can begin to repair damage caused by words. Take responsibility without making excuses.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to use your words for good. Let your speech reflect the respect you want to show others.

p: Words cannot always be taken back, so wisdom in speech matters. We can choose language that strengthens instead of damages.
In Ephesians 4:29 we read: “Let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth, but that which is good to the use of edifying, that it may minister grace unto the hearers.”
Let one conversation today become an opportunity to build someone up.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Ephesians 4:29
Say one encouraging thing to someone today. Choose the words with care.

pages.q: Words can strengthen a person when they are spoken with truth and care.

135.pq: Judge not, that ye be not judged.

p: We often see only part of another person's story.
Jesus Christ teaches us to be careful about condemning others. We can hold to truth while still choosing fairness and mercy.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you see others more clearly before continuing.

pages.q: Judge not, that ye be not judged.

pages.prompt: How will you respond when you are tempted to judge someone quickly?

o.l: I will remember that I do not know everything.
o.r: Remembering what you do not know can make room for greater fairness. Avoid deciding another person's whole story from one moment.

o.l: I will look for something good in the person.
o.r: Looking for good does not mean pretending wrong is right. It means remembering that every person has worth and can grow.

o.l: I will focus on improving myself.
o.r: Examining your own choices can lead to meaningful progress. Use your energy to correct what you can change in your own life.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another response that is fair and merciful. Ask God to help you see people with greater understanding.

p: We can make wise decisions without treating ourselves as the final judge of another person's heart.
In Luke 6:36-37 we read: “Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful.”
Today, choose understanding before unnecessary condemnation.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Luke 6:36-37
Notice a time you judge someone today. Replace it with a question.

pages.q: We see only part of another person's story, so we should be careful in our judgments.

136.pq: Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.

p: Peace does not always happen by accident.
A peacemaker chooses words and actions that reduce conflict and help people move toward understanding.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you become a peacemaker before continuing.

pages.q: Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.

pages.prompt: What will you do to bring more peace into a situation today?

o.l: I will listen before responding.
o.r: Listening can help you understand what is truly happening. Give the other person time to speak before preparing your answer.

o.l: I will refuse to spread conflict.
o.r: You do not have to repeat words that increase anger between people. Choose not to carry harmful messages from one person to another.

o.l: I will take the first step toward peace.
o.r: The first step may be a calm conversation, an apology, or a willingness to forgive. Do what you can without forcing another person's response.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another action that can reduce conflict and increase understanding. Ask God to guide you toward a peaceful response.

p: Being a peacemaker does not mean avoiding every difficult conversation. It means approaching those conversations with a desire for truth and peace.
In Romans 12:18 we read: “If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.”
Look for one place today where your choices can reduce conflict.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Romans 12:18
Help settle one disagreement today, or choose not to start one.

pages.q: Peace can begin when one person chooses understanding over unnecessary conflict.

137.pq: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.

p: Some burdens are difficult to carry for a long time.
Jesus Christ invites us to come to Him. His rest can include strength, peace, direction, and help as we continue through life.
Take a moment to pray and bring your burdens honestly to God before continuing.

pages.q: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.

pages.prompt: How will you come closer to Christ when you feel burdened?

o.l: I will tell Him honestly how I feel.
o.r: You do not need perfect words when you pray. Tell God honestly what is weighing on your heart and ask for the help you need.

o.l: I will spend quiet time with Him.
o.r: Quiet time can help you turn your attention away from constant pressure. Sit with the Lord in prayer and allow yourself time to be still.

o.l: I will take one manageable step.
o.r: You may not be able to solve everything today. Ask Christ to help you identify the next step you can take.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to turn toward the Savior. Bring Him your real burden and trust that He understands.

p: Coming to Christ does not mean every burden disappears immediately. It means we do not have to face life without His help.
In 1 Peter 5:7 we read: “Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.”
You can come to Him exactly as you are.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 1 Peter 5:7
Take a rest today, even a short one. Hand your burden to the Savior.

pages.q: Jesus Christ invites us to bring Him the burdens we cannot carry alone.

138.pq: Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just…

p: Our minds often notice faults quickly.
Choosing to see the good in others can change how we speak, think, and build relationships.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you notice the good around you before continuing.

pages.q: Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things.

pages.prompt: How will you focus more on the good in someone today?

o.l: I will notice one strength in them.
o.r: Every person has something good that can be recognized. Look beyond your first impression and notice a real strength.

o.l: I will tell them something I appreciate.
o.r: A sincere expression of appreciation can help someone feel seen. Say something specific that you truly value about them.

o.l: I will stop repeating their weaknesses.
o.r: Repeatedly focusing on another person's weaknesses can damage trust and relationships. Choose not to make their faults the main subject of your thoughts or conversations.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Find another way to recognize the good in someone. Let your choice reflect the truth that people are more than their weaknesses.

p: Seeing the good in others does not require us to ignore problems. It helps us remember that each person has value.
In Doctrine and Covenants 121:45 we read: “Let thy bowels also be full of charity towards all men, and to the household of faith, and let virtue garnish thy thoughts unceasingly.”
Today, let someone be strengthened because you chose to notice what is good.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 121:45
Tell someone one good thing you see in them.

pages.q: People are more than the weaknesses we first notice.

139.pq: But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run…

p: Waiting can be difficult when we want answers or change quickly.
Waiting upon the Lord includes continuing to trust, act, and remain faithful while we seek His timing.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to strengthen you as you wait before continuing.

pages.q: But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.

pages.prompt: How will you wait upon the Lord with greater faith?

o.l: I will continue doing what I know is right.
o.r: Waiting does not mean doing nothing. Continue with the good you already know to do while you seek further direction.

o.l: I will be patient with the process.
o.r: Some growth and answers take time. Ask God to help you remain steady when progress feels slow.

o.l: I will trust that God sees more than I do.
o.r: You may not see every reason for a delay or difficulty. Trusting God's greater knowledge can help you remain faithful through uncertainty.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another faithful action while you wait. Let this period become a time of growth rather than only a time of delay.

p: Waiting upon the Lord can strengthen us when we continue turning toward Him. His timing may be different from ours, but we can keep moving forward in faith.
In Psalm 27:14 we read: “Wait on the LORD: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart.”
Today, trust God with what you cannot yet see.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Psalm 27:14
Pick one thing you are waiting on. Pray with patience and trust.

pages.q: While we wait for answers, we can continue doing the good we already know to do.

140.pq: Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth.

p: Our thoughts influence our feelings, desires, and choices.
We cannot always control the first thought that comes, but we can choose what we continue to give our attention.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you direct your thoughts toward what is good before continuing.

pages.q: Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth.

pages.prompt: What will you do when your thoughts move toward something unhelpful?

o.l: I will turn my attention to something good.
o.r: Changing your focus can interrupt an unhelpful pattern. Choose a truth, task, or uplifting thought that deserves your attention.

o.l: I will pray for help.
o.r: Prayer can help you turn your mind toward God. Ask for strength to release the thought and choose something better.

o.l: I will fill my mind with truth.
o.r: Truth can give your mind something stronger to hold onto. Read or remember a scripture that helps you focus on what is good.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another healthy way to direct your attention. Do not assume that every thought deserves to remain in your mind.

p: A better life is often built through repeated choices, including choices about where we place our attention.
In Mosiah 4:30 we read: “But this much I can tell you, that if ye do not watch yourselves, and your thoughts, and your words, and your deeds, and observe the commandments of God.”
Today, choose one thought that will help you move closer to God.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Mosiah 4:30
Notice one thought today that pulls you down. Replace it with a better one.

pages.q: We can choose what we continue to give our attention.

141.pq: But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another…

p: God invites us to live where truth can guide us.
Walking in the light means choosing what brings us closer to Jesus Christ, even when a better choice requires effort.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you walk in His light before continuing.

pages.q: But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin.

pages.prompt: What will help you walk more fully in God's light today?

o.l: I will choose one good thing even when it is difficult.
o.r: A difficult good choice can strengthen your commitment to Christ. Focus on the next right action and ask God for strength to take it.

o.l: I will leave behind something that pulls me away from God.
o.r: Leaving something behind may create space for a better influence in your life. Identify one change you can begin today.

o.l: I will follow the truth I already know.
o.r: You may not have every answer, but you can act on the truth you have already received. Faithfulness often begins with what is already clear.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another action that moves you closer to Jesus Christ. Let your decision today reflect your desire to live in His light.

p: Walking in the light happens through daily choices. Each choice can help us move closer to God.
In John 12:35-36 we read: “Then Jesus said unto them, Yet a little while is the light with you.”
You do not need to change everything at once. Take one step toward the light today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in John 12:35-36
Do one thing today that you would be glad to have everyone see.

pages.q: Every good choice can become another step toward the light.

142.theme: Holding Fast to What Is Good
142.pq: Prove all things; hold fast that which is good.

p: Not every idea, influence, or message deserves our trust.
God invites us to examine what we receive and hold firmly to what is good and true.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you recognize what is good before continuing.

pages.q: Prove all things; hold fast that which is good.

pages.prompt: How will you hold fast to what is good today?

o.l: I will keep one good habit.
o.r: A good habit can strengthen your life through repeated action. Continue doing what helps you become the person you want to be.

o.l: I will test an idea against truth.
o.r: Not every idea is equally reliable. Compare what you hear with scripture and the truths God has already revealed.

o.l: I will protect a good influence in my life.
o.r: Good influences deserve intentional care. Make time for something that consistently helps you choose what is right.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to keep what is good close to you. Do not easily release something that strengthens your relationship with God.

p: Discernment helps us choose carefully. Once we recognize what is good, we can make a deliberate effort to keep it.
In Moroni 7:13 we read: “But behold, that which is of God inviteth and enticeth to do good continually.”
Hold firmly to the truths that help you move forward.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Moroni 7:13
Write one good thing you want to hold onto. Keep it close this week.

pages.q: Recognizing what is good matters, but choosing to hold fast to it matters too.

143.pq: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.

p: The way we live can influence people around us.
We do not need to seek attention for our goodness. A faithful life can quietly point others toward what is true and good.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help your life reflect His goodness before continuing.

pages.q: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.

pages.prompt: How will you let your light be seen through your actions today?

o.l: I will do what is right when no one expects it.
o.r: Unexpected goodness can show the strength of your character. Choose what is right because it matters, not because someone is watching.

o.l: I will treat someone with greater respect.
o.r: Respect can be shown through your words, attention, and actions. Let one person feel their worth through the way you treat them.

o.l: I will be a good example in one situation.
o.r: You do not need to be perfect to influence someone for good. One faithful choice can encourage another person to choose well too.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another action that reflects the goodness you believe in. Let your life give others a reason to see something better.

p: Our actions can speak before we say anything. A life centered on good choices can bless people around us.
In 3 Nephi 18:24 we read: “Therefore, hold up your light that it may shine unto the world.”
Let your light be seen through something you do today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 3 Nephi 18:24
Do one quiet act of goodness today that shows your faith.

pages.q: One faithful action can quietly influence another person for good.

144.pq: Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees;

p: Some people around us may be struggling in ways we cannot easily see.
We can notice those who need encouragement and help them feel less alone.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you notice someone who needs strength before continuing.

pages.q: Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees;

pages.prompt: How will you strengthen someone who may be struggling today?

o.l: I will check on someone.
o.r: A simple question can show that you care. Reach out sincerely and give the person space to respond honestly.

o.l: I will offer practical help.
o.r: Practical help can reduce a real burden. Look for something specific you can do rather than only wishing the person well.

o.l: I will give sincere encouragement.
o.r: Sincere encouragement can remind someone of strengths they may have forgotten. Speak honestly about something good you see in them.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to strengthen someone today. Ask God to help you recognize a need and respond with genuine care.

p: We may not be able to remove every burden another person carries. But we can often help them carry the day with greater strength.
In Mosiah 18:8-9 we read: “Are willing to mourn with those that mourn; yea, and comfort those that stand in need of comfort.”
Look around today and notice whose hands may need lifting.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Mosiah 18:8-9
Call or visit someone who feels weak or alone. Offer to help in one way.

pages.q: Sometimes strength begins when someone realizes they are not alone.

145.pq: Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.

p: Being hurt can make forgiveness difficult.
Forgiveness does not mean saying that wrong actions were acceptable. It means choosing not to let resentment control our hearts.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you move toward forgiveness before continuing.

pages.q: Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.

pages.prompt: What step can you take toward a more forgiving heart today?

o.l: I will stop repeating the offense in my mind.
o.r: Repeatedly returning to an offense can keep the pain active. When the thought returns, gently choose to focus on a healthier direction.

o.l: I will pray for help to forgive.
o.r: You may need God's help before you feel ready to forgive. Be honest about the hurt and ask Him to change what you cannot change alone.

o.l: I will choose not to seek revenge.
o.r: Refusing revenge can break a cycle of further harm. Leave room for justice while choosing not to add more wrong through your own actions.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another safe and honest step toward releasing resentment. Forgiveness can be a process, and you can begin with one sincere decision.

p: A forgiving heart often develops over time. God can help us release what we cannot heal by ourselves.
In Doctrine and Covenants 64:9-10 we read: “Wherefore, I say unto you, that ye ought to forgive one another.”
Take one step today toward greater freedom from resentment.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 64:9-10
Write the name of someone you need to forgive. Pray for them today.

pages.q: Forgiveness can begin before every feeling has fully changed.

146.pq: If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God.

p: Daily responsibilities are important, but they are not the only things that should guide our lives.
We can make choices with eternal values in mind and allow Christ to shape what we seek.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you seek what has lasting value before continuing.

pages.q: If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God.

pages.prompt: What will you give greater attention to because it has lasting value?

o.l: I will strengthen my relationship with God.
o.r: Your relationship with God grows through time and sincere attention. Choose one simple action that helps you come closer to Him today.

o.l: I will invest in an important relationship.
o.r: Relationships can require time, patience, and care. Reach out to someone whose presence in your life has lasting value.

o.l: I will choose what matters over what only distracts me.
o.r: Some activities take attention without giving much back. Review one part of your day and choose something more meaningful.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another action that reflects what matters beyond the present moment. Let your priorities show what you truly value.

p: Eternal values can guide ordinary decisions. When Christ is central, we can see more clearly what deserves our time.
In Matthew 6:19-21 we read: “Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal.”
Choose one thing today that will still matter tomorrow.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Matthew 6:19-21
Spend ten minutes on something that lasts, like prayer, scripture, or family.

pages.q: What we value most should have a place in how we spend our lives.

147.pq: If ye know these things, happy are ye if ye do them.

p: Knowing what is good is only the beginning.
Understanding becomes more meaningful when we are ready to act. Small acts of willing service can become part of our daily discipleship.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you recognize an opportunity to act before continuing.

pages.q: If ye know these things, happy are ye if ye do them.

pages.prompt: What will you do with a good thing you know today?

o.l: I will act on it now.
o.r: Acting now can prevent a good intention from being forgotten. If the next step is clear and possible, begin today.

o.l: I will prepare to act on it soon.
o.r: Some good actions need planning before they can happen. Make a clear plan and decide when you will take the next step.

o.l: I will help someone else act on it too.
o.r: You can strengthen another person by inviting them into a good action. Encourage them without controlling their decision.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to turn good knowledge into action. Let what you know influence something real in your day.

p: Good intentions are valuable, but action gives them direction. We can begin with what is possible now.
In James 2:17 we read: “Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.”
When you know one good thing to do, look for a way to do it.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in James 2:17
Do one thing today to serve, not just plan to serve.

pages.q: Truth becomes part of our lives when we are willing to act on it.

148.pq: Let love be without dissimulation. Abhor that which is evil; cleave to that which is good.

p: God invites us to be sincere in our love and our choices.
A sincere life does not require us to pretend to be perfect. It asks us to be honest about what we believe and genuinely seek what is good.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you live with greater sincerity before continuing.

pages.q: Let love be without dissimulation. Abhor that which is evil; cleave to that which is good.

pages.prompt: How will you choose greater sincerity today?

o.l: I will be genuine in my care for someone.
o.r: Genuine care listens and responds without pretending. Give one person your honest attention today.

o.l: I will admit when I do not know something.
o.r: Admitting what you do not know can be a sign of strength and honesty. It creates room for learning instead of pretending.

o.l: I will make my actions match my values.
o.r: Your values become clearer when they influence your choices. Identify one action today that can better reflect what you believe.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to live more sincerely. Let your words, motives, and actions move closer together.

p: Sincerity helps us build stronger relationships with God and others. We do not need to perform goodness for people.
In 1 Peter 1:22 we read: “Seeing ye have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit unto unfeigned love of the brethren, see that ye love one another with a pure heart fervently.”
Today, choose to be genuine in one important way.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 1 Peter 1:22
Be honest in one conversation today where you would normally pretend.

pages.q: A sincere life does not pretend to be perfect. It honestly seeks what is good.

149.pq: See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.

p: Time is given to us one day at a time.
We cannot do everything, but we can make wiser choices about what receives our attention.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you use your time wisely before continuing.

pages.q: See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.

pages.prompt: What will you do to use your time more wisely today?

o.l: I will begin with my most important task.
o.r: Beginning with what matters most can keep important responsibilities from being pushed aside. Identify your priority and give it focused attention.

o.l: I will reduce one unnecessary distraction.
o.r: A small distraction can take more time than we realize. Choose one thing you can limit so your attention can return to something important.

o.l: I will make time for someone I care about.
o.r: Relationships need more than good intentions. Give someone meaningful attention instead of waiting for a perfect opportunity.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another practical way to use your time with greater purpose. One thoughtful decision can change the direction of your day.

p: Using time wisely does not mean filling every moment with activity. It means giving proper attention to what matters.
In Psalm 90:12 we read: “So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.”
Ask God to help you see what deserves your time today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Psalm 90:12
Plan your time tonight for tomorrow. Put the most important thing first.

pages.q: Wise use of time begins with knowing what truly deserves our attention.

150.pq: The LORD is my strength and my shield; my heart trusted in him, and I am helped:

p: There are times when our own strength does not feel sufficient.
We can trust God and seek His help. His strength may help us continue, endure, or do what we could not do alone.
Take a moment to pray and ask God for the strength you need before continuing.

pages.q: The LORD is my strength and my shield; my heart trusted in him, and I am helped:

pages.prompt: Where will you seek the Lord's strength today?

o.l: I will ask for strength in a specific challenge.
o.r: Be specific about the challenge you face. Ask God to help you know what to do and give you strength for the next step.

o.l: I will remember that I do not have to do everything alone.
o.r: Recognizing your need for help is not weakness. Turn to God and also accept appropriate support from trustworthy people.

o.l: I will keep going with God's help.
o.r: You may still need to take difficult steps after praying. Move forward with the confidence that God can strengthen you as you act.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to rely more fully on the Lord today. Bring your real needs to Him and trust that He hears you.

p: God's help does not always remove the challenge immediately. Often, He gives us strength to meet it.
In Psalm 18:2 we read: “The LORD is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer.”
Whatever you face today, you can ask the Lord for help.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Psalm 18:2
Write where you need strength. Ask God for it in prayer.

pages.q: We may face difficult things, but we do not have to seek strength alone.

151.pq: Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.

p: People sometimes need more than our judgment. They need understanding, patience, and a fair opportunity to grow.
Mercy does not remove truth or accountability. It changes how we respond to the weaknesses and failures of others.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you become more merciful before continuing.

pages.q: Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.

pages.prompt: How will you show greater mercy today?

o.l: I will give someone another opportunity.
o.r: Another opportunity can allow a person to learn and improve. Offer it wisely and without ignoring what still needs to change.

o.l: I will respond with more understanding.
o.r: Understanding begins by listening before deciding. Try to see the situation more fully before choosing your response.

o.l: I will be less harsh toward a weakness.
o.r: You can recognize a weakness without making it the whole definition of a person. Leave room for growth in yourself and others.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to show mercy without abandoning truth. Ask God to help you respond with both wisdom and compassion.

p: We all need mercy at different times in our lives. As we receive it from God, we can learn to extend it more freely.
In Luke 6:35-36 we read: “But love ye your enemies, and do good, and lend, hoping for nothing again.”
Look for one opportunity today to make your response more merciful.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
