a: Study related verses in Luke 6:35-36
Show mercy once today to someone who has made a mistake.

pages.q: Mercy leaves room for people to learn, change, and grow.

152.pq: He that walketh with wise men shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed.

p: The people around us can influence how we think and live.
Good relationships can encourage growth, honesty, and better decisions.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you choose wise influences before continuing.

pages.q: He that walketh with wise men shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed.

pages.prompt: How will you choose better influences in your life?

o.l: I will spend time with someone who helps me grow.
o.r: Choose someone whose example encourages good decisions. Pay attention to what you can learn from the way they live.

o.l: I will reduce an influence that leads me in a wrong direction.
o.r: Some influences gradually weaken our best desires. Consider one relationship or influence that may need healthier boundaries.

o.l: I will become a better influence myself.
o.r: You also influence the people around you. Choose one behavior today that can encourage someone else toward what is good.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to surround yourself with influences that strengthen your life. Ask God for wisdom in the relationships you develop.

p: Choosing good influences does not mean believing you are better than others. It means being honest about what shapes your choices.
In 1 Corinthians 15:33 we read: “Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.”
Today, move closer to an influence that helps you become better.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 1 Corinthians 15:33
Think about who you spend time with. Spend time today with someone who lifts you.

pages.q: The people and influences around us can shape the direction we choose.

153.theme: Opening Your Heart to God's Word
153.pq: And I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within you; and I will take the stony heart out of their flesh…

p: Sometimes disappointment or pain can make us want to close our hearts.
God can help us become open again. He can soften what has become hard and help us respond with greater willingness.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to soften your heart before continuing.

pages.q: And I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within you; and I will take the stony heart out of their flesh, and will give them an heart of flesh:

pages.prompt: What will you do to become more open to God's influence?

o.l: I will be honest with God about what has hurt me.
o.r: God already knows what you carry, but honest prayer can help you bring it to Him. Tell Him what has made it difficult to remain open.

o.l: I will let go of one resentment.
o.r: Resentment can keep an old hurt active within us. Ask God to help you begin releasing one part of what you have been holding.

o.l: I will become more willing to change.
o.r: Change can feel uncomfortable, even when it is good. Choose one area where you are willing to let God teach you something new.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another step that opens your heart more fully to God. Trust Him to help you change at a pace that leads to real growth.

p: A softened heart can receive truth in ways a closed heart cannot. God can help us become willing again.

In Alma 32:27-28 we read: “But behold, if ye will awake and arouse your faculties, even to an experiment upon my words, and exercise a particle of faith, yea, even if ye can no more than desire to believe.”
Today, give Him permission to teach and change you.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Alma 32:27-28
Read one verse slowly today. Ask what it wants you to change.

pages.q: God can soften what life has made hard and help us become willing again.

154.pq: Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name.

p: Some days are easy to appreciate, while others are not.
Giving thanks in every circumstance does not mean being grateful for every painful thing. It means we can still look for God's goodness even during difficulty.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you recognize something good before continuing.

pages.q: Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name.

pages.prompt: What will you do to notice goodness in a difficult day?

o.l: I will name one good thing that is still present.
o.r: Even on a difficult day, one good thing may still be present. Notice it clearly and allow yourself to appreciate it.

o.l: I will thank someone who has helped me.
o.r: Another person's kindness may be easier to notice when life feels difficult. Tell them specifically how their help has mattered.

o.l: I will remember that difficult moments do not last forever.
o.r: A hard moment can feel larger when you believe it will never change. Remember that circumstances can shift and that God can help you continue.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another honest way to notice goodness without denying what is difficult. Let gratitude and reality exist together.

p: Gratitude can remain present even when life is not easy. It helps us notice blessings that difficulty might otherwise hide.
In 1 Chronicles 16:34 we read: “O give thanks unto the LORD; for he is good; for his mercy endureth for ever.”
Look for one good thing today and thank God for it.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 1 Chronicles 16:34
Say thank you to God before you eat, before you sleep, and when you wake.

pages.q: Even on difficult days, we can still look for something good.

155.theme: Being Willing to Learn from Others
155.pq: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes: but he that hearkeneth unto counsel is wise.

p: We all have limits to what we can see and understand by ourselves.
Wise counsel can help us recognize mistakes, consider new possibilities, and make better decisions.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you recognize good counsel before continuing.

pages.q: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes: but he that hearkeneth unto counsel is wise.

pages.prompt: How will you become more willing to receive wise counsel?

o.l: I will listen without becoming defensive.
o.r: Listening does not require you to agree with every word immediately. Give good counsel time and consider it honestly.

o.l: I will ask someone trustworthy for advice.
o.r: Choose someone with wisdom, honesty, and good character. Explain your situation clearly and listen carefully to their perspective.

o.l: I will consider feedback before rejecting it.
o.r: Initial discomfort does not always mean feedback is wrong. Look for any truth that may help you improve.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to become more open to wise counsel. Ask God to help you recognize truth even when it comes through correction.

p: Receiving counsel does not remove personal responsibility. We still need to seek God and make our own choices.
In Proverbs 19:20 we read: “Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.”
A wise person remains willing to learn.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Proverbs 19:20
Ask someone you respect for advice on a choice you are making.

pages.q: Wisdom grows when we remain willing to learn from good counsel.

156.pq: Let us not be desirous of vain glory, provoking one another, envying one another.

p: It is easy to compare our lives with the lives of other people.
Envy can make us overlook our own blessings and turn another person's success into a reason for unhappiness.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you find freedom from unhealthy comparison before continuing.

pages.q: Let us not be desirous of vain glory, provoking one another, envying one another.

pages.prompt: What will you do when comparison begins to affect your heart?

o.l: I will remember one blessing in my own life.
o.r: Your life contains gifts that comparison can make easy to overlook. Take time to notice something good that is already yours.

o.l: I will be happy for another person's success.
o.r: Another person's blessing does not remove the possibility of good in your own life. Practice celebrating something good that has happened for them.

o.l: I will focus on my own next step.
o.r: Your path does not need to match another person's path. Ask what you can do today to move forward from where you are.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to leave unhealthy comparison behind. Ask God to help you see your own life with greater gratitude and clarity.

p: Comparison can distract us from the work God has given us personally. We can celebrate others without losing sight of our own path.
In James 3:16 we read: “For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.”
Today, focus on the good you can do with the life you have.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in James 3:16
When you feel envy today, say one kind thing about the person instead.

pages.q: Another person's success does not reduce the value of your own path.

157.pq: Wherefore lay apart all filthiness and superfluity of naughtiness, and receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.

p: God's word can correct us, comfort us, and guide us.
Receiving it with meekness means allowing truth to teach us instead of only looking for messages that confirm what we already think.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you receive His word with a willing heart before continuing.

pages.q: Wherefore lay apart all filthiness and superfluity of naughtiness, and receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.

pages.prompt: How will you receive God's word more openly today?

o.l: I will look for one truth I need to apply.
o.r: A scripture can become personal when you ask what it invites you to do. Choose one truth and consider a real way to live it.

o.l: I will let scripture correct me.
o.r: Correction can be uncomfortable, but it can also lead to growth. Ask yourself whether there is something you need to change.

o.l: I will read without rushing.
o.r: Slower reading can give you time to think and listen. Stay with one meaningful verse long enough to consider its message.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to receive God's word with greater willingness. Come to scripture ready to learn, not only to finish a task.

p: God's word can bless us most deeply when we allow it to influence our lives. A willing heart creates room for change.
In Psalm 119:11 we read: “Thy word have I hid in mine heart, that I might not sin against thee.”
Read one truth today and ask what it means for you.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Psalm 119:11
Read your scriptures today with a quiet, willing heart. Take your time.

pages.q: A willing heart allows truth to teach, correct, and guide.

158.theme: Living by Every Word of God
158.pq: But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.

p: Our bodies need physical nourishment, and our spirits also need regular nourishment.
God's word can guide us, strengthen us, and help us remember what matters.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to nourish your spirit through His word before continuing.

pages.q: But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.

pages.prompt: How will you give your spirit greater nourishment today?

o.l: I will read one passage of scripture.
o.r: You do not need to read a large amount to receive something meaningful. Read attentively and notice one truth that stands out.

o.l: I will memorize one short verse.
o.r: A memorized verse can remain with you when you need guidance later. Choose a verse and repeat it until you can remember its message.

o.l: I will think about a scripture during my day.
o.r: Returning to a scripture in your thoughts can help its meaning become clearer. Consider how its message connects with a real situation you face.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to make God's word part of your day. Give your spirit regular attention just as you care for your physical needs.

p: Spiritual strength grows through regular nourishment. God's word can remain with us and guide our decisions.
In Deuteronomy 8:3 we read: “And he humbled thee, and suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna, which thou knewest not, neither did thy fathers know.”
Give your spirit something good to receive today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Deuteronomy 8:3
Read one verse and write what it asks you to do. Do it today.

pages.q: Our spirits need regular nourishment as surely as our bodies do.

159.theme: Doing Things in the Right Spirit
159.pq: Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God.

p: The same action can be done with very different motives.
When we remember that our lives are accountable to God, ordinary responsibilities can be approached with greater sincerity and care.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you act with the right motives before continuing.

pages.q: Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God.

pages.prompt: How will you approach your responsibilities with greater sincerity today?

o.l: I will give my best effort to one task.
o.r: Your best effort does not require perfection. It means giving honest attention to what you have been asked to do.

o.l: I will improve my attitude toward a responsibility.
o.r: Some responsibilities may still be difficult, but you can choose how you approach them. Ask God to help you work with greater willingness.

o.l: I will do what is right even without praise.
o.r: Praise can be encouraging, but it does not need to be your reason for doing good. Let your character guide you when no recognition comes.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to bring sincerity to what you do today. Let your motives become as important as your actions.

p: God sees more than the visible result of our work. He also knows the effort and desires behind it.
In Colossians 3:17 we read: “And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.”
Today, do one ordinary thing with greater sincerity.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Colossians 3:17
Do one ordinary task today with a prayer in your heart.

pages.q: Sincerity changes the way we approach even ordinary responsibilities.

160.theme: Learning to Be Still Before God
160.pq: Rest in the LORD, and wait patiently for him.

p: Life can fill our minds with noise, pressure, and constant activity.
Stillness can help us remember who God is and create space to recognize what matters most.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you become still before continuing.

pages.q: Rest in the LORD, and wait patiently for him.

pages.prompt: How will you create a moment of stillness with God today?

o.l: I will sit quietly for a few minutes.
o.r: Set aside a short time without distractions. You do not need to force an experience. Simply turn your attention toward God.

o.l: I will pause before making an important decision.
o.r: A pause can give you time to seek wisdom instead of reacting quickly. Bring the decision to God before moving forward.

o.l: I will take a break from unnecessary noise.
o.r: Constant sound and activity can make reflection difficult. Choose one source of noise you can set aside for a little while.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another simple way to become still before God. Give yourself enough quiet to remember that you do not have to carry every thought alone.

p: Stillness is not emptiness. It can become a time to remember God's presence and listen with greater attention.
In Doctrine and Covenants 101:16 we read: “Therefore, let your hearts be comforted concerning Zion.”
Take one quiet moment today and turn your heart toward Him.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 101:16
Take five minutes of stillness. Put your worries down in prayer.

pages.q: A quiet moment can help us remember who God is and where to turn.

161.pq: I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.

p: Progress often requires us to keep moving even when the journey feels long.
We can remember our purpose and continue toward Jesus Christ one decision at a time.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you move forward with purpose before continuing.

pages.q: I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.

pages.prompt: How will you keep moving forward today?

o.l: I will take the next right step.
o.r: You may not need to see the entire path today. Focus on the next good decision that is already within your reach.

o.l: I will remember why my goal matters.
o.r: Remembering your purpose can strengthen you when motivation becomes weak. Think about the good result you hope to achieve through faithful effort.

o.l: I will continue after a difficult moment.
o.r: A difficult moment does not have to end your progress. Pause, learn what you can, and continue with renewed effort.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another meaningful action that helps you continue forward. Ask God to help you keep your life directed toward what matters most.

p: Progress is often made through ordinary decisions repeated over time. You do not need to complete everything today.
In 2 Nephi 31:20 we read: “Wherefore, ye must press forward with a steadfastness in Christ, having a perfect brightness of hope, and a love of God and of all men.”
Keep moving toward Jesus Christ with purpose.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 2 Nephi 31:20
Write one goal you are moving toward. Take one step today.

pages.q: You do not need to see the whole path to take the next right step.

162.pq: Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.

p: Some burdens become heavier when people carry them alone.
We may not be able to solve another person's problems, but we can offer support, time, and understanding.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to show you whose burden you may help carry before continuing.

pages.q: Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.

pages.prompt: How can you help carry someone's burden today?

o.l: I will listen to someone who needs to talk.
o.r: Listening can be a meaningful form of support. Give the person your attention without quickly trying to solve everything for them.

o.l: I will help with something practical.
o.r: A practical action can reduce a real burden. Look for one specific need you can help meet today.

o.l: I will stay connected to someone who is struggling.
o.r: Support can matter after the first conversation ends. Check in again and let the person know they have not been forgotten.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another thoughtful way to support someone. Ask God to help you offer help that is both sincere and useful.

p: We are not expected to carry every burden alone. God can work through people who are willing to help one another.
In Romans 15:1 we read: “We then that are strong ought to bear the infirmities of the weak, and not to please ourselves.”
Today, look for one person who may need support.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Romans 15:1
Ask someone how you can help carry their load. Offer one concrete thing.

pages.q: A burden may become lighter when someone chooses to help carry it.

163.pq: But speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ:

p: Truth and love do not need to oppose each other.
We can be honest without being cruel. We can address difficult matters while still respecting the person before us.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you speak truth with love before continuing.

pages.q: But speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ:

pages.prompt: How will you communicate a difficult truth with greater care?

o.l: I will speak respectfully.
o.r: Respect affects how truth is received. Choose words that address the issue without attacking the person.

o.l: I will listen as well as speak.
o.r: A difficult conversation should include room for understanding. Listen carefully to what the other person sees and feels.

o.l: I will check my motive before I speak.
o.r: Ask yourself whether you want to help, correct, or simply win. A sincere desire for another person's good can guide your words.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to communicate with both honesty and care. Let Christ influence not only what you say but how you say it.

p: Truth spoken without love can unnecessarily wound. Love without honesty can leave important things unsaid.
In Proverbs 27:5-6 we read: “Open rebuke is better than secret love.”
Ask God to help you hold both truth and love together.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Proverbs 27:5-6
Say one honest thing today with kindness. Choose your timing with care.

pages.q: Truth and love can work together when our purpose is to help.

164.pq: I will remember the works of the LORD: surely I will remember thy wonders of old.

p: When the present feels uncertain, we can remember what God has already done.
Remembering His works can strengthen our confidence and help us recognize His hand across time.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you remember His works before continuing.

pages.q: I will remember the works of the LORD: surely I will remember thy wonders of old.

pages.prompt: What will you remember about God's work today?

o.l: I will remember an answer to a past prayer.
o.r: Think about a time when you received help, direction, or strength after seeking God. Let that memory strengthen your trust today.

o.l: I will remember a scripture story that gives me strength.
o.r: Scripture preserves examples of God's power and faithfulness. Choose one story and consider what it teaches you now.

o.l: I will record something God has done for me.
o.r: Writing down a spiritual experience can help you remember it later. Record it simply and honestly while the details are still clear.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to remember God's works. Let the past help you recognize reasons to continue trusting Him.

p: Memory can strengthen faith when we remember God's help with honesty. What He has done before can give us courage for the present.
In Alma 5:6 we read: “And now behold, I say unto you, my brethren, you that belong to this church, have you sufficiently retained in remembrance the captivity of your fathers?”
Take time today to remember one work of the Lord.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Alma 5:6
Write three ways the Lord has helped you in the past. Thank Him.

pages.q: Remembering God's past help can strengthen us in the present.

165.pq: Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.

p: What we repeatedly welcome into our hearts can influence our choices.
We can be careful about the desires, messages, and habits we allow to shape us.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you guard your heart before continuing.

pages.q: Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.

pages.prompt: What will you do to protect what is growing in your heart?

o.l: I will reduce one harmful influence.
o.r: A harmful influence may become easier to remove when you identify it clearly. Take one practical step to limit its place in your life.

o.l: I will make room for something uplifting.
o.r: Removing something unhelpful creates an opportunity for something better. Choose an influence that strengthens your mind and desires.

o.l: I will examine what I desire most.
o.r: Your strongest desires can influence many of your decisions. Ask God to help you recognize any desire that needs to change.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another wise action that protects your heart. Let what you allow into your life support the person you are becoming.

p: Guarding your heart is an active choice. It requires attention to what is shaping your desires.
In Alma 37:36 we read: “Yea, and cry unto God for all thy support; yea, let all thy doings be unto the Lord, and whithersoever thou goest let it be in the Lord.”
Choose one influence today that will help your heart move toward God.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Alma 37:36
Notice what you let into your heart today. Guard against one thing.

pages.q: What we allow to shape our hearts can influence the direction of our lives.

166.pq: And beside this, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue.

p: God invites us to give sincere effort rather than living only for approval.
We can raise our standards by remembering who we want to become and why our choices matter.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you reach for higher things before continuing.

pages.q: And beside this, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue.

pages.prompt: Where will you choose a higher standard today?

o.l: I will give greater care to my responsibilities.
o.r: Greater care can be shown through focused effort and attention to detail. Choose one responsibility and do it more thoughtfully.

o.l: I will choose what is right over what is easy.
o.r: The easier choice is not always the better choice. Ask what reflects your values and take that direction.

o.l: I will improve one area of my life.
o.r: Real improvement often begins with one clear area. Choose something specific and take a practical step toward becoming better.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to raise your personal standard. Let your effort reflect your desire to become more like Jesus Christ.

p: Higher standards are not about comparing yourself with other people. They are about becoming more willing to live according to what is good.
In Ecclesiastes 9:10 we read: “Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might.”
Choose one area today where you will give your best.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Ecclesiastes 9:10
Pick one thing you want to improve. Practice it for fifteen minutes.

pages.q: A higher standard begins with the choice to give greater care to what matters.

167.pq: He is in the way of life that keepeth instruction: but he that refuseth reproof erreth.

p: Correction can be difficult because it may show us something we did not want to see.
When correction is true and helpful, we can receive it as an opportunity to grow rather than only as a reason to feel discouraged.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you receive helpful correction before continuing.

pages.q: He is in the way of life that keepeth instruction: but he that refuseth reproof erreth.

pages.prompt: How will you respond when you receive needed correction?

o.l: I will listen carefully.
o.r: Listening carefully can help you understand what the other person is actually saying. Resist the desire to prepare your defense before you have fully heard them.

o.l: I will look for what I can improve.
o.r: Not every part of a correction may be equally helpful, but there may still be something you can learn. Look honestly for one area where growth is possible.

o.l: I will avoid making excuses.
o.r: Excuses can prevent us from facing what needs to change. Take responsibility for your part and focus on what you can do differently.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another mature response to helpful correction. Ask God to help you value growth more than the comfort of always appearing right.

p: Correction can help us see what we cannot always see ourselves. A willing response can turn a difficult moment into growth.
In Proverbs 15:31-32 we read: “The ear that heareth the reproof of life abideth among the wise.”
Today, let truth teach you even when it is uncomfortable.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Proverbs 15:31-32
Accept one correction today without arguing. Say thank you.

pages.q: Helpful correction can become a gift when we are willing to learn from it.

168.pq: A merry heart doeth good like a medicine: but a broken spirit drieth the bones.

p: Joy can be strengthened by the way we choose to see and live each day.
A joyful heart does not deny real problems. It makes room for goodness, gratitude, and hope even while facing them.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you recognize wholesome joy before continuing.

pages.q: A merry heart doeth good like a medicine: but a broken spirit drieth the bones.

pages.prompt: What will help you make room for wholesome joy today?

o.l: I will notice something good around me.
o.r: Good things can be easy to miss when your mind is focused only on problems. Pause and deliberately notice one thing that brings genuine joy.

o.l: I will spend time with someone who lifts me.
o.r: A good conversation can bring encouragement and perspective. Choose time with someone whose presence helps you become better.

o.l: I will do something wholesome that I enjoy.
o.r: Rest and wholesome enjoyment can be part of a balanced life. Choose an activity that refreshes you without pulling you away from what matters.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another wholesome way to make room for joy. Let yourself receive the good gifts that God places in your life.

p: Joy is not the same as pretending that everything is easy. It can grow as we notice goodness and choose what gives life meaning.
In 2 Nephi 2:25 we read: “Adam fell that men might be; and men are, that they might have joy.”
Allow yourself to receive one good thing today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 2 Nephi 2:25
Do one thing today that brings you real joy and keeps you close to God.

pages.q: Joy can make room for goodness without denying that life can also be difficult.

169.pq: Without counsel purposes are disappointed: but in the multitude of counsellors they are established.

p: Important decisions can sometimes benefit from more than one perspective.
Seeking wise counsel does not remove our responsibility to pray and choose. It can help us see what we might otherwise miss.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to guide you toward wise counsel before continuing.

pages.q: Without counsel purposes are disappointed: but in the multitude of counsellors they are established.

pages.prompt: How will you seek greater wisdom for an important decision?

o.l: I will pray before deciding.
o.r: Prayer can help you place your decision before God. Ask for wisdom and remain willing to consider an answer that differs from your first preference.

o.l: I will seek a wise perspective.
o.r: Choose someone whose character and judgment you respect. Listen to understand their perspective, not simply to hear agreement.

o.l: I will take time before making a choice.
o.r: Not every decision should be rushed. When time allows, give yourself space to consider the consequences and available options.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another wise step before making your decision. Ask God to help you combine careful thought with spiritual guidance.

p: Wise decisions often involve humility, prayer, and careful thought. We do not need to pretend that every answer must come from us alone.
In Doctrine and Covenants 9:7-8 we read: “Behold, you have not understood; you have supposed that I would give it unto you, when you took no thought save it was to ask me.”
Seek the help you need, then move forward responsibly.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 9:7-8
Seek counsel on one decision from someone wise and trusted.

pages.q: Wise counsel can help us see what we may have missed on our own.

170.pq: In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.

p: We often want clear direction for every part of our lives.
God can guide us as we remember Him in our decisions and invite His influence into more than only our moments of crisis.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to direct your path before continuing.

pages.q: In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.

pages.prompt: How will you invite God into your decisions today?

o.l: I will pray about a specific choice.
o.r: Bring one real decision to God. Explain what you understand, ask for wisdom, and remain willing to act on righteous guidance.

o.l: I will pause and ask what matters most.
o.r: A short pause can help you see beyond immediate pressure. Consider which choice best aligns with the truths you value.

o.l: I will follow guidance I have already received.
o.r: Sometimes we seek new direction while ignoring what God has already made clear. Review what you already know and take the next faithful step.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to acknowledge God in your life today. Let Him become part of your thinking before as well as after you make decisions.

p: God's guidance may come step by step rather than all at once. We can continue seeking Him while faithfully moving forward.
In Psalm 32:8 we read: “I will instruct thee and teach thee in the way which thou shalt go.”
Invite Him into one decision today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Psalm 32:8
Pray about one decision today. Then act on the first right thought.

pages.q: We can invite God into our decisions before uncertainty becomes a crisis.

171.pq: Give unto the LORD the glory due unto his name; worship the LORD in the beauty of holiness.

p: Holiness can shape the way we approach God.
When we treat sacred things with care, our hearts can become more prepared to recognize the Lord's presence.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you recognize the beauty of holiness before continuing.

pages.q: Give unto the LORD the glory due unto his name; worship the LORD in the beauty of holiness.

pages.prompt: How will you show greater respect for something sacred today?

o.l: I will prepare my heart before worship.
o.r: Preparation can begin with a quiet prayer and a willing mind. Set aside distractions and remember why you have come to worship.

o.l: I will treat sacred things with greater care.
o.r: Respect can be shown in simple actions. Consider how you speak, listen, and behave around things that are holy.

o.l: I will create a more reverent moment in my day.
o.r: You can create a short period of focused attention on God. Turn away from unnecessary distractions and give Him your full heart for a moment.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to show respect for what is sacred. Let your actions reflect the value you place on your relationship with God.

p: Reverence is more than outward behavior. It begins with the value we place on God and sacred things.
In Psalm 96:9 we read: “O worship the LORD in the beauty of holiness: fear before him, all the earth.”
Today, approach one sacred moment with greater care.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Psalm 96:9
Take a moment to notice something beautiful today. Thank God for it.

pages.q: Reverence begins with recognizing that some things deserve our deepest care.

172.pq: And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.

p: A clear conscience can help us live with greater peace and honesty.
When we recognize that something needs to be corrected, we can respond instead of repeatedly ignoring what we know.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you listen to a righteous conscience before continuing.

pages.q: And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.

pages.prompt: What will you do when your conscience shows you something needs to change?

o.l: I will correct what I can.
o.r: Some mistakes can be repaired through a clear and honest action. Consider what responsibility is yours and take the next appropriate step.

o.l: I will apologize when I have caused harm.
o.r: An apology can acknowledge another person's pain and accept responsibility. Be sincere without adding excuses that weaken your words.

o.l: I will stop doing what I know is wrong.
o.r: A clear conscience requires more than recognizing a problem. Choose a practical change that helps you leave the wrong action behind.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another honest response to what your conscience is showing you. Ask God for courage to make needed changes.

p: A clear conscience grows as our actions become more honest and responsible. When correction is needed, we can face it with faith.
In Romans 2:15 we read: “Which shew the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts the mean while accusing or else excusing one another.”
Do not ignore a good prompting to make something right.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Romans 2:15
Notice your conscience once today and follow it right away.

pages.q: A clear conscience is strengthened when we respond to what we know needs to change.

173.pq: Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee.

p: Peace is not always the absence of problems.
The peace of Jesus Christ can remain with us even while we face uncertainty, questions, or difficult circumstances.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you receive His peace before continuing.

pages.q: Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee.

pages.prompt: How will you make more room for the peace of Christ today?

o.l: I will bring my worries to God in prayer.
o.r: You do not need to hide your worries from God. Name them honestly and ask for the peace and guidance you need.

o.l: I will reduce one source of unnecessary anxiety.
o.r: Some pressure cannot be avoided, but some can be limited. Identify one influence or habit that increases worry without helping you.

o.l: I will focus on what I can do today.
o.r: Thinking about every possible problem can overwhelm the present moment. Identify one useful action you can take now.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to turn toward the peace of Christ. Give your heart space to receive help rather than carrying every concern alone.

p: Christ's peace may not answer every question immediately. It can still strengthen us while we continue through uncertainty.
In Psalm 29:11 we read: “The LORD will give strength unto his people; the LORD will bless his people with peace.”
Bring one concern to Him today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Psalm 29:11
Say a short prayer for peace. Write what you feel afterward.

pages.q: The peace of Christ can strengthen us even before every problem is resolved.

174.pq: Serve him with a perfect heart and with a willing mind.

p: Some responsibilities are easier to accept than others.
A willing mind can change how we approach the work before us, especially when we remember that faithful effort can be an offering to God.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you serve with a willing mind before continuing.

pages.q: Serve him with a perfect heart and with a willing mind.

pages.prompt: How will you approach an unwanted responsibility today?

o.l: I will begin without delaying.
o.r: Beginning can be the hardest part of an unwanted task. Start with one small part instead of waiting until you feel completely ready.

o.l: I will change my attitude toward the task.
o.r: You may not enjoy every responsibility, but you can choose greater willingness. Consider one good purpose that can come from completing it.

o.l: I will do it carefully.
o.r: Careful effort shows respect for the responsibility you have been given. Give attention to doing what is needed rather than simply finishing quickly.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another positive way to approach the responsibility. Ask God to help you bring willingness to what is before you.

p: Willingness does not mean every task becomes easy. It means we choose how to respond to the work that must be done.

In Mosiah 2:20-21 we read: “I say unto you, my brethren, that if you should render all the thanks and praise which your whole soul has power to possess, to that God who has created you, and has kept and preserved you.”
Today, begin one responsibility with a better heart.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Mosiah 2:20-21
Offer to help with a task you would normally skip. Do it gladly.

pages.q: A willing mind can change the way we approach even a difficult responsibility.

175.pq: For all the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen, unto the glory of God by us.

p: God's promises give us reasons to continue when we cannot yet see the full result.
Trust grows as we learn who God is and remember that His faithfulness does not depend on changing circumstances.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you trust His promises before continuing.

pages.q: For all the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen, unto the glory of God by us.

pages.prompt: How will you strengthen your trust in God's promises today?

o.l: I will study one promise God has given.
o.r: Choose a promise found in scripture and read it carefully. Consider what it teaches about God's character and His relationship with His children.

o.l: I will remember how God has been faithful before.
o.r: Past experiences can strengthen present trust. Think about a time when you received help or strength to continue.

o.l: I will remain faithful while I wait.
o.r: Trust often requires continued faithfulness before we see the result we hope for. Keep doing the good you know while placing the outcome in God's hands.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to strengthen your confidence in God. Let His promises become a reason to continue with hope.

p: Trust in God's promises does not require us to know every detail of the future. It invites us to know and rely on Him.
In Moroni 10:32 we read: “Yea, come unto Christ, and be perfected in him, and deny yourselves of all ungodliness.”
Hold to one promise today and let it strengthen your heart.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Moroni 10:32
Write a promise God has kept for you. Hold onto it today.

pages.q: God's promises can give us strength to continue before we see the full result.

176.pq: Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.

p: Sometimes the changes we need are deeper than our outward actions.
God can help us examine our desires and become more willing to choose what is right.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help renew your heart before continuing.

pages.q: Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.

pages.prompt: What part of your heart would you like God to help you change?

o.l: I will ask God to help me change one wrong desire.
o.r: Be honest about the desire you want to change. Ask God to help you replace it with a desire that leads you toward what is good.

o.l: I will examine the reason behind my choices.
o.r: Our actions often begin with what we want most. Take time to consider whether your motives are leading you in a good direction.

o.l: I will make one change that reflects a better heart.
o.r: Inner change can become visible through real choices. Choose one action today that reflects the person you want to become.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another sincere way to seek a better heart. Ask God to help you become more willing to receive the change He can bring.

p: God can help us change from within. We do not have to remain controlled by old desires and patterns.
In Ezekiel 36:26 we read: “A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you.”
Bring your heart honestly to Him today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Ezekiel 36:26
Pray today for a softer heart. Ask what you could change.

pages.q: God can help change not only what we do, but also what we desire.

177.pq: But godliness with contentment is great gain.

p: It is easy to focus on what we still want and overlook what we already have.
Contentment can help us appreciate God's blessings without losing the desire to grow and improve.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you recognize what is already enough before continuing.

pages.q: But godliness with contentment is great gain.

pages.prompt: How will you practice greater contentment today?

o.l: I will appreciate something I already have.
o.r: Pause and notice one blessing you may have begun to treat as ordinary. Gratitude can help you see its value again.

o.l: I will stop comparing myself with someone else.
o.r: Another person's life does not determine the worth of your own. Turn your attention toward your responsibilities, blessings, and opportunities.

o.l: I will be grateful while still working toward my goals.
o.r: Contentment does not mean giving up on growth. You can work faithfully for improvement while appreciating where God has already brought you.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to appreciate the good already present in your life. Let gratitude reduce the power of unnecessary comparison.

p: Contentment helps us live more fully in the present. It allows us to work toward tomorrow without despising today.
In Hebrews 13:5 we read: “Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have.”
Notice one thing you already have reason to appreciate.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Hebrews 13:5
Write what you have enough of. Thank God for it.

pages.q: Contentment helps us appreciate today while still preparing for tomorrow.

178.pq: Therefore if thou bring thy gift to the altar, and there rememberest that thy brother hath ought against thee;

p: Broken relationships can sometimes remain unresolved because taking the first step feels difficult.
When it is safe and appropriate, we can seek peace by addressing hurt honestly and with humility.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you know whether you should take a step toward reconciliation before continuing.

pages.q: Therefore if thou bring thy gift to the altar, and there rememberest that thy brother hath ought against thee;

pages.prompt: What step could help repair a relationship?

o.l: I will acknowledge my part in the problem.
o.r: You may not be responsible for everything that happened, but you can honestly examine your own actions. Taking responsibility for your part can be a meaningful beginning.

o.l: I will reach out with respect.
o.r: A simple and respectful message can open a door. Speak honestly without demanding that the other person respond in a particular way.

o.l: I will seek peace without forcing the outcome.
o.r: You can choose to act rightly even when you cannot control another person's response. Do your part with sincerity and leave room for time and healing.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another appropriate step toward greater peace. Ask God for wisdom, especially when the situation is complicated.

p: Reconciliation may take time and may not always happen in the way we hope. Still, we can examine whether there is a righteous step we should take.
In Matthew 5:24 we read: “Leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way.”
Ask God to help you become a person who seeks peace.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Matthew 5:24
Reach out to someone you have a quarrel with. Say a kind word first.

pages.q: Seeking peace begins with a willingness to examine what we can do.

179.pq: And Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him.

p: A relationship with God can become part of our daily life.
Walking with Him means remembering Him not only during major decisions, but also through ordinary moments and choices.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you walk with Him today before continuing.

pages.q: And Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him.

pages.prompt: How will you remember God during your ordinary day?

o.l: I will pause briefly and turn my thoughts to God.
o.r: A short moment of prayer or reflection can redirect your heart. You do not need to wait for a crisis before turning to God.

o.l: I will include God in one decision.
o.r: Bring one real choice before God today. Ask what course of action would help you live according to His will.

o.l: I will remember God while doing my daily work.
o.r: Ordinary responsibilities can still be part of a faithful life. Let your honesty, effort, and treatment of others reflect your relationship with Him.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another simple way to remember God throughout the day. Small moments of awareness can strengthen your relationship with Him.

p: Walking with God is not limited to one place or one hour. It can become part of how we live.
In Micah 6:8 we read: “He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?”
Invite Him into an ordinary part of your day today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Micah 6:8
Take a ten-minute walk and talk with God while you walk.

pages.q: A daily walk with God can begin in the ordinary moments of life.

180.pq: A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.

p: The way we respond can influence what happens next.
A gentle answer does not mean agreeing with everything. It means choosing words that do not unnecessarily increase anger.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you respond with greater calm before continuing.

pages.q: A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.

pages.prompt: How will you respond when someone speaks to you with anger?

o.l: I will pause before answering.
o.r: A short pause can keep anger from controlling your response. Give yourself time to choose words instead of reacting immediately.

o.l: I will lower my voice and speak calmly.
o.r: Calm speech can prevent a disagreement from becoming worse. Focus on communicating clearly rather than trying to overpower the other person.

o.l: I will address the issue without attacking the person.
o.r: You can disagree with an action or idea without insulting someone. Keep your words focused on the matter that needs to be discussed.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another peaceful response that does not add unnecessary anger. Ask God to help you remain in control of your words.

p: We cannot control every conversation, but we can choose our own response. A gentle answer can create space for greater understanding.
In Proverbs 29:11 we read: “A fool uttereth all his mind: but a wise man keepeth it in till afterwards.”
Choose calm words when tension rises today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Proverbs 29:11
Answer one hard moment today with a soft voice.

pages.q: A calm response can prevent anger from deciding what we say next.

181.pq: And thy Father which seeth in secret himself shall reward thee openly.

p: Not every good action will be noticed by other people.
We can still choose what is right when no recognition is expected because God sees the sincerity behind our actions.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you value goodness even when it remains unseen before continuing.

pages.q: And thy Father which seeth in secret himself shall reward thee openly.

pages.prompt: What good can you do today without seeking recognition?

o.l: I will help someone quietly.
o.r: Look for a need and meet it without drawing attention to yourself. Let the person's well-being matter more than receiving credit.

o.l: I will do the right thing when no one is watching.
o.r: Private choices reveal much about our character. Choose honesty even when you believe nobody else will know.

o.l: I will stop needing praise for one good action.
o.r: It is natural to appreciate encouragement, but approval does not have to be the reason for doing good. Let your values guide your actions.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another act of goodness that does not require attention. Trust that God sees the intentions and choices that others may never notice.

p: Some of the most meaningful choices we make may remain known only to God. Their value does not become smaller because they are unseen.
In Matthew 6:6 we read: “But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret.”
Do one good thing today simply because it is right.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Matthew 6:6
Do one good deed today that no one will ever know about.

pages.q: Goodness does not lose its value because no one else sees it.

182.pq: Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong.

p: Difficult situations can test what we truly believe and value.
Standing firm does not mean never feeling afraid. It means choosing not to abandon what is right because a moment has become difficult.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to strengthen you before continuing.

pages.q: Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong.

pages.prompt: Where do you need greater firmness today?

o.l: I will remain true to what I know is right.
o.r: Pressure from others can make a good choice feel difficult. Remember your values and let them guide your decision.

o.l: I will not give up because progress is slow.
o.r: Slow progress is still progress when you continue moving in the right direction. Keep taking the next faithful step.

o.l: I will ask God for strength before facing a challenge.
o.r: You do not need to face every difficult moment relying only on yourself. Bring the challenge to God and ask for the strength you need.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another faithful way to remain firm. Let difficulty become a reason to seek greater strength rather than a reason to abandon what is good.

p: Strength is often shown by continuing when it would be easier to stop. God can help us remain firm through challenges.
In Doctrine and Covenants 87:8 we read: “Wherefore, stand ye in holy places, and be not moved, until the day of the Lord come.”
Face one difficult situation today with greater faithfulness.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 87:8
Stand firm on one thing today that is right, even if others disagree.

pages.q: Being firm does not mean feeling no fear. It means choosing what is right despite it.

183.pq: But if we hope for that we see not, then do we with patience wait for it.

p: Some answers and blessings take longer than we expected.
Waiting does not have to mean doing nothing. We can continue living faithfully while trusting that not every good thing arrives immediately.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you wait with hope before continuing.

pages.q: But if we hope for that we see not, then do we with patience wait for it.

pages.prompt: How will you use a season of waiting well?

o.l: I will continue doing the good I already know to do.
o.r: You may not have every answer yet, but you can still act on the truths you already understand. Faithful action gives purpose to a season of waiting.

o.l: I will stop trying to force the outcome.
o.r: Not every result can be controlled through greater pressure. Do what is yours to do and recognize what must be left in God's hands.

o.l: I will look for growth during the waiting.
o.r: A delayed answer does not mean the present has no value. Consider what you can learn, strengthen, or prepare while you wait.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another faithful way to use this period well. Ask God to help hope remain active while the answer is still unseen.

p: Waiting can test our confidence, but it can also teach us endurance and trust. We can continue doing good before we understand the full outcome.
In Lamentations 3:25-26 we read: “The LORD is good unto them that wait for him, to the soul that seeketh him.”
Let hope guide what you do while you wait.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Lamentations 3:25-26
Write one thing you are waiting for. Hope for it with patience today.

pages.q: Waiting with hope means continuing to live faithfully before the answer arrives.

184.pq: When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.

p: Our commitments shape trust.
Keeping our word helps others know they can rely on us, and it helps us become more consistent in the promises we make.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you honor your commitments before continuing.

pages.q: When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.

pages.prompt: Which commitment needs your attention today?

o.l: I will complete something I promised to do.
o.r: Look at a promise that is still within your ability to fulfill. Take a clear step toward completing what you said you would do.

o.l: I will communicate honestly if I cannot meet a commitment.
o.r: Sometimes circumstances change and a commitment cannot be fulfilled as planned. Speak honestly and as early as possible rather than leaving others uncertain.

o.l: I will be more careful before making a promise.
o.r: A sincere commitment deserves thoughtful consideration. Do not make promises quickly simply because it feels easier in the moment.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another responsible way to honor your word. Ask God to help you become someone whose commitments can be trusted.

p: Keeping commitments requires both honesty and effort. Our reliability can become a quiet blessing to the people around us.
In Matthew 5:37 we read: “But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay.”
Give attention today to one promise you have made.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Matthew 5:37
Keep one small promise today, exactly as you said you would.

pages.q: Trust grows when our words and actions remain connected.

185.pq: For the LORD seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart.

p: People are often judged quickly by what others can see.
God sees more deeply. We can also learn to look beyond appearance and avoid deciding a person's worth too quickly.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you see people with greater understanding before continuing.

pages.q: For the LORD seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart.

pages.prompt: How will you look beyond appearances today?

o.l: I will avoid making a quick judgment about someone.
o.r: You may not know the full story behind another person's appearance or behavior. Give yourself more information before deciding what kind of person they are.

o.l: I will look for a person's good qualities.
o.r: Every person has strengths that may not be immediately visible. Make an effort to notice one good quality you might otherwise overlook.

o.l: I will examine my own heart instead of focusing on appearances.
o.r: It can be easier to notice the outward lives of others than our own inner condition. Ask what God may want you to improve within yourself.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to see beyond the surface. Ask God to give you greater patience and understanding toward other people.

p: Outward appearances can tell us only part of a person's story. God sees the heart, and we can become slower to judge what we do not fully understand.
In John 7:24 we read: “Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment.”
Look for deeper understanding today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in John 7:24
Look for one good thing in someone today that you usually miss.

pages.q: A person's outward appearance does not reveal everything God sees within them.

186.pq: I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.

p: There are times when our own strength feels limited.
Jesus Christ can strengthen us to face responsibilities, endure difficulties, and continue doing what is right.
Take a moment to pray and ask Christ for the strength you need before continuing.

pages.q: I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.

pages.prompt: Where do you need Christ's strength today?

o.l: I need strength for a difficult responsibility.
o.r: Bring the responsibility honestly to God. Then take the next step you can while trusting that strength can come as you act.

o.l: I need strength to keep going.
o.r: You may not need enough strength for the whole future today. Ask for strength for the next hour, the next choice, and the next step.

o.l: I need strength to do what is right.
o.r: A righteous choice can require courage when another path feels easier. Ask Christ to strengthen your desire and ability to follow what you know is right.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Name another need that feels larger than your own strength. Turn to Christ and ask for the help you need to continue.

p: Christ does not ask us to pretend that we are strong enough on our own. We can turn to Him and receive strength for the work before us.
In Isaiah 40:29-31 we read: “He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength.”
Ask for His help with one specific need today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Isaiah 40:29-31
Name one task that feels too big. Ask Jesus Christ for strength and begin.

pages.q: We can ask Christ for strength when our own strength is not enough.

187.pq: A friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.

p: Good friendships need more than pleasant moments.
A faithful friend can be present during difficulty, speak honestly with kindness, and remain dependable over time.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you become a better friend before continuing.

pages.q: A friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.

pages.prompt: How will you strengthen a friendship today?

o.l: I will check on someone who may need support.
o.r: A simple message or conversation can show that someone has not been forgotten. Reach out with genuine interest rather than expecting anything in return.

o.l: I will keep something entrusted to me private.
o.r: Trust is strengthened when we respect appropriate confidence. Do not share another person's personal information simply because you know it.

o.l: I will be honest with kindness.
o.r: Faithful friendship includes more than saying what another person wants to hear. Speak truth with respect and with a sincere desire for their good.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to show that you are dependable. Let your friendship be strengthened through sincere care and consistent actions.

p: Friendship can become stronger through trust, honesty, and presence. Small actions can show people that they matter.
In Proverbs 27:17 we read: “Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.”
Do one thing today that helps someone feel valued as a friend.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Proverbs 27:17
Check in on a friend today. Ask how you can help.

pages.q: Faithful friendship is shown through consistent care, not only pleasant moments.

188.pq: Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery.

p: Each person has abilities that can be developed and used for good.
A talent may grow slowly, but neglecting it can keep us from discovering how much good it could do.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you recognize and develop your gifts before continuing.

pages.q: Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery.

pages.prompt: How will you use one of your abilities for good today?

o.l: I will practice one skill.
o.r: Growth often comes through repeated effort. Give focused time to one ability you want to improve.

o.l: I will use an ability to help someone.
o.r: Your skills can become a blessing when you use them beyond yourself. Consider who might benefit from something you know how to do.

o.l: I will stop comparing my abilities with someone else's.
o.r: Comparison can make you overlook what you have been given. Focus on developing your own gifts with gratitude and effort.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another meaningful way to develop or use an ability. Ask God to help you recognize opportunities to use your gifts wisely.

p: Gifts and abilities grow when they are developed with patience and used with purpose. You do not need to have every talent to make a meaningful contribution.
In Doctrine and Covenants 46:11-12 we read: “For all have not every gift given unto them; for there are many gifts, and to every man is given a gift by the Spirit of God.”
Use one ability today in a way that brings good.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 46:11-12
Write one talent you have. Use it to help someone this week.

pages.q: A gift becomes more useful when we develop it and use it for good.

189.pq: Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:

p: Listening well requires more than waiting for our turn to speak.
When we listen carefully, we may understand a person or situation more accurately before forming a response.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you listen with greater attention before continuing.

pages.q: Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:

pages.prompt: How will you become a better listener today?

o.l: I will let someone finish speaking.
o.r: Avoid interrupting simply because you think you know what the person will say. Give them time to express their full thought.

o.l: I will ask a question before giving my opinion.
o.r: A thoughtful question can help you understand more clearly. Seek information before assuming you already know the full situation.

o.l: I will listen without preparing my response immediately.
o.r: When your mind is focused only on what you will say next, you may miss important words. Give your attention first to understanding.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another practical way to listen more carefully. Ask God to help you understand people before rushing to respond.

p: Careful listening can prevent misunderstanding and strengthen relationships. It shows that we value what another person is trying to communicate.
In Proverbs 18:13 we read: “He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him.”
Give someone your full attention today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Proverbs 18:13
In one conversation today, listen fully before you answer.

pages.q: Listening becomes more meaningful when our goal is to understand.

190.pq: Can two walk together, except they be agreed?

p: The people we spend time with can influence our thinking and choices.
We can choose relationships that encourage what is good and help us remain true to our values.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you choose wise influences before continuing.

pages.q: Can two walk together, except they be agreed?

pages.prompt: What will you do to choose better influences?

o.l: I will spend more time with people who encourage good choices.
o.r: Pay attention to how certain relationships influence your actions. Make room for people who help you become more honest, responsible, and faithful.

o.l: I will set a healthy boundary around a harmful influence.
o.r: Some influences repeatedly lead us away from what we know is right. Consider one boundary that can help protect your values.

o.l: I will become a better influence myself.
o.r: You also influence the people around you. Choose words and actions that make it easier for others to do what is good.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another wise step regarding the influences in your life. Ask God to help you recognize which relationships strengthen your best choices.

p: Our associations do not remove our agency, but they can make some choices easier or harder. We can choose influences that support the life we want to live.
In Psalm 1:1 we read: “Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.”
Consider one influence you will choose more carefully today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Psalm 1:1
Spend time today with someone who helps you do right.

pages.q: The people around us can influence the choices we find easier to make.

191.pq: Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.

p: We do not have to make every important decision alone.
Wise counsel can help us see what we may have missed and consider a situation more carefully.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you recognize good counsel before continuing.

pages.q: Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.

pages.prompt: What will you do when you need guidance for an important decision?

o.l: I will seek counsel from someone wise and trustworthy.
o.r: Choose someone whose character and judgment you respect. Listen carefully to their perspective without expecting them to make the decision for you.

o.l: I will consider more than one perspective.
o.r: One viewpoint may not reveal every part of a situation. Thoughtful counsel from more than one wise source can help you see more clearly.

o.l: I will pray before making my decision.
o.r: Counsel from others can be helpful, but you can also take your decision to God. Ask Him for wisdom as you consider what you have learned.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another wise way to seek guidance. Remain humble enough to recognize that another person may help you see something you had not considered.

p: Seeking counsel is not a sign of weakness. It can show humility and a desire to make wiser decisions.
In Proverbs 15:22 we read: “Without counsel purposes are disappointed: but in the multitude of counsellors they are established.”
When an important choice comes, do not be afraid to seek good guidance.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Proverbs 15:22
Ask a wise person for advice on a choice. Listen carefully.

pages.q: Wise counsel can help us see what we cannot always see alone.

192.theme: Keeping Your Mind on What Is Good
192.pq: And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind.

p: What we repeatedly allow into our minds can influence our feelings and choices.
We cannot control every thought that comes, but we can choose what we continue to focus on.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you fill your mind with what is good before continuing.

pages.q: And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind.

pages.prompt: What will you choose to give more attention to today?

o.l: I will focus on something true and worthwhile.
o.r: Choose something that strengthens understanding and leads your mind toward what is good. Give it your attention instead of feeding unnecessary negativity.

o.l: I will reduce something that fills my mind with harmful thoughts.
o.r: Notice one influence that repeatedly leaves your mind disturbed or pulled toward what is not good. Set a clear limit around it today.

o.l: I will replace an unhelpful thought with a better one.
o.r: You do not have to remain focused on every negative thought. Intentionally turn your attention toward something true, pure, or worthy of praise.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to direct your mind toward what is good. Ask God to help you recognize what deserves more of your attention.

p: A good mind is not built by accident. It is strengthened through repeated choices about what we welcome and what we reject.
In Philippians 2:5 we read: “Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus.”
Give your attention today to something that is true and good.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Philippians 2:5
Choose one thing to fill your mind with today that is good.

pages.q: We may not choose every thought that comes, but we can choose what we continue to feed.

193.pq: A wise man will hear, and will increase learning; and a man of understanding shall attain unto wise counsels:

p: Learning can continue throughout life.
A person becomes more teachable by listening, asking questions, and remaining willing to discover that there is more to understand.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you remain ready to learn before continuing.

pages.q: A wise man will hear, and will increase learning; and a man of understanding shall attain unto wise counsels:

pages.prompt: How will you become more willing to learn today?

o.l: I will listen to someone who knows more than I do.
o.r: You do not lose anything by learning from another person's experience or knowledge. Listen with respect and look for something useful you can understand better.

o.l: I will ask a question instead of pretending to know.
o.r: Honest questions can open the door to greater understanding. Be willing to say that you do not yet know and seek the answer.

o.l: I will learn something that can help me serve better.
o.r: Knowledge becomes especially valuable when it helps us bless others. Choose one thing to learn that can improve your ability to do good.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to keep learning. Ask God for a humble mind that remains open to truth wherever it is found.

p: A wise person does not believe there is nothing left to learn. Growth continues when we remain willing to listen and understand.
In 2 Nephi 9:29 we read: “But to be learned is good if they hearken unto the counsels of God.”
Let today teach you something useful.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 2 Nephi 9:29
Learn one new thing today and write it down.

pages.q: A willing mind can continue learning at every stage of life.

194.theme: Making Room for What Matters Most
194.pq: And that which fell among thorns are they, which, when they have heard, go forth…

p: Life can become crowded with many responsibilities and distractions.
Not everything asking for our attention deserves the same place in our lives. We need to make room for what matters most.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you see what deserves your attention before continuing.

pages.q: And that which fell among thorns are they, which, when they have heard, go forth, and are choked with cares and riches and pleasures of this life, and bring no fruit to perfection.

pages.prompt: What will you make more room for today?

o.l: I will give time to something spiritually important.
o.r: Choose a specific time to turn your attention toward God. Protect that time as you would another important responsibility.

o.l: I will reduce one unnecessary distraction.
o.r: Some activities take more attention than they are worth. Identify one distraction you can limit so something better has room to grow.

o.l: I will review how I am using my time.
o.r: Look honestly at where your hours are going. Small adjustments can help your daily life better reflect what you value.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to make space for what truly matters. Ask God to help you recognize what may be crowding out something more important.

p: Good things can be neglected when less important things take all our attention. Our priorities become clearer through how we use our time.
In Luke 10:41-42 we read: “And Jesus answered and said unto her, Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things.”
Make room today for something that truly matters.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Luke 10:41-42
Put one distraction away today so you can give someone your full attention.

pages.q: What matters most needs more than good intentions. It needs a place in our lives.

195.pq: Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom.

p: Many good things in our lives have come through the help, kindness, knowledge, and sacrifice of others.
As we recognize what we have received, we can look for ways to give without always expecting something in return.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to show you what you can freely give before continuing.

pages.q: Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom.

pages.prompt: What can you freely give to someone today?

o.l: I will give some of my time.
o.r: Time can be one of the most meaningful gifts you offer. Give someone your attention without making them feel rushed.

o.l: I will share something useful that I know.
o.r: Your knowledge may help someone solve a problem or understand something better. Share what you know with patience and respect.

o.l: I will offer encouragement without expecting anything back.
o.r: A sincere word of encouragement can strengthen someone who is struggling. Give it freely without waiting for praise or repayment.

o.l: I can do something else
