o.r: Choose another good thing you can offer freely. Look beyond money and remember that your time, abilities, and care can also bless others.

p: Giving reminds us that life is not only about receiving. What we have can become more meaningful when we use it to bless someone else.

In Acts 20:35 we read: “I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.”
Look for one thing you can freely give today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Acts 20:35
Give something today without being asked.

pages.q: What we freely give can become a blessing far beyond its size.

196.pq: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.

p: There are many things we can pursue, and it is easy to lose sight of why we are living.
Remembering our purpose can help us make better decisions when many choices compete for our attention.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you remember what matters most before continuing.

pages.q: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.

pages.prompt: What will help you live with greater purpose today?

o.l: I will make one decision based on what matters most.
o.r: Before choosing, ask whether the decision moves you toward the kind of life you want to live. Let your deeper values guide one practical action.

o.l: I will remember God while planning my day.
o.r: Include your relationship with God when considering your responsibilities. Ask how you can honor Him through the choices before you.

o.l: I will stop giving too much importance to something temporary.
o.r: Some concerns feel urgent but will matter very little later. Step back and consider whether one temporary issue is receiving more attention than it deserves.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another action that helps you live more intentionally. Ask God to help your daily choices reflect your true purpose.

p: Purpose gives direction to ordinary choices. When we remember what matters most, we can live with greater clarity.
In 1 Corinthians 10:31 we read: “Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God.”
Let one decision today reflect your deeper purpose.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 1 Corinthians 10:31
Write what you believe your purpose is. Take one step toward it.

pages.q: Purpose becomes clearer when our daily choices reflect what matters most.

197.pq: Now the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned.

p: Our conscience can help us notice when something in our choices needs attention.
Living with a clear conscience requires honesty, correction, and a willingness to make things right when possible.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you live with greater sincerity before continuing.

pages.q: Now the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned.

pages.prompt: What will you do to protect a clear conscience?

o.l: I will correct something I know is wrong.
o.r: Do not ignore a wrong simply because correcting it may feel uncomfortable. Take one appropriate step toward making the situation better.

o.l: I will be honest even when it costs me something.
o.r: Honesty may sometimes require courage. Choose truth over an easier answer that would leave you with regret.

o.l: I will stop excusing a choice I know is not right.
o.r: Excuses can make it harder to change. Be honest with yourself about what needs to be different and begin there.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another action that brings greater honesty into your life. Ask God to help you recognize and respond to what your conscience is teaching you.

p: A clear conscience is strengthened through consistent choices. When we recognize a wrong, we can choose to address it rather than hide from it.
In 1 Peter 3:16 we read: “Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ.”
Take one honest step today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 1 Peter 3:16
Before you sleep, ask yourself whether you did what you knew was right. Make a note.

pages.q: A clear conscience is protected by the choices we are willing to make honestly.

198.pq: So then every one of us shall give account of himself to God.

p: Our choices belong to us, even when other people influence or pressure us.
Taking responsibility means being honest about what we choose and being willing to learn from the results.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you take responsibility with humility before continuing.

pages.q: So then every one of us shall give account of himself to God.

pages.prompt: How will you take greater responsibility today?

o.l: I will admit when I make a mistake.
o.r: Admitting a mistake can be uncomfortable, but it is often the first step toward correcting it. Speak honestly instead of hiding behind excuses.

o.l: I will focus on what I can control.
o.r: You cannot control every circumstance or another person's choices. Give your energy to the decisions and actions that are actually yours.

o.l: I will repair a problem I helped create.
o.r: When possible, take part in making things right. Responsibility is shown not only by admitting a problem but also by helping address it.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another honest way to take ownership of your choices. Ask God to help you act responsibly without becoming discouraged by your imperfections.

p: Taking responsibility helps us grow. It moves us away from excuses and toward honest action.
In Galatians 6:5 we read: “For every man shall bear his own burden.”
Choose one area today where you will own your part and act accordingly.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Galatians 6:5
Own one choice today, good or bad. Say it plainly and move forward.

pages.q: Growth begins when we stop hiding from our choices and learn from them.

199.pq: But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.

p: Learning truth is important, but knowledge becomes more powerful when it changes how we live.
We can ask ourselves whether something we have learned is waiting for us to put it into practice.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you act on the truth you receive before continuing.

pages.q: But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.

pages.prompt: What truth will you put into action today?

o.l: I will act on something I already know is right.
o.r: You may not need more information before taking the next step. Identify one truth you understand and let it guide a real action today.

o.l: I will stop delaying a good change.
o.r: Delay can become a habit when we keep waiting for the perfect moment. Begin with one small action instead of waiting for everything to feel easy.

o.l: I will make my beliefs visible through my choices.
o.r: Your values become clearer through what you repeatedly do. Choose one action that matches what you say you believe.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to put truth into practice. Ask God to show you how today's learning can become today's action.

p: Truth is meant to influence the way we live. Even a small act of obedience to what we know can move us forward.
In Matthew 7:24 we read: “Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock.”
Choose one truth today and practice it.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Matthew 7:24
Read a verse today and do what it says before the day ends.

pages.q: Truth becomes part of us when we are willing to live it.

200.theme: Looking for Ways to Lift Others
200.pq: Wherefore comfort yourselves together, and edify one another, even as also ye do.

p: People around us may be carrying burdens we cannot see.
Our words and actions can either make another person's day heavier or help them feel strengthened.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to show you someone you can help lift before continuing.

pages.q: Wherefore comfort yourselves together, and edify one another, even as also ye do.

pages.prompt: How will you help strengthen someone today?

o.l: I will give sincere encouragement.
o.r: Be specific and honest in what you say. A person may need to hear that their effort, goodness, or progress has been noticed.

o.l: I will offer practical help.
o.r: Look for a real need and help in a useful way. Sometimes a simple action can provide more support than many words.

o.l: I will listen when someone needs to talk.
o.r: You may not have to solve every problem. Giving someone your patient attention can help them feel less alone.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to strengthen another person. Ask God to help you notice needs that you might otherwise overlook.

p: We can build others through simple and sincere actions. We do not need to do something large to make a real difference.
In Hebrews 10:24-25 we read: “And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works.”
Look for one person you can help strengthen today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Hebrews 10:24-25
Send one message today that lifts someone's spirits.

pages.q: A sincere effort to strengthen someone can change more than we may realize.

201.pq: He that walketh uprightly walketh surely: but he that perverteth his ways shall be known.

p: The way we live matters, even when no one is watching.
A life of upright choices brings greater confidence because we do not need to hide who we are.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you walk uprightly before continuing.

pages.q: He that walketh uprightly walketh surely: but he that perverteth his ways shall be known.

pages.prompt: How will you choose to walk more uprightly today?

o.l: I will do what is right even when no one sees me.
o.r: Private choices shape our character. Choose what is right because of who you want to become, not because someone is watching.

o.l: I will be consistent in my words and actions.
o.r: Let your actions support the values you express. Consistency builds trust with God, with others, and with yourself.

o.l: I will correct one habit that does not match my values.
o.r: Notice one pattern that needs improvement. Take a practical step toward changing it today.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to live with greater uprightness. Ask God to help your private and public choices become more consistent.

p: Walking uprightly does not mean being perfect. It means sincerely choosing what is right and correcting your course when needed.
In Psalm 15:1-2 we read: “Lord, who shall abide in thy tabernacle? who shall dwell in thy holy hill?”
Let one honest choice today strengthen your character.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Psalm 15:1-2
Do one thing today the same way whether anyone is watching or not.

pages.q: Character is strengthened when we choose what is right even when no one is watching.

202.pq: Pleasant words are as an honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.

p: The words we choose can either build someone up or wear them down.
A kind word costs little to give, but it can mean a great deal to the person who receives it.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you speak words that heal rather than words that harm.

pages.q: Pleasant words are as an honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.

pages.prompt: How will you choose kinder words today?

o.l: I will compliment someone sincerely.
o.r: A genuine compliment can brighten someone's entire day. Look for something true and good to say, and say it.

o.l: I will soften how I say something difficult.
o.r: Hard truths do not have to be delivered harshly. Choose words that are honest but also gentle.

o.l: I will speak encouragement instead of criticism.
o.r: Notice an opportunity today to build someone up rather than point out a flaw. Encouragement often accomplishes more than correction.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to let your words be a source of healing today. Ask God to help your speech reflect His love for others.

p: Words are never truly small. They can linger in someone's memory long after the moment has passed.
In Colossians 4:6 we read: “Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man.”
Speak today in a way you would want to be spoken to.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Colossians 4:6
Say something kind today that you would normally keep to yourself.

pages.q: Kind words cost little, but their effect can last a lifetime.

203.pq: In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips is wise.

p: Words can be useful, but not every thought needs to be spoken.
Wisdom includes knowing when our words will help and when silence is the better choice.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you use your words wisely before continuing.

pages.q: In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips is wise.

pages.prompt: What will guide your words today?

o.l: I will pause before saying something unnecessary.
o.r: A short pause can prevent words you may later regret. Ask yourself whether what you are about to say is truly needed.

o.l: I will avoid repeating harmful information about someone.
o.r: You do not need to pass along every story you hear. Protect another person's dignity when the information does not need to be shared.

o.l: I will speak less when I am feeling emotional.
o.r: Strong emotions can make careful communication difficult. Give yourself time to become calm before discussing an important matter.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to exercise greater wisdom with your words. Ask God to help you recognize when silence would be more helpful.

p: Wise speech is not measured only by how much we say. It is also shown by what we choose not to say.
In Ecclesiastes 5:2 we read: “Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter any thing before God.”
Let your words today be thoughtful and necessary.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Ecclesiastes 5:2
Pause before you speak in one conversation today. Say only what is needed.

pages.q: Wisdom includes knowing when fewer words are better words.

204.pq: That which is altogether just shalt thou follow, that thou mayest live, and inherit the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee.

p: We should care about what is fair and right.
Justice asks us to avoid favoritism and to treat people with honesty and respect.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you choose what is just before continuing.

pages.q: That which is altogether just shalt thou follow, that thou mayest live, and inherit the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee.

pages.prompt: How will you act more justly today?

o.l: I will treat people fairly.
o.r: Do not give better treatment only because someone is important to you. Let fairness guide how you deal with others.

o.l: I will consider both sides before forming an opinion.
o.r: A quick judgment may overlook important facts. Take time to understand a situation before deciding what is right.

o.l: I will refuse to benefit from something unfair.
o.r: An unfair advantage may appear useful in the moment. Choose what is right even when fairness requires you to give something up.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another action that reflects fairness and justice. Ask God to help you see situations clearly and treat people with respect.

p: Justice is expressed through real choices. It affects how we speak, judge, share, and treat people.
In Amos 5:24 we read: “But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.”
Look for one opportunity today to choose fairness.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Amos 5:24
Choose to be fair in one moment today, even when it costs you.

pages.q: Choosing what is fair may require courage, but it protects the dignity of others.

205.pq: Harden not your heart, as in the provocation, and as in the day of temptation in the wilderness:

p: Disappointment and pain can make us want to close our hearts.
A soft heart remains willing to learn, forgive, receive truth, and respond to God.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you keep your heart open before continuing.

pages.q: Harden not your heart, as in the provocation, and as in the day of temptation in the wilderness:

pages.prompt: What will help you keep a softer heart today?

o.l: I will remain willing to forgive.
o.r: Forgiveness may take time, but refusing to let resentment grow can protect your heart. Take one step toward releasing the desire to hold onto the wrong.

o.l: I will remain open to correction.
o.r: Correction can be difficult to receive. Listen for what may help you improve instead of immediately becoming defensive.

o.l: I will not let one disappointment define everything.
o.r: A painful experience is real, but it does not have to close you to future good. Leave room for healing and for new possibilities.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to keep your heart open to God and goodness. Ask Him to help you remain tender without becoming discouraged.

p: A soft heart can still be strong. It allows us to respond to truth and continue growing through life's experiences.
In Hebrews 3:15 we read: “While it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts, as in the provocation.”
Protect your heart from becoming closed today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Hebrews 3:15
Notice one moment today when your heart feels hard. Pray to soften it.

pages.q: A soft heart remains open to truth, healing, and change.

206.pq: Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might.

p: Ordinary responsibilities can become opportunities to develop good character.
Doing our best does not mean never making mistakes. It means giving sincere effort to the work before us.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you give your best effort before continuing.

pages.q: Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might.

pages.prompt: How will you improve your effort today?

o.l: I will give full attention to one important task.
o.r: Choose one responsibility and work on it without unnecessary distractions. Focus can improve both the quality of your effort and your sense of progress.

o.l: I will finish something I have been neglecting.
o.r: An unfinished responsibility can continue demanding attention. Take a practical step toward completing something important.

o.l: I will improve the quality of something I already do.
o.r: Look for one simple way to do your work better. Small improvements, repeated consistently, can produce meaningful growth.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to give sincere effort. Ask God to help you work with purpose rather than only seeking the approval of others.

p: Our attitude toward ordinary work can reveal much about our character. Sincere effort is valuable even when no one praises it.
In Proverbs 22:29 we read: “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings.”
Give your best honest effort to something before you today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Proverbs 22:29
Give one task your best effort today. Finish it fully.

pages.q: Sincere effort gives value to even the ordinary responsibilities of life.

207.pq: The young lions do lack, and suffer hunger: but they that seek the LORD shall not want any good thing.

p: It is easy to spend life thinking we will finally be satisfied when we have more.
Contentment helps us appreciate what is already good without preventing us from working toward worthy goals.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you recognize enough before continuing.

pages.q: The young lions do lack, and suffer hunger: but they that seek the LORD shall not want any good thing.

pages.prompt: How will you practice greater contentment today?

o.l: I will appreciate something I already have.
o.r: Pause and notice one blessing that has become familiar to you. Appreciation can help you see value that you may have stopped noticing.

o.l: I will stop comparing my life with someone else's.
o.r: You do not know every part of another person's life. Return your attention to your own responsibilities, blessings, and opportunities.

o.l: I will pursue improvement without believing more will solve everything.
o.r: It is good to work toward worthy goals. Keep your goals in perspective and remember that a meaningful life is not built only by gaining more.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to appreciate the good already present in your life. Ask God to help you recognize blessings without losing the desire to grow.

p: Contentment is not laziness or lack of ambition. It is the ability to recognize present blessings while still moving forward wisely.
In Philippians 4:19 we read: “But my God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus.”
Find one reason to be satisfied and grateful today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Philippians 4:19
Write what you have enough of. Be glad for it today.

pages.q: Contentment helps us recognize that a meaningful life is not measured only by what we gain.

208.pq: Holiness becometh thine house, O LORD, for ever.

p: Some things deserve special care because they are sacred.
Reverence is shown through our attitude, our words, and the way we prepare ourselves to approach holy things.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you recognize what is sacred before continuing.

pages.q: Holiness becometh thine house, O LORD, for ever.

pages.prompt: How will you show greater respect for what is sacred today?

o.l: I will prepare my mind before a spiritual experience.
o.r: Do not move into sacred moments without thought. Take time to become calm and intentional so you can give the experience greater attention.

o.l: I will speak respectfully about holy things.
o.r: Words can show whether we value something. Choose language that reflects sincerity and respect when speaking about God and sacred matters.

o.l: I will treat a sacred place with greater reverence.
o.r: Let your behavior show that you recognize the purpose of the place. Small choices in speech and conduct can express deep respect.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to show respect for something sacred. Ask God to help you approach holy things with a sincere and prepared heart.

p: Reverence is more than being quiet. It is an inward respect that influences how we approach God and sacred things.
In Leviticus 19:30 we read: “Ye shall keep my sabbaths, and reverence my sanctuary.”
Let your actions today show what you truly value.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Leviticus 19:30
Show respect for something sacred today with quiet and care.

pages.q: Reverence is shown by the care we give to what we recognize as sacred.

209.pq: He that speaketh truth sheweth forth righteousness: but a false witness deceit.

p: Truth builds trust, while deception damages it.
Living without deceit requires us to be truthful not only when it is easy, but also when honesty may be uncomfortable.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you choose truth before continuing.

pages.q: He that speaketh truth sheweth forth righteousness: but a false witness deceit.

pages.prompt: How will you choose greater truthfulness today?

o.l: I will give an honest answer when honesty is needed.
o.r: Avoid changing the truth to make yourself look better. Speak honestly while still choosing words that are respectful and kind.

o.l: I will correct a false impression I have created.
o.r: If someone believes something untrue because of what you said or allowed them to believe, take responsibility for correcting it.

o.l: I will avoid exaggerating to gain attention.
o.r: You do not need to make a story larger to be valued. Let the truth be enough.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to live more truthfully. Ask God to help you recognize subtle forms of deception and choose honesty instead.

p: Truthfulness strengthens relationships because trust depends on it. Each honest choice helps make our character more dependable.
In Zechariah 8:16 we read: “These are the things that ye shall do; Speak ye every man the truth to his neighbour.”
Let truth guide one difficult conversation or decision today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Zechariah 8:16
Speak only what is true today, even in small things.

pages.q: Trust grows where truth is spoken with sincerity.

210.pq: For whom the Lord loveth he correcteth; even as a father the son in whom he delighteth.

p: Correction can be difficult because it often shows us where we need to change.
When received with humility, loving correction can become an opportunity for growth rather than a reason for discouragement.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you learn from correction before continuing.

pages.q: For whom the Lord loveth he correcteth; even as a father the son in whom he delighteth.

pages.prompt: How will you respond when you are corrected?

o.l: I will listen before defending myself.
o.r: Your first reaction may be to explain yourself. Pause long enough to understand what the other person is trying to help you see.

o.l: I will look for something useful in the correction.
o.r: Not every criticism is completely accurate, but there may still be something worth considering. Look honestly for what can help you improve.

o.l: I will make a change where I know correction is needed.
o.r: Understanding a weakness is not the same as addressing it. Choose one practical action that reflects what you have learned.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another healthy way to respond to correction. Ask God for humility to recognize what you need to change without losing hope.

p: Correction does not always mean rejection. Sometimes it is evidence that growth is still possible and worth pursuing.
In Hebrews 12:11 we read: “Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous.”
When correction comes, ask what it can teach you.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Hebrews 12:11
Think of a correction that helped you. Thank God for it.

pages.q: Correction can become a source of growth when we are willing to learn from it.

211.pq: Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful.

p: People depend on one another in families, work, communities, and Church service.
Being dependable means taking our responsibilities seriously and becoming someone others can reasonably trust.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you become more dependable before continuing.

pages.q: Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful.

pages.prompt: How will you become more dependable today?

o.l: I will do something I promised to do.
o.r: Review a commitment you have made and take action on it. Keeping promises builds trust over time.

o.l: I will communicate early if I cannot meet a responsibility.
o.r: Sometimes circumstances change. Honest communication is better than leaving others uncertain or waiting without explanation.

o.l: I will complete a small responsibility without being reminded.
o.r: Do not always wait for someone else to ask. Take initiative where you already know what needs to be done.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to become more trustworthy in your responsibilities. Ask God to help you develop steady and faithful habits.

p: Dependability is built through repeated choices. Small responsibilities handled faithfully prepare us for greater trust.
In Luke 16:10 we read: “He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much.”
Let someone benefit today because they can depend on you.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Luke 16:10
Do what you said you would do today, and do it on time.

pages.q: Trust is strengthened when our actions repeatedly show that we can be depended upon.

212.pq: My brethren, have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons.

p: It is easy to give greater attention to people because of status, appearance, influence, or what they can offer us.
The gospel teaches us to see people as souls of worth, not as categories of greater or lesser importance.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you treat people without favoritism before continuing.

pages.q: My brethren, have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons.

pages.prompt: How will you show greater respect to every person today?

o.l: I will give equal courtesy to people regardless of status.
o.r: Respect should not depend on what someone can give you. Treat each person with basic dignity and kindness.

o.l: I will notice someone who may be overlooked.
o.r: Look beyond the people who naturally receive attention. Include someone who may feel unseen or left out.

o.l: I will question one unfair assumption I have made about someone.
o.r: Assumptions can prevent us from seeing people clearly. Replace a quick judgment with a desire to understand the individual.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to treat people with greater fairness. Ask God to help you see the worth of people beyond outward differences.

p: Every person deserves to be treated with dignity. We become more Christlike when our respect is not controlled by status or advantage.
In Acts 10:34-35 we read: “Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons.”
Give someone today the same courtesy you would hope to receive.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Acts 10:34-35
Greet or include someone today who is usually overlooked.

pages.q: True respect does not depend on a person's status or usefulness to us.

213.pq: Wait on the LORD: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the LORD.

p: Some answers and changes do not come as quickly as we want.
Waiting can become a time of spiritual growth when we continue trusting, serving, and doing what is right.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to strengthen you while you wait before continuing.

pages.q: Wait on the LORD: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the LORD.

pages.prompt: How will you use a season of waiting today?

o.l: I will continue doing what I know is right.
o.r: Do not stop making good choices simply because you are still waiting for an answer or change. Faithfulness can continue during uncertainty.

o.l: I will stop trying to force an outcome I cannot control.
o.r: Some things require patience and cannot be rushed. Focus on your responsibilities and release what is outside your power.

o.l: I will use this time to prepare myself.
o.r: Waiting does not have to mean doing nothing. Develop a skill, strengthen your character, or prepare for the opportunity you hope will come.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another constructive way to use this period of waiting. Ask God to help you find strength and purpose while answers are still unfolding.

p: Waiting can test us, but it can also strengthen us. We can continue moving forward even when we do not yet see the full outcome.
In Psalm 40:1 we read: “I waited patiently for the LORD; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry.”
Use today well, even if something important is still unresolved.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Psalm 40:1
Write one thing you are waiting on. Wait today with hope, not worry.

pages.q: Waiting does not mean life has stopped. We can still grow while answers are unfolding.

214.pq: It is an honour for a man to cease from strife: but every fool will be meddling.

p: Not every disagreement needs to become a quarrel.
We can have different opinions while still choosing respect, self-control, and peace.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you step away from unnecessary conflict before continuing.

pages.q: It is an honour for a man to cease from strife: but every fool will be meddling.

pages.prompt: How will you reduce unnecessary conflict today?

o.l: I will not continue an argument that is becoming harmful.
o.r: Notice when the conversation is no longer helping either person. It may be wiser to pause and return later with calmer minds.

o.l: I will disagree without attacking the other person.
o.r: You can challenge an idea without insulting a person. Keep your words focused on the issue and maintain respect.

o.l: I will choose not to become involved in someone else's unnecessary conflict.
o.r: You do not need to join every disagreement around you. Stay out of conflict that does not require your involvement.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to reduce unnecessary strife. Ask God to help you recognize when peace is more valuable than proving a point.

p: Peace does not require us to agree about everything. It requires us to choose how we respond when differences arise.
In 2 Timothy 2:23-24 we read: “But foolish and unlearned questions avoid, knowing that they do gender strifes.”
Choose one response today that prevents a disagreement from becoming worse.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 2 Timothy 2:23-24
Walk away from one argument today with a kind word.

pages.q: Not every disagreement deserves more of our time and energy.

215.pq: Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time…

p: Our time in this life is precious.
Remembering that life is brief can help us stop postponing what is truly important.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you use your time wisely before continuing.

pages.q: Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away.

pages.prompt: What important thing will you stop postponing?

o.l: I will begin a good action I have delayed.
o.r: You may not need to wait for a perfect time. Take the first realistic step today.

o.l: I will give attention to an important relationship.
o.r: Relationships need time and care. Reach out, listen, or express appreciation to someone who matters.

o.l: I will spend less time on something that has little lasting value.
o.r: Review one habit that consumes more time than it deserves. Use some of that time for something more meaningful.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another important action you have been delaying. Ask God to help you recognize what deserves your time now.

p: We cannot control how much time we have, but we can influence how we use the time given to us.
In Psalm 39:4 we read: “LORD, make me to know mine end, and the measure of my days, what it is.”
Do one meaningful thing today instead of always waiting for tomorrow.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Psalm 39:4
Write how you will use this week well. Choose one thing that matters most.

pages.q: Because time is precious, what we do today matters.

216.pq: Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.

p: People can feel alone when they enter an unfamiliar place or meet an unfamiliar group.
Hospitality is a simple way of helping others feel seen, welcomed, and respected.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you notice someone who may need a welcome before continuing.

pages.q: Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.

pages.prompt: How will you make someone feel more welcome today?

o.l: I will greet someone who may feel new or unfamiliar.
o.r: Do not assume another person already feels included. A simple greeting can help remove some of the discomfort of being new.

o.l: I will include someone in a conversation.
o.r: Notice if a person is standing alone or being left out. Make space for them to participate.

o.l: I will offer practical help to someone unfamiliar with the situation.
o.r: New people may not know where to go or what to do. Give clear and respectful help without making them feel embarrassed.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to make another person feel welcomed. Ask God to help you notice people who may feel unseen.

p: Hospitality does not always require a large act. Often it begins by noticing another person and making room for them.
In Romans 12:13 we read: “Distributing to the necessity of saints; given to hospitality.”
Help someone feel that they belong today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Romans 12:13
Invite someone to share a meal or a visit this week.

pages.q: A simple welcome can help a person feel that they are not alone.

217.pq: Abstain from all appearance of evil.

p: The influences we repeatedly choose can shape our thoughts, desires, and actions.
Avoiding harmful influences can be an important part of protecting the kind of person we want to become.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you recognize influences that are not good for you before continuing.

pages.q: Abstain from all appearance of evil.

pages.prompt: What will you do to choose better influences today?

o.l: I will stop giving attention to one harmful influence.
o.r: Be specific about what you need to reduce or remove. A clear boundary can make a good decision easier to keep.

o.l: I will choose entertainment that leaves me feeling better.
o.r: Pay attention to how what you watch or listen to affects your mind. Choose something that supports the values you want to live.

o.l: I will spend more time with people who encourage good choices.
o.r: The people around us can influence our direction. Strengthen relationships with those who encourage what is good.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to protect your mind and choices from harmful influences. Ask God to help you recognize what should have less influence in your life.

p: Our environment can influence us more than we realize. Wise boundaries can protect our ability to choose what is right.
In Psalm 101:3 we read: “I will set no wicked thing before mine eyes: I hate the work of them that turn aside.”
Choose one influence today that will support your best direction.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Psalm 101:3
Choose one thing today to avoid, so your heart stays clean.

pages.q: What we repeatedly allow around us can slowly influence what we allow within us.

218.pq: Boast not thyself of to morrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.

p: We rarely know what tomorrow actually holds, no matter how carefully we plan.
Trusting God with the unknown does not mean stopping preparation. It means holding our plans loosely enough to let Him lead.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you trust Him with what you cannot yet see before continuing.

pages.q: Boast not thyself of to morrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.

pages.prompt: Where do you need to trust God with the unknown today?

o.l: I will release a worry about something I cannot control.
o.r: Notice the worry you keep circling back to. Name it honestly to God, and let Him carry what you cannot control.

o.l: I will hold my plans loosely instead of rigidly.
o.r: A good plan still leaves room for God to redirect it. Stay open to a different path than the one you expected.

o.l: I will trust Him even without knowing the outcome.
o.r: You do not need certainty to move forward faithfully. Take the next step and trust Him with what remains unknown.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another honest way to place tomorrow in God's hands. Ask Him to help you live fully in today instead of only worrying about what's ahead.

p: No one can fully know what a single day will bring. That uncertainty is not meant to frighten us, but to remind us who is truly in control.
In James 4:13-15 we read: “Go to now, ye that say, To day or to morrow we will go into such a city, and continue there a year, and buy and sell, and get gain.”
Trust Him today with whatever tomorrow holds.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in James 4:13-15
Write one thing you do not know about tomorrow. Give it to God.

pages.q: We rarely know what a day will bring, but we can always know who holds it.

219.pq: Serve the LORD with gladness: come before his presence with singing.

p: Our service to God can become routine if we forget why we are doing it.
Gladness can grow when we remember that following God is an opportunity to draw closer to Him.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to renew your willingness to serve before continuing.

pages.q: Serve the LORD with gladness: come before his presence with singing.

pages.prompt: How will you bring greater gladness into your service today?

o.l: I will remember why I am doing what I do.
o.r: Pause before a responsibility and connect it with a meaningful purpose. Remembering why can change the way you approach the task.

o.l: I will serve without complaining about the effort.
o.r: Some responsibilities are tiring, but constant complaining can make them feel heavier. Focus on doing the good that is in front of you.

o.l: I will express gratitude for an opportunity to contribute.
o.r: Your contribution may be small, but it can still matter. Give thanks for the ability and opportunity to help.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to serve with a more willing heart. Ask God to help you find meaning in the good you are able to do.

p: Gladness does not mean every responsibility will be easy. It means we can choose to remember the good purpose behind our efforts.
In Doctrine and Covenants 64:34 we read: “Behold, the Lord requireth the heart and a willing mind.”
Let gratitude change the way you approach one responsibility today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 64:34
Begin your prayer today with thanks before you ask for anything.

pages.q: A willing heart can find deeper purpose in ordinary acts of service.

220.pq: Turn away mine eyes from beholding vanity; and quicken thou me in thy way.

p: Some things attract our attention but give little lasting value.
We can choose where to direct our eyes, thoughts, time, and energy.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you turn toward what has greater value before continuing.

pages.q: Turn away mine eyes from beholding vanity; and quicken thou me in thy way.

pages.prompt: What will you give less attention to today?

o.l: I will reduce time spent on something that does not help me.
o.r: Be honest about one activity that regularly takes more than it gives. Set a practical limit and use some of that time better.

o.l: I will stop returning to something I know is harmful.
o.r: Repeatedly going back can make change difficult. Strengthen your boundary by choosing a different action when the temptation returns.

o.l: I will replace empty attention with something worthwhile.
o.r: Removing a habit can be easier when something better takes its place. Choose an activity that strengthens your mind or spirit.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to turn your attention toward what has greater value. Ask God to help you see clearly what is worth your time.

p: Attention is valuable because it shapes how we spend our lives. We do not have to give equal attention to everything that asks for it.
In Colossians 3:2 we read: “Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth.”
Turn away from one empty pursuit and choose something better today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Colossians 3:2
Put aside one worthless distraction today. Use the time for something good.

pages.q: Where we repeatedly place our attention can influence the direction of our lives.

221.pq: Therefore if thou bring thy gift to the altar, and there rememberest that thy brother hath ought against thee…

p: Relationships sometimes become damaged through misunderstandings, harsh words, or wrong choices.
When possible, taking a sincere step toward reconciliation can bring healing and peace.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to guide you in repairing what you can before continuing.

pages.q: Therefore if thou bring thy gift to the altar, and there rememberest that thy brother hath ought against thee; Leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift.

pages.prompt: What step will you take toward greater reconciliation?

o.l: I will apologize for a wrong I have done.
o.r: A sincere apology does not need to defend or excuse the wrong. Acknowledge your part honestly and express your desire to do better.

o.l: I will begin a respectful conversation about a problem.
o.r: Avoid attacking or blaming the other person. Speak calmly about the concern and make room to hear their perspective.

o.l: I will stop adding to an existing conflict.
o.r: Even if a relationship cannot be repaired immediately, you can choose not to make the situation worse. Let your next action move toward peace.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another appropriate step toward reconciliation. Ask God for wisdom to know when to speak, what to say, and how to act with sincerity.

p: We cannot control another person's response, but we can take responsibility for our own efforts to make peace.
In Hebrews 12:14 we read: “Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord.”
If there is something you can repair, consider taking one sincere step today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Hebrews 12:14
Think of someone you need to make peace with. Send one kind message.

pages.q: We may not control every relationship, but we can control whether we are sincerely trying to make peace.

222.pq: But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.

p: Not every idea, message, or influence deserves immediate acceptance.
Discernment requires us to examine what we hear and choose carefully what we allow to guide our lives.
Take a moment to pray and ask God for wisdom to recognize what is good before continuing.

pages.q: But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.

pages.prompt: How will you practice better discernment today?

o.l: I will examine information before believing it.
o.r: Do not accept something as true simply because it was confidently stated or widely repeated. Look carefully for reliable understanding.

o.l: I will consider the results of a choice before making it.
o.r: Ask where the decision is likely to lead. Thinking beyond the immediate moment can help you recognize consequences more clearly.

o.l: I will hold firmly to something I know is good.
o.r: Discernment is not only about rejecting what is harmful. It also means recognizing what is true and continuing to choose it.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to examine your choices with greater wisdom. Ask God to help you recognize truth and reject what would lead you away from good.

p: Discernment develops through careful thought, experience, and spiritual guidance. We do not need to accept every influence that comes before us.
In 1 John 4:1 we read: “Beloved, believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God.”
Examine one important choice carefully today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 1 John 4:1
Notice one choice today and ask whether it is good or only easy.

pages.q: Discernment helps us recognize not only what is popular, but what is truly good.

223.pq: Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter any thing before God: for God is in heaven…

p: Words spoken quickly can create commitments we have not carefully considered.
Thoughtfulness before speaking can help us become more sincere and responsible.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you speak with greater care before continuing.

pages.q: Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter any thing before God: for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.

pages.prompt: How will you become more thoughtful before speaking today?

o.l: I will avoid making a promise I am not sure I can keep.
o.r: It is better to be honest about your limits than to make a promise only to disappoint someone later. Let your commitments be sincere.

o.l: I will take time before responding to an important request.
o.r: You do not always need to answer immediately. Consider your responsibilities before agreeing to something significant.

o.l: I will speak more carefully when emotions are strong.
o.r: Strong feelings can push us toward words we do not fully mean. Pause until you can speak with greater clarity and self-control.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to become more thoughtful with your words. Ask God to help your speech reflect sincerity rather than impulse.

p: Careful speech protects both us and others. We show maturity when our words are sincere and our commitments are considered.
In Proverbs 17:27 we read: “He that hath knowledge spareth his words: and a man of understanding is of an excellent spirit.”
Pause before making one important statement today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Proverbs 17:27
Think before you promise something today. Say yes only if you can keep it.

pages.q: Thoughtful words can prevent commitments and conflicts created by haste.

224.pq: Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise:

p: Nature can teach us lessons about preparation and steady effort.
Small tasks completed consistently can prepare us for needs and opportunities that come later.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you become more prepared before continuing.

pages.q: Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise:

pages.prompt: What will you prepare for today?

o.l: I will complete a small task before it becomes a bigger problem.
o.r: Some responsibilities are easier when handled early. Take care of one small matter before delay makes it more difficult.

o.l: I will prepare for something I know is coming.
o.r: Do not wait until the last moment when preparation can begin now. Take one useful step toward a future responsibility.

o.l: I will develop a steady routine for an important goal.
o.r: Large progress often comes through repeated small actions. Choose a simple routine you can realistically continue.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to prepare wisely. Ask God to help you recognize what can be done now rather than always being delayed.

p: Preparation is often quiet and gradual. What we do consistently today can make tomorrow's responsibilities easier.
In Doctrine and Covenants 38:30 we read: “I tell you these things because of your prayers.”
Take one small step toward being better prepared.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Doctrine and Covenants 38:30
Start one small task today and finish it without being told.

pages.q: Small preparation today can provide greater strength when tomorrow's needs arrive.

225.pq: Owe no man any thing, but to love one another: for he that loveth another hath fulfilled the law.

p: Love is not only a feeling. It is shown through the way we treat people.
When we choose to love others, we become more aware of their needs, dignity, and worth.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you show sincere love today before continuing.

pages.q: Owe no man any thing, but to love one another: for he that loveth another hath fulfilled the law.

pages.prompt: How will you show love through your actions today?

o.l: I will give someone my patient attention.
o.r: Put aside distractions and listen sincerely. Attention can be a meaningful expression of care.

o.l: I will do something helpful without waiting to be asked.
o.r: Look for a need you can meet in a simple way. Let your care become visible through useful action.

o.l: I will speak with greater warmth to someone close to me.
o.r: Familiar relationships can sometimes receive less careful speech. Choose words that communicate respect and appreciation.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another sincere way to show love. Ask God to help you recognize how someone near you may need care today.

p: Love becomes stronger when it is expressed. Simple actions can communicate care more clearly than good intentions left unspoken.
In 1 John 3:18 we read: “My little children, let us not love in word, neither in tongue.”
Let one person experience your sincere care today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 1 John 3:18
Show love today in one practical way, not only in words.

pages.q: Love becomes visible when sincere care leads us to action.

226.pq: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness…

p: Some blessings are so familiar that we stop noticing them.
Daily provision, strength, opportunities, and the people who help us can all remind us that good gifts are present in our lives.
Take a moment to pray and thank God for something good before continuing.

pages.q: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.

pages.prompt: What will you do to notice God's good gifts today?

o.l: I will thank God for one ordinary blessing.
o.r: Choose something you often take for granted. Express gratitude specifically rather than only giving a general thank you.

o.l: I will recognize the good someone else has done for me.
o.r: Many blessings come through people. Take time to acknowledge someone whose effort has helped or strengthened you.

o.l: I will notice something good that happened today.
o.r: At the end of the day, pause and remember one good moment. This practice can help you become more aware of blessings that might otherwise be forgotten.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to recognize the good in your life. Ask God to help you see blessings that familiarity may have hidden from your attention.

p: Gratitude becomes deeper when we notice specific gifts. Many good things become more meaningful when we stop and recognize them.
In Psalm 103:2 we read: “Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits.”
Take time today to notice and thank God for something good.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Psalm 103:2
Write three things you received today that you did not earn. Thank God.

pages.q: A blessing often becomes more meaningful when we stop long enough to notice it.

227.pq: Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself.

p: Worry often borrows trouble from a day that has not yet arrived.
Christ invites us to trust Him fully enough that we do not have to carry tomorrow's burdens today.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you release worry into faith before continuing.

pages.q: Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself.

pages.prompt: What worry could you exchange for faith today?

o.l: I will focus on what I can do today, not the whole future.
o.r: You do not need a plan for every future scenario right now. Give your full attention to today's responsibilities and trust tomorrow to God.

o.l: I will bring a specific worry honestly to God.
o.r: Name the worry plainly in prayer instead of carrying it silently. Ask God for the peace that comes from placing it in His hands.

o.l: I will remind myself that God has cared for me before.
o.r: Look back at a past worry that eventually resolved. Let that memory strengthen your trust in what lies ahead now.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another honest way to exchange worry for faith today. Ask God to help you trust Him one day at a time.

p: Faith does not remove every uncertainty about the future. It simply trusts that God is already there, waiting.
In Luke 12:22 we read: “And he said unto his disciples, Therefore I say unto you, Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat.”
Give today's worry to God, and let tomorrow wait for tomorrow.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Luke 12:22
Write tomorrow's worry. Then write one thing you can do about today.

pages.q: Worry borrows trouble from a day that has not yet arrived.

228.theme: Not Growing Weary in Well Doing
228.pq: And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.

p: Doing good can sometimes feel tiring, especially when results are slow.
Not every good effort produces an immediate reward, but faithful effort can still be meaningful and valuable.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to strengthen you when doing good feels difficult before continuing.

pages.q: And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.

pages.prompt: How will you continue doing good when you feel tired?

o.l: I will take one small step instead of giving up completely.
o.r: You may not have strength for everything at once. Do the good you can do now and allow small progress to continue.

o.l: I will remember why this good effort matters.
o.r: Reconnect with the purpose behind what you are doing. Meaning can strengthen our willingness to continue.

o.l: I will ask for appropriate help instead of carrying everything alone.
o.r: Some burdens are too heavy to manage without support. Seeking help can make continued effort more sustainable.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another healthy way to continue in doing good. Ask God to renew your strength and help you avoid becoming discouraged.

p: Steady goodness can require patience. Even when results are not immediately visible, the effort to do what is right still shapes us.
In 2 Thessalonians 3:13 we read: “But ye, brethren, be not weary in well doing.”
Do not give up on one good thing that still deserves your effort.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 2 Thessalonians 3:13
Do one good thing today that you feel tired of doing. Keep going.

pages.q: When good results are slow, steady effort can still be worth continuing.

229.pq: And he said unto them, Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while:

p: There are times when continued activity can leave us physically, mentally, or spiritually tired.
Rest can help us recover and return to our responsibilities with greater strength and clarity.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you recognize when healthy rest is needed before continuing.

pages.q: And he said unto them, Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while:

pages.prompt: How will you make room for healthy rest today?

o.l: I will take a short break from unnecessary activity.
o.r: Step away from something that is not urgently required. Use the time to become calm, quiet, and refreshed.

o.l: I will set a healthier boundary around my time.
o.r: You do not have to accept every demand on your attention. Consider what can wait so you can care for necessary responsibilities and recovery.

o.l: I will use part of my rest to draw closer to God.
o.r: Rest can include quiet spiritual renewal. Spend a few moments praying, reading scripture, or simply becoming still before God.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another healthy way to rest and recover. Ask God to help you balance sincere effort with the renewal you need.

p: Rest is not always the same as avoiding responsibility. Wise rest can prepare us to return to our responsibilities with greater strength.
In Exodus 33:14 we read: “And he said, My presence shall go with thee, and I will give thee rest.”
Make room today for the kind of renewal you genuinely need.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Exodus 33:14
Take a short rest today without guilt. Thank God for it.

pages.q: Healthy rest can help us return to what matters with greater strength and clarity.

230.pq: Rejoice with them that do rejoice, and weep with them that weep.

p: Love helps us care about what others are experiencing.
We can learn to celebrate another person's good news without envy and offer sincere comfort when they are hurting.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you care more deeply about others before continuing.

pages.q: Rejoice with them that do rejoice, and weep with them that weep.

pages.prompt: How will you better share in another person's experience today?

o.l: I will sincerely celebrate someone's good news.
o.r: Let another person's success be a reason for genuine joy. Offer congratulations without comparing their blessing to your own situation.

o.l: I will sit with someone who is going through something difficult.
o.r: You may not have the perfect answer. Your sincere presence and willingness to listen can still communicate care.

o.l: I will stop comparing another person's life with mine.
o.r: Comparison can make it difficult to rejoice with others. Return your attention to gratitude for your own life while allowing others to have their moment of joy.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to show sincere concern for another person's experiences. Ask God to help you become less focused on yourself and more aware of others.

p: We do not have to experience exactly what another person is experiencing in order to care. Love allows us to make room for both another person's joy and another person's pain.
In 1 Corinthians 12:26 we read: “And whether one member suffer, all the members suffer with it.”
Share sincerely in someone's experience today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 1 Corinthians 12:26
Celebrate someone else's good news today and mean it.

pages.q: Love makes room in our hearts for another person's joy and another person's pain.

231.pq: I love them that love me; and those that seek me early shall find me.

p: God invites us to seek Him. He does not ask us to wait until life becomes difficult before turning to Him.
Seeking God early can mean giving Him a place at the beginning of our day, our decisions, and our plans.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: I love them that love me; and those that seek me early shall find me.

pages.prompt: When can you make a more deliberate effort to seek God?

o.l: At the beginning of each day
o.r: Beginning your day with God can help you remember what matters most. Even a short moment of prayer or scripture can help you start with greater purpose.

o.l: Before making important decisions
o.r: Seeking God before important decisions shows that you want His guidance. Take time to pray, think, and act according to what you know is right.

o.l: Whenever I feel spiritually distant
o.r: You do not have to remain distant from God. When you notice that distance, choose one simple action that helps you turn your heart back to Him.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another specific time to seek God more intentionally. What matters is not copying someone else's pattern, but sincerely making room for Him in your life.

p: God can be sought at any time, but we are blessed when we choose to seek Him willingly and consistently.
In Jeremiah 29:12-13 we read: “Then shall ye call upon me, and ye shall go and pray unto me, and I will hearken unto you.”
Today, make a place for God before other things begin to demand your attention.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Jeremiah 29:12-13
Pray first thing tomorrow morning. Ask God to guide your day.

pages.q: Seek God deliberately. A willing heart can begin to find Him in every part of life.

232.pq: For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them.

p: Your life has purpose. God has given you opportunities to do good in ways that may bless people around you.
Good works do not always need to be large or public. Many begin with simple choices made faithfully.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them.

pages.prompt: What good work can you choose more intentionally today?

o.l: Help someone with a practical need
o.r: Look for a real need you can help meet. Your assistance may be simple, but it can make another person's burden easier.

o.l: Do my responsibilities more faithfully
o.r: Faithful work is also a form of goodness. Give honest effort to the responsibilities already placed before you.

o.l: Encourage someone who may need strength
o.r: A sincere word can help someone continue when they feel discouraged. Think of one person and offer specific encouragement.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another good work that fits your circumstances. Ask yourself what loving action you can actually complete today.

p: You were not created without purpose. God can work through your willing efforts to bring good into the lives of others.
In Titus 3:8 we read: “This is a faithful saying, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly, that they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works.”
Do not wait for a perfect opportunity. Walk in the good you are able to do now.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Titus 3:8
Do one good work today that you were made to do.

pages.q: A life of purpose is built through many willing acts of good.

233.pq: Rooted and built up in him, and stablished in the faith, as ye have been taught, abounding therein with thanksgiving.

p: A strong life needs a strong foundation. Jesus Christ can become the center that helps us remain steady.
Being rooted in Him takes time. It grows as we learn, obey, remember, and continue to trust Him.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: Rooted and built up in him, and stablished in the faith, as ye have been taught, abounding therein with thanksgiving.

pages.prompt: What can help you become more firmly rooted in Christ?

o.l: Remember what He has already done for me
o.r: Remembering the Savior can strengthen your faith during uncertain times. Write down one blessing or spiritual experience that helps you remember Him.

o.l: Be more consistent in my daily discipleship
o.r: Consistency strengthens spiritual roots. Choose one small practice you can do faithfully rather than waiting to do everything perfectly.

o.l: Trust Him when I do not understand everything
o.r: You may not have every answer today. You can still remain close to Christ and trust Him while understanding comes gradually.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another action that helps Christ become more central in your life. Let it be specific enough that you can begin today.

p: When Christ is at the center of our lives, we can continue forward even when circumstances change.
In Ephesians 3:17 we read: “That Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith; that ye, being rooted and grounded in love.”
Build your life in Him one faithful choice at a time.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Ephesians 3:17
Write what keeps you rooted in Christ. Do one thing to deepen it.

pages.q: The closer your life is built around Christ, the stronger your foundation can become.

234.pq: Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.

p: We do not need to know everything already. Wisdom often grows when we are willing to listen and learn.
Good instruction can sometimes correct us. A humble heart can receive needed guidance without losing hope.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.

pages.prompt: How can you better receive helpful instruction?

o.l: Listen without becoming defensive
o.r: Try to understand what is being said before responding. You may discover something useful when you give counsel an honest hearing.

o.l: Consider what I can learn from correction
o.r: Correction can show you where growth is needed. Instead of focusing only on discomfort, look for one truth you can use.

o.l: Ask for guidance when I need it
o.r: Asking for guidance is a sign of willingness to grow. Seek help from trustworthy sources and then carefully consider what you learn.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to become more teachable. A desire to learn can prepare you for wisdom that comes over time.

p: Wise people continue learning. They do not believe that growth has ended because they have already gained some experience.
In Proverbs 12:15 we read: “The way of a fool is right in his own eyes: but he that hearkeneth unto counsel is wise.”
Today, let one piece of good instruction help you move forward.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Proverbs 12:15
Ask for instruction on something you want to learn. Take notes.

pages.q: A willing heart can turn instruction into greater wisdom.

235.pq: Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it.

p: Sometimes the question is not whether we know what is right. The greater question is whether we are willing to act on what we know.
Knowledge becomes more meaningful when it changes our choices. Small acts of obedience can strengthen our character.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it.

pages.prompt: What good thing do you already know you should do?

o.l: Take care of a responsibility I have delayed
o.r: Choose one responsibility you have been putting aside and begin it today. Starting may be more important than completing everything at once.

o.l: Make something right with another person
o.r: If you know a relationship needs attention, take a sincere step toward making things better. Begin with honesty and respect.

o.l: Stop doing something I know is wrong
o.r: Recognizing a wrong pattern is an important beginning. Take one clear action that creates distance between you and that choice.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Think honestly about what God has already helped you understand. Choose one good action and do not delay it without reason.

p: We grow when truth moves from our minds into our actions.
In Luke 12:47 we read: “And that servant, which knew his lord's will, and prepared not himself, neither did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes.”
Do one good thing you already know should be done.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Luke 12:47
Think of something you already know is right. Do it today.

pages.q: Knowing what is right is a beginning. Choosing to do it is the next step.

236.theme: The Value of a Good Name
236.pq: A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold.

p: What people know you for matters more than what you own.
A good name is not built in a single moment. It is built quietly, choice by choice, over years.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you build a name worth having before continuing.

pages.q: A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold.

pages.prompt: What is one way you could strengthen your own good name today?

o.l: I will follow through on something small so my word means something.
o.r: A reputation is built on small, kept promises more than grand gestures. Follow through today on something easy to overlook.

o.l: I will act the same in private as I do in public.
o.r: A good name that only exists in public is not a good name at all. Let your private choices match what people see.

o.l: I will treat someone well even when it costs me nothing to be noticed.
o.r: Real character often shows itself precisely when no one is watching. Choose kindness today, even unseen.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another honest way to build a name worth trusting. Ask God to help your reputation reflect who you actually are.

p: Wealth can be lost overnight. A good name, carefully built, tends to last far longer.
In Ecclesiastes 7:1 we read: “A good name is better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one's birth.”
Guard yours today with the same care you would guard anything truly valuable.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Ecclesiastes 7:1
Do one thing today that you would want your name to stand for.

pages.q: A good name is not inherited. It is built, one honest choice at a time.

237.pq: I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help.

p: There are times when our own strength feels limited. In those moments, we can remember that we are not required to face life alone.
Looking to God does not mean refusing to act. It means acting while trusting that His help is greater than our limitations.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help.

pages.prompt: Where do you most need God's help right now?

o.l: In a difficult decision
o.r: Bring the decision honestly to God. Study what you can, consider your choices, and seek help as you move forward.

o.l: In carrying a personal burden
o.r: You do not need to pretend that the burden is easy. Tell God honestly what you are carrying and ask for strength for the next step.

o.l: In becoming a better person
o.r: Real change can require more than determination alone. Ask God to help you recognize where growth is needed and give you strength to continue.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Name another area where you need divine help. Then pray specifically instead of leaving your need only as a general thought.

p: God's help may come through strength, guidance, comfort, opportunities, or people who assist us.
In Psalm 46:1 we read: “God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.”
Lift your heart to Him and continue with faith.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Psalm 46:1
When worry comes today, pause and ask God for help. Then wait.

pages.q: When your strength feels limited, you can still look to God for help.

238.pq: Buy the truth, and sell it not; also wisdom, and instruction, and understanding.

p: Truth is worth seeking and keeping. It can guide us even when a different path appears easier.
Living in truth requires more than recognizing facts. It also requires refusing to trade what is right for temporary advantage.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: Buy the truth, and sell it not; also wisdom, and instruction, and understanding.

pages.prompt: How can you hold more firmly to truth?

o.l: Choose truth even when it costs me something
o.r: Doing what is right may sometimes require sacrifice. Remember that temporary convenience is not worth losing your integrity.

o.l: Keep learning what is true
o.r: Continue seeking greater understanding. A sincere learner is willing to examine, study, and receive truth.

o.l: Stop repeating things I do not know are true
o.r: Be careful with information before sharing it. Choosing accuracy shows respect for truth and for the people who hear you.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to show that truth matters to you. Let your decision strengthen both your understanding and your actions.

p: Truth deserves more than temporary interest. It deserves a place in the way we live and make decisions.
In 3 John 1:4 we read: “I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth.”
Hold on to what is true, and continue seeking greater light and understanding.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 3 John 1:4
Say only what is true today. Ask yourself before you speak.

pages.q: Do not trade lasting truth for temporary advantage.

239.pq: Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit.

p: God does not force us to become better. He invites us to have willing hearts.
A willing spirit can turn toward God again, even after weakness, mistakes, or discouragement.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit.

pages.prompt: What would show God that your heart is willing?

o.l: Accept a needed change
o.r: Change can feel difficult even when it is good. Ask God to help you become willing to take the next right step.

o.l: Let go of an excuse
o.r: An excuse may explain why something is difficult, but it does not always need to decide what you do next. Choose responsibility where you are able.

o.l: Respond more quickly when I know what is right
o.r: You do not need to wait until you feel completely ready. A willing heart often begins by acting on the good already understood.

o.l: I can do something else
