o.r: Think of another way you can show greater willingness. Offer that decision sincerely to God and begin where you are.

p: God can work with a willing heart. We do not need to be perfect before choosing to turn toward Him.
In Mosiah 3:19 we read: “For the natural man is an enemy to God, and has been from the fall of Adam, and will be, forever and ever, unless he yields to the enticings of the Holy Spirit.”
Today, replace resistance with one sincere act of willingness.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Mosiah 3:19
Offer God a willing spirit today. Say yes to one small request.

pages.q: A willing heart can begin changing before every difficulty has disappeared.

240.pq: And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye thankful.

p: Gratitude does not require us to call every difficult experience good. It invites us to notice that blessings can still exist in difficult seasons.
A thankful response can change what we choose to focus on. It helps us remember gifts that might otherwise be overlooked.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye thankful.

pages.prompt: What can you choose to give thanks for today?

o.l: A person who has blessed my life
o.r: Think of the person specifically and consider telling them. Gratitude becomes more meaningful when it is expressed.

o.l: A simple need that has been provided
o.r: Daily provision can become easy to overlook because it is familiar. Pause and recognize one ordinary blessing that supports your life.

o.l: A lesson I learned through difficulty
o.r: You do not need to be thankful for pain itself to recognize growth that came through it. Notice one lesson that has made you wiser or stronger.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another blessing that is meaningful to you today. Name it clearly and offer sincere thanks to God.

p: Gratitude can be practiced in ordinary moments as well as special ones.
In Psalm 107:1 we read: “O give thanks unto the LORD, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.”
Today, notice what is good and give thanks for it.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Psalm 107:1
Choose to thank someone today when you would normally complain.

pages.q: Gratitude helps us notice blessings that familiarity can hide.

241.pq: So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.

p: Life can become centered on gaining things that cannot last. Jesus Christ taught us to think about what has greater and lasting value.
Being rich toward God includes the way we use our time, abilities, resources, and attention.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.

pages.prompt: What can help you place greater value on what matters eternally?

o.l: Give more attention to my relationship with God
o.r: Relationships grow through time and sincere attention. Choose a moment today to turn toward God without treating it as an afterthought.

o.l: Use what I have to bless someone
o.r: Your resources include more than money. Consider how your time, skills, experience, or possessions could help another person.

o.l: Reduce my focus on things that do not last
o.r: Examine what receives too much of your attention. You may not need to remove everything, but you can place temporary things in a healthier position.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to invest in what has lasting value. Let your decision reflect what you truly want your life to become.

p: What we value shapes how we spend our lives. Jesus Christ invites us to consider treasures that reach beyond temporary possessions.
In 1 Timothy 6:17 we read: “Charge them that are rich in this world, that they be not highminded, nor trust in uncertain riches, but in the living God, who giveth us richly all things to enjoy.”
Choose one way today to become richer toward God.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 1 Timothy 6:17
Give one thing today to God or to someone in need.

pages.q: Give lasting things a lasting place in your life.

242.pq: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith:

p: Starting is important, but faithfulness also means continuing. Some worthwhile things require patience long after the first excitement is gone.
Finishing well does not mean every step was perfect. It means we continue to return to what is right.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith:

pages.prompt: What do you need to continue faithfully?

o.l: A responsibility that has become difficult
o.r: Break the responsibility into a smaller next step. You may not be able to complete everything today, but you can continue.

o.l: A good habit I want to maintain
o.r: Protect the habit through consistency. Make it simple enough that you can continue even on busy or difficult days.

o.l: A spiritual goal that takes time
o.r: Spiritual growth is often gradual. Keep moving toward your goal and do not reject progress because it seems small.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another worthwhile commitment that needs your continued effort. Decide what the next faithful step will be.

p: A meaningful life is often built through continued effort. We learn to endure by taking the next step again and again.
In Hebrews 12:1-2 we read: “Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us.”
Do not let a difficult middle prevent you from continuing toward a good ending.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Hebrews 12:1-2
Think about how you want to finish this year. Take one step toward it.

pages.q: You do not need a perfect journey to continue faithfully toward a good finish.

243.pq: The light of the eyes rejoiceth the heart: and a good report maketh the bones fat.

p: The quality of our effort can reflect the kind of person we are becoming. Even ordinary work can be done with honesty and care.
Doing something heartily does not mean exhausting yourself without wisdom. It means giving sincere effort to what is rightfully yours to do.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: The light of the eyes rejoiceth the heart: and a good report maketh the bones fat.

pages.prompt: Where can you give more sincere effort today?

o.l: In my work or studies
o.r: Give your attention to the task in front of you. Focus on doing it well rather than only doing enough to finish.

o.l: In caring for my home or responsibilities
o.r: Ordinary responsibilities still matter. Do one needed task with care and remember that faithfulness is often shown in simple things.

o.l: In my service to others
o.r: Serve with genuine concern rather than only performing an obligation. Consider what would truly help the person you are serving.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another area where your effort has become careless or divided. Give that responsibility your honest attention today.

p: Sincere effort can give ordinary work greater meaning. We can choose to act with care even when no one is watching.
In Proverbs 25:25 we read: “As cold waters to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country.”
Today, do one thing wholeheartedly.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Proverbs 25:25
Share one piece of good news today with someone.

pages.q: Give sincere effort to the good work that is yours to do.

244.pq: Ye shall do no unrighteousness in judgment: thou shalt not respect the person of the poor, nor honour the person of the mighty.

p: It is easy to treat people differently because of appearance, position, wealth, education, or influence. The gospel calls us to see people with greater fairness.
Every person is a child of God. Respect should not depend on what someone can offer us.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: Ye shall do no unrighteousness in judgment: thou shalt not respect the person of the poor, nor honour the person of the mighty.

pages.prompt: How can you treat people with greater fairness?

o.l: Give the same respect to people who cannot help me
o.r: Notice how you treat people when there is nothing to gain. Choose respect because of their worth, not because of their usefulness to you.

o.l: Listen to people I might normally overlook
o.r: Make room for someone whose voice is not often heard. Listening can help you recognize experiences and needs you did not understand before.

o.l: Examine my assumptions about others
o.r: Assumptions can affect how we speak and act without us noticing. Pause before judging someone based on limited information.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to show equal respect. Let your actions reflect the truth that every soul has worth before God.

p: The way we treat people reveals what we value. Christlike respect reaches beyond status and outward appearance.
In James 2:9 we read: “But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors.”
Today, choose fairness in one real interaction.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in James 2:9
Treat everyone you meet today the same, with respect and kindness.

pages.q: Treat people with respect because of their worth, not because of their position.

245.pq: But covet earnestly the best gifts: and yet shew I unto you a more excellent way.

p: What we repeatedly give our attention to can influence our thoughts, desires, and actions. God invites us to seek what is good and worthy.
This does not mean pretending that problems do not exist. It means choosing not to fill our minds unnecessarily with what pulls us away from truth and goodness.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: But covet earnestly the best gifts: and yet shew I unto you a more excellent way.

pages.prompt: What can you give more attention to today?

o.l: Something true and worth learning
o.r: Choose something that increases your understanding and helps you grow. Give focused attention instead of allowing constant distraction.

o.l: Something pure and uplifting
o.r: Select influences that leave your mind in a better condition. Pay attention to how what you consume affects your thoughts afterward.

o.l: Something good I can appreciate
o.r: Look for goodness already present around you. Appreciating what is good can help you develop a more grateful and hopeful mind.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another worthy focus for your thoughts. Ask whether it will help you become more truthful, pure, just, and good.

p: We cannot always control the first thought that enters our minds, but we can make choices about what we continue to welcome and feed.
In Philippians 1:10 we read: “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere and without offence till the day of Christ.”
Today, intentionally give your attention to something worthy of your mind.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Philippians 1:10
Choose one thing that is excellent to learn or do today.

pages.q: Give your mind more of what helps you become good.

246.pq: See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise,

p: Life is shaped by many choices that can seem small at the moment. Wisdom helps us consider where those choices are leading.
Living with purpose means paying attention to the direction of our lives instead of moving forward without thought.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise,

pages.prompt: Where do you need to be more intentional?

o.l: In the way I use my time
o.r: Look at one part of your day that often disappears without purpose. Make a simple plan for using some of that time more wisely.

o.l: In the influences I allow
o.r: What you repeatedly allow around you can shape your thinking. Choose one influence to reduce and one better influence to increase.

o.l: In the direction of my personal goals
o.r: Ask whether your current habits support the future you hope to build. Adjust one habit so your daily life better matches your purpose.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another area where you have been acting without enough thought. Take one deliberate step toward a better direction.

p: Wisdom helps us live with greater awareness. We do not need to control every detail of life to choose our direction carefully.
In Proverbs 4:26-27 we read: “Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy ways be established.”
Today, make one intentional choice that supports the person you want to become.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Proverbs 4:26-27
Write what you want your life to stand for. Take one step toward it.

pages.q: Purpose grows when daily choices begin to match what matters most.

247.pq: Recompense to no man evil for evil. Provide things honest in the sight of all men.

p: When someone treats us badly, the desire to respond in the same way can be strong. The gospel teaches a better pattern.
Choosing not to return evil for evil does not mean approving of wrongdoing. It means refusing to let another person's wrong choice decide your own character.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: Recompense to no man evil for evil. Provide things honest in the sight of all men.

pages.prompt: How can you respond better when someone treats you unfairly?

o.l: Pause before I react
o.r: Give yourself time before responding. A short pause can prevent words or actions that create greater harm.

o.l: Speak honestly without trying to hurt back
o.r: You can address a problem clearly without becoming cruel. Focus on truth and respect rather than revenge.

o.l: Leave justice to proper and righteous means
o.r: Not every wrong must be answered personally. When action is needed, seek fair and appropriate ways to address the situation.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another response that keeps you from returning wrong with more wrong. Let your character remain under your own control.

p: Another person's choices do not have to determine yours. You can remain committed to what is right even when you have been treated unfairly.
In 1 Peter 3:9 we read: “Not rendering evil for evil, or railing for railing.”
Today, choose a response you can respect afterward.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 1 Peter 3:9
When you are wronged today, answer with kindness instead of payback.

pages.q: Do not allow another person's wrong choice to decide your character.

248.pq: Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things, which thou knowest not.

p: God invites us to seek. He wants us to bring our questions, needs, and desires to Him.
Seeking often requires more than one moment. We may need to ask, study, act, and continue patiently.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things, which thou knowest not.

pages.prompt: What do you need to seek more earnestly?

o.l: Greater understanding
o.r: Ask a sincere question and then study carefully. Be willing to learn gradually rather than demanding every answer immediately.

o.l: Help with a personal need
o.r: Tell God clearly what you need. Then remain open to help that may come in ways you did not expect.

o.l: Direction for my next step
o.r: You may not receive a complete plan for your future all at once. Seek enough light to recognize and take the next right step.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Name another thing you need to seek. Ask sincerely, do what you can, and remain willing to continue the search.

p: God's invitation to ask is also an invitation to act. Seeking can involve prayer, study, listening, and faithful effort.
In Luke 11:9 we read: “And I say unto you, Ask, and it shall be given you.”
Do not leave an important spiritual question only in your thoughts. Bring it sincerely to God.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Luke 11:9
Ask God one question today. Write the first thought that comes.

pages.q: A sincere question can become the beginning of a deeper search for truth.

249.pq: Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise: and he that shutteth his lips is esteemed a man of understanding.

p: Not every thought needs to be spoken out loud.
Sometimes the wisest thing you can say is nothing at all, at least not yet.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you know when silence serves better than speech.

pages.q: Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise: and he that shutteth his lips is esteemed a man of understanding.

pages.prompt: Where could choosing silence serve you better today?

o.l: I will pause instead of responding to criticism right away.
o.r: A quick reply to criticism rarely helps. Give yourself time before you respond, if you respond at all.

o.l: I will keep a private struggle between myself and God for now.
o.r: Not everything needs an audience. Some things are meant to be worked through quietly, in prayer, before anywhere else.

o.l: I will let an unnecessary comment go unsaid.
o.r: Notice the comment that doesn't actually need to be made today, and simply let it pass.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to practice restraint today. Ask God to help you know the difference between silence that serves and silence that avoids.

p: Silence is not the same as weakness. Sometimes it is simply wisdom, choosing not to add noise to a moment that doesn't need it.
In Ecclesiastes 3:7 we read: “A time to rend, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak.”
Notice today when holding your peace serves better than filling it.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Ecclesiastes 3:7
Spend ten minutes in silence today. Notice what you hear.

pages.q: Sometimes the wisest words are the ones never spoken.

250.theme: The Danger of a Hasty Word
250.pq: Seest thou a man that is hasty in his words? there is more hope of a fool than of him.

p: Words spoken too quickly are hard to take back.
A hasty word often says more about your own impatience than about the situation in front of you.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you slow down before you speak today.

pages.q: Seest thou a man that is hasty in his words? there is more hope of a fool than of him.

pages.prompt: Where could slowing down your words help you today?

o.l: I will think before I answer a difficult question.
o.r: Give yourself a moment before responding, especially when a question catches you off guard. A slower answer is often a better one.

o.l: I will avoid replying to something in anger right now.
o.r: Words sent in anger are rarely words you're glad you sent. Wait until the heat has passed before you respond.

o.l: I will choose my words carefully in a hard conversation.
o.r: A hard conversation deserves careful words, not the first ones that come to mind. Slow down and choose them with care.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose another way to slow your words down today. Ask God to help you speak thoughtfully, not hastily.

p: A hasty word can undo in a moment what patience took years to build.
In Proverbs 15:28 we read: “The heart of the righteous studieth to answer: but the mouth of the wicked poureth out evil things.”
Choose today to let your words be slower than your feelings.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Proverbs 15:28
Before speaking in a heated moment today, wait ten seconds.

pages.q: A hasty word can undo in a moment what patience took years to build.

251.pq: But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

p: God did not wait for you to become worthy before He loved you.
His love was proven before you ever asked for it, while you were still far from Him.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you trust a love that came first, before you deserved it.

pages.q: But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

pages.prompt: How could trusting God's love more fully change something today?

o.l: I can stop trying to earn love that was already given.
o.r: You do not need to earn what God already gave freely. Rest today in a love that came before any effort of yours.

o.l: I can trust Him even in a season that feels distant.
o.r: Distance in feeling does not mean distance in fact. Trust today that His love reaches exactly where you are.

o.l: I can extend that same first-love to someone else.
o.r: Love someone today before they've earned it, the same way God loved you first.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However you respond to God's love today, let it be with real trust, not earned worthiness.

p: This is not a love that waited for you to clean yourself up first.
In Romans 8:38 we read: “For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come.”
It arrived while you were still in the middle of everything, and it has not changed since.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Romans 8:38
Write one way God has shown love to you. Say thank you in prayer.

pages.q: His love came first, before you ever asked for it.

252.pq: The secret of the LORD is with them that fear him; and he will shew them his covenant.

p: There is a kind of closeness with God that only comes through genuine reverence.
It is not about secrecy for its own sake, but about the quiet trust shared between friends.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to draw you into that closer friendship today.

pages.q: The secret of the LORD is with them that fear him; and he will shew them his covenant.

pages.prompt: How could you draw closer to this kind of friendship with God today?

o.l: I can approach Him with more reverence in prayer.
o.r: Real friendship with God begins with real reverence. Bring that today, not just routine words.

o.l: I can trust Him with something private I've been carrying alone.
o.r: Bring the private thing to Him today. He is not a stranger to what you carry quietly.

o.l: I can spend unhurried time simply being near Him.
o.r: Friendship needs time, not just requests. Spend a few unhurried minutes with Him today.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However closeness with God grows today, remember it deepens through reverence, not distance.

p: This kind of closeness is not reserved for a select few.
In John 15:15 we read: “Henceforth I call you not servants; for the servant knoweth not what his lord doeth.”
It is offered to anyone willing to approach Him with real reverence and real trust.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in John 15:15
Take time today to talk with God as with a trusted friend.

pages.q: Reverence opens a door that casualness never finds.

253.pq: This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.

p: Every morning is a fresh gift from God.
It is easy to look past today while worrying about tomorrow, but today has its own purpose.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.

pages.prompt: How can you receive today as a gift instead of just another day to get through?

o.l: I can look for one good thing in this day
o.r: Even on a difficult day, there is usually something good waiting to be noticed. Choose to look for it, and let it be your anchor for the rest of the day.

o.l: I can live this day with intention
o.r: Instead of drifting through the hours, decide now to bring your full attention to what is in front of you. One intentional choice can change the entire direction of your day.

o.l: I can thank God for being here, right now
o.r: Gratitude for the present moment can shift your whole perspective. Thank God for this breath, this hour, this ordinary moment, and see how your heart begins to change.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose a simple way to honor the day you have been given. Today will not come again, so receive it with both hands and an open heart.

p: Yesterday is already gone, and tomorrow is not promised. What you have is today.
In Lamentations 3:22-23 we read: “It is of the LORD's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.”
Do not waste it. Receive it, fully, as the gift it truly is.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Lamentations 3:22-23
Start today with a short prayer of thanks. Notice one good thing.

pages.q: Today is a gift from God. Open it with gratitude.

254.pq: Thou shalt not go up and down as a talebearer among thy people.

p: Words spoken about someone who is not present can cause lasting harm.
Gossip often begins with a small comment, but it can grow into something that damages trust and reputation.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: Thou shalt not go up and down as a talebearer among thy people.

pages.prompt: What can you do when you are tempted to share something that is not yours to tell?

o.l: I can stop before I repeat it
o.r: Pause and ask yourself: does this need to be said? Does it need to be said by me? Does it need to be said right now? A simple pause can prevent a mistake you cannot take back.

o.l: I can change the subject away from someone else
o.r: When conversation turns toward gossip, you have the power to steer it somewhere else. You can protect someone's reputation simply by refusing to participate.

o.l: I can protect the person being spoken about
o.r: A kind word in defense of someone who is not present shows real character. You can gently remind others that you do not know the whole story.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose a way to withdraw from the conversation without making others defensive. Your silence on the matter is a powerful statement of integrity.

p: Your words are powerful. They can build up or tear down, and what you say about others says more about you than about them.
In Proverbs 20:19 we read: “He that goeth about as a talebearer revealeth secrets.”
Choose to protect, not expose. Choose to build, not break.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Proverbs 20:19
When gossip starts today, change the subject or stay quiet.

pages.q: A gossiping tongue reveals more about the speaker than the subject.

255.pq: Better is an handful with quietness, than both the hands full with travail and vexation of spirit.

p: More is not always better. Sometimes less, held peacefully, is worth more than plenty held anxiously.
A quiet handful can be richer than two hands full of striving.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you notice the peace already in your hands today.

pages.q: Better is an handful with quietness, than both the hands full with travail and vexation of spirit.

pages.prompt: Where could quietness serve you better than more striving today?

o.l: I can stop chasing more and notice what I already have.
o.r: Pause today and notice the handful already in front of you, instead of reaching for a second one.

o.l: I can choose rest over one more task today.
o.r: Not every task needs to be finished today. Choose rest where striving would only add vexation.

o.l: I can simplify something that has grown too complicated.
o.r: Look at what's grown overly complicated, and simplify it today, even in a small way.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However quietness shows up today, remember a peaceful handful can outweigh two anxious ones.

p: Striving for more can quietly cost you the peace you already had.
In Philippians 4:11-12 we read: “Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.”
Today, notice what a little, held calmly, is actually worth.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Philippians 4:11-12
Choose one simple, quiet joy today. Enjoy it fully.

pages.q: A quiet handful is worth more than two hands full of striving.

256.theme: The Value of a Quiet Spirit
256.pq: The ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price.

p: A quiet spirit is not a weak spirit.
It takes strength to remain calm in a world that constantly shouts for attention.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: The ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price.

pages.prompt: Where could a quieter spirit serve you better today?

o.l: I can speak less and listen more
o.r: You do not always need to fill the silence with words. Sometimes the most powerful thing you can do is simply listen and let the other person be heard.

o.l: I can respond with calm instead of reacting with emotion
o.r: A reaction often comes from impulse. A response comes from thought. Take a breath before you answer, and let calm guide your next word.

o.l: I can find peace in a moment of stillness
o.r: Stillness can feel uncomfortable at first, but it is often where God speaks most clearly. Allow yourself to sit quietly and simply be present.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose a way to bring more quiet into your spirit today. A little less noise, a little more peace. That is a treasure worth seeking.

p: You do not have to be the loudest voice in the room to make a difference.
In Psalm 46:10 we read: “Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth.”
A quiet spirit, rooted in faith, carries a weight that no amount of noise can match.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Psalm 46:10
Spend five minutes today in a quiet, peaceful spirit.

pages.q: A quiet spirit is not weakness. It is strength that does not need to prove itself.

257.pq: Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and steadfast.

p: Life can feel like a storm. Circumstances shift, plans change, and uncertainty can feel overwhelming.
Hope is the anchor that keeps you steady when everything else is moving.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and steadfast.

pages.prompt: Where do you need hope to hold you steady right now?

o.l: I can hold onto hope in a situation I cannot control
o.r: You cannot control every outcome. But you can choose to keep hoping, not because you know how it will end, but because you trust the One who does.

o.l: I can trust that God is still working even when I cannot see it
o.r: Sometimes the most important work is happening beneath the surface. God does not stop moving just because you cannot see the movement.

o.l: I can refuse to give up on something that still matters
o.r: There is a difference between accepting reality and giving up on hope. You can accept where you are without abandoning faith that things can change.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose to place your hope in something solid today. Not in circumstances that change, but in the God who never changes.

p: Hope is not naive optimism. It is trusting that God is still at work, even in the middle of what feels unfinished.
In Romans 15:13 we read: “Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.”
Let hope anchor you today. It is sure. It is steadfast. And it will not let go.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Romans 15:13
Write one hope that anchors you. Read it when you feel unsteady.

pages.q: Hope does not change your circumstances, but it changes how you face them.

258.pq: By long forbearing is a prince persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone.

p: Patience and gentle words can accomplish what force and pressure never manage to.
A carefully chosen word, given time, can move even the most stubborn resistance.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you choose patience over pressure today.

pages.q: By long forbearing is a prince persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone.

pages.prompt: Where could patience and gentle words serve you better than pressure today?

o.l: I can wait patiently instead of pushing for an immediate answer.
o.r: Some things cannot be rushed. Practice patience today instead of pressing for a quicker resolution.

o.l: I can soften my tone in a difficult conversation.
o.r: A softer tone today might accomplish what force could not. Choose gentleness in the hard conversation ahead.

o.l: I can trust that persistence, not force, will make the difference.
o.r: Keep going gently today, trusting that steady patience often outlasts forceful pressure.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However patience shows up in your words today, remember gentleness can accomplish what force cannot.

p: Force rarely changes a mind. Patience, given time, often does.
In Proverbs 15:1 we read: “A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.”
Choose the soft tongue today, and trust it to do its slow, real work.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Proverbs 15:1
Choose your words carefully in one conversation today.

pages.q: A soft tongue accomplishes what force cannot.

259.pq: For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.

p: Baptism is not just a step you took. It is something you were given to wear, every day since.
Being clothed in Christ means His identity now covers yours, wherever you go.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you live today as one clothed in Christ.

pages.q: For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.

pages.prompt: How could living 'clothed in Christ' shape your choices today?

o.l: I can let His example guide a decision I'm facing.
o.r: Ask what someone clothed in Christ would choose here, and let that guide your decision today.

o.l: I can represent Him well in how I treat someone.
o.r: You are wearing His name today. Let your treatment of someone reflect that.

o.l: I can remember this covering when I feel inadequate.
o.r: When you feel inadequate today, remember you are not facing it alone or unclothed. Christ covers you.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However being clothed in Christ shapes today, remember it is a covering you were given, not one you earned.

p: This is not a garment you put on once and set aside.
In Colossians 3:9-10 we read: “Lie not one to another, seeing that ye have put off the old man with his deeds.”
It is worn daily, in every choice that reflects whose you have become.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Colossians 3:9-10
Think of one way to act like the Savior today. Do it.

pages.q: You are not just baptized once. You are clothed, every day since.

260.pq: Being enriched in every thing to all bountifulness, which causeth through us thanksgiving to God.

p: What you've been given was never meant to stop with you.
True abundance flows through you toward others, and back to God in thanksgiving.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help your gratitude overflow into generosity today.

pages.q: Being enriched in every thing to all bountifulness, which causeth through us thanksgiving to God.

pages.prompt: How could your own abundance overflow toward someone else today?

o.l: I can share something I've been given, not just keep it.
o.r: What you've received was meant to flow through you. Share it today, rather than only keeping it.

o.l: I can let gratitude lead me to give generously.
o.r: Let today's gratitude become today's generosity. The two were always meant to move together.

o.l: I can thank God specifically for what enriches my life.
o.r: Name specifically today what has enriched you, and let that gratitude reach all the way to God.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However overflow shows up in your life today, remember it was never meant to stop with you.

p: Abundance that stays with you is only half the gift.
In Luke 6:38 we read: “Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom.”
Let it move through you today, into thanksgiving and into generosity.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Luke 6:38
Say thanks to three people today for something they did.

pages.q: What flows through you multiplies. What stops with you does not.

261.pq: Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.

p: You do not need to approach God timidly, as though your need might be unwelcome.
He invites boldness, not hesitation, especially when you need help most.
Take a moment to pray and ask God for the confidence to come to Him boldly today.

pages.q: Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.

pages.prompt: Where could you approach God more boldly today?

o.l: I can ask Him plainly for help I've been hesitant to request.
o.r: Ask plainly today for the help you've been hesitant to request. He invites boldness, not hesitation.

o.l: I can bring a need I've been embarrassed to bring before.
o.r: Bring that need to Him today, without the embarrassment. He already knows, and He welcomes you anyway.

o.l: I can trust that mercy, not judgment, waits for me there.
o.r: Approach Him today trusting mercy is what waits for you, not judgment.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However boldness shows up in your prayers today, remember He invites it, rather than merely tolerating it.

p: The throne of grace was never meant to be approached with fear.
In Ephesians 3:12 we read: “In whom we have boldness and access with confidence by the faith of him.”
Come to it today boldly, trusting mercy and help are exactly what's waiting there.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Ephesians 3:12
Pray today with confidence. Tell God what you really need.

pages.q: You were invited to come boldly, not to wait timidly.

262.pq: That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good…

p: God's generosity does not wait for you to deserve it first.
He gives sunlight and rain freely, to the grateful and the ungrateful alike.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you reflect that same generosity today.

pages.q: That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.

pages.prompt: How could you reflect God's generosity to someone today, deserving or not?

o.l: I can be kind to someone who hasn't earned it from me.
o.r: Offer kindness today to someone who hasn't earned it, the way God's sun and rain reach everyone freely.

o.l: I can give without first checking if it's deserved.
o.r: Give today without weighing whether it's deserved. That's exactly how God's generosity works.

o.l: I can trust that His generosity toward me isn't based on my performance.
o.r: Rest today in the truth that His generosity toward you was never based on your performance.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However generosity shows up today, remember it was never meant to be rationed only to the deserving.

p: God's generosity is not selective. It reaches everyone, whether they've earned it or not.
In Luke 6:35 we read: “But love ye your enemies, and do good, and lend, hoping for nothing again.”
Let that same generosity shape how you give today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Luke 6:35
Show kindness today to someone who is not kind to you.

pages.q: His generosity was never rationed only to the deserving.

263.pq: For I am the LORD, I change not; therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed.

p: In a world where nearly everything shifts, God's character remains exactly the same.
The God who kept His promises generations ago is the same God keeping them now.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you trust His unchanging nature today.

pages.q: For I am the LORD, I change not; therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed.

pages.prompt: Where could God's unchanging nature give you steadiness today?

o.l: I can trust He's the same even in a season that feels uncertain.
o.r: Circumstances shift, but He hasn't. Trust that steadiness today, even in the uncertainty.

o.l: I can remember He kept His promises before, and will again.
o.r: Look back at a promise He already kept, and let that memory steady your trust today.

o.l: I can rely on His character instead of my changing feelings.
o.r: Your feelings may shift today. His character will not. Anchor to that instead.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However God's unchanging nature steadies you today, remember He is the same today as He has always been.

p: Everything around you may shift. He does not.
In Hebrews 13:8 we read: “Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever.”
Rest today in a God whose character has never once wavered.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Hebrews 13:8
Write one thing about God that never changes. Take comfort in it.

pages.q: Everything shifts around you. He does not.

264.theme: Living in the Light of Truth
264.pq: And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.

p: Truth is not just information. It is freedom.
Living in the light of truth means refusing to hide from what is real, even when it is uncomfortable.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.

pages.prompt: Where could embracing truth bring you greater freedom today?

o.l: I can be honest with myself about a difficult reality
o.r: Avoiding the truth does not make it go away. Look at the situation honestly, and decide what you can do from where you actually are.

o.l: I can stop pretending everything is fine when it is not
o.r: Pretending takes energy that could be used for real change. Let yourself feel what is real, and then find help and strength to address it.

o.l: I can build my life on what is true, not what is easy
o.r: The easy path is not always the true path. Choose to stand on what you know is right, even when it costs you something.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Ask yourself: what truth have I been avoiding? Bring it into the light today. The truth may be uncomfortable, but it is the only foundation for real freedom.

p: Truth does not always feel good in the moment, but it is the only thing that can set you free.
In John 14:6 we read: “Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life.”
Choose to live in the light today. It is the path to lasting peace.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in John 14:6
Choose to follow the truth in one small decision today.

pages.q: Truth is not a burden. It is the door to freedom.

265.pq: Giving thanks always for all things unto God and the Father in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ;

p: A life of gratitude is a life of joy.
It is not about ignoring hardship, but about choosing to see the good alongside it.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: Giving thanks always for all things unto God and the Father in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ;

pages.prompt: How can you weave gratitude more deeply into your daily life?

o.l: I can start each day by thanking God for one thing
o.r: Begin your day with gratitude. Even before you open your eyes, thank God for something, and let that be the first thought that sets the tone for your day.

o.l: I can pause when something good happens and say thank you
o.r: Good things often pass by unnoticed. When something good happens, stop for a moment and thank God right then.

o.l: I can keep a simple record of blessings I notice
o.r: Writing down small blessings can help you see God's hand more clearly. A simple note can serve as a reminder on difficult days.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Find a way to make gratitude a habit, not just an occasional thought. It takes practice, but the practice is worth it.

p: Gratitude changes how you experience life. It opens your eyes to what is already good.
In Psalm 106:1 we read: “Praise ye the LORD. O give thanks unto the LORD; for he is good.”
Make gratitude a daily practice. It will not remove difficulty, but it will give you strength to face it.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Psalm 106:1
Write ten things you are grateful for. Read them aloud.

pages.q: A grateful heart is a magnet for peace.

266.pq: But whoso hath this world's good, and seeth his brother have need, and shutteth up his bowels of compassion from him…

p: Compassion is not just a feeling. It is action.
Seeing a need and responding is how love becomes real.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: But whoso hath this world's good, and seeth his brother have need, and shutteth up his bowels of compassion from him, how dwelleth the love of God in him?

pages.prompt: Where can you turn compassion into action today?

o.l: I can help someone I see struggling
o.r: A need is often right in front of you. You do not need to solve everything, just do one thing that lightens someone's load today.

o.l: I can be more patient with someone who is having a hard day
o.r: Patience is a form of compassion. Giving someone space to struggle without criticism is a gift that costs nothing but means everything.

o.l: I can share something I have with someone who needs it
o.r: You have something that someone else lacks. Whether it is time, attention, or a material need, sharing it is an act of love.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Let God show you a need you can meet. Then do it, not for recognition, but because love is meant to move.

p: Love is not real until it reaches someone else. Compassion becomes real when it is acted on.
In Matthew 25:35-36 we read: “For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink.”
Look around you today. There is someone who needs what you can give.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Matthew 25:35-36
Help someone today with something real: food, time, or a ride.

pages.q: Compassion without action is just a feeling. Compassion with action is love.

267.theme: The Fruit of a Quiet Heart
267.pq: The heart of the wise teacheth his mouth, and addeth learning to his lips.

p: What is in your heart will eventually come out through your words.
A quiet heart is not empty. It is full of wisdom that knows when and how to speak.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: The heart of the wise teacheth his mouth, and addeth learning to his lips.

pages.prompt: How can you cultivate a quieter, wiser heart today?

o.l: I can think before I speak
o.r: Your words are a reflection of what is in your heart. Let the first pause be a moment to decide whether what you are about to say is helpful and true.

o.l: I can listen more than I talk today
o.r: You already know what you think. Listening is how you learn something new. Give someone else the gift of being heard.

o.l: I can spend time in quiet reflection
o.r: A busy mind cannot hear wisdom. Give yourself space to be still, even for a few minutes, and let your heart become calm.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Find a way to slow down today. A quiet heart is not hurried, and it speaks with more care.

p: Wisdom does not shout. It speaks quietly and clearly.
In Proverbs 15:4 we read: “A wholesome tongue is a tree of life: but perverseness therein is a breach in the spirit.”
Let your heart become a source of wisdom through stillness and thoughtfulness.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Proverbs 15:4
Speak calmly today, even when you are tired or frustrated.

pages.q: A quiet heart speaks words that others can actually hear.

268.pq: And the LORD God planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed.

p: God placed the first people in a garden. A place of simple, quiet beauty.
Joy does not require complexity. Often it is found in the simplest things: sunlight, a moment of peace, a kind word.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: And the LORD God planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed.

pages.prompt: How can you find joy in something simple today?

o.l: I can notice something beautiful in nature
o.r: A single flower, the warmth of sunlight, or the sound of rain. Each is a gift from a creative God. Pause long enough to see it today.

o.l: I can appreciate a quiet moment
o.r: You do not always need to be doing something. A quiet moment without productivity is not wasted. It is a chance to rest.

o.l: I can enjoy a simple pleasure without guilt
o.r: God gave you the capacity to enjoy good things. A good meal, a laugh with a friend, a moment of rest. Receive it as a gift.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose something simple and good, and let yourself be fully present in it. Joy often hides in the ordinary.

p: You do not have to wait for a big event to find joy.
In Ecclesiastes 5:18-19 we read: “It is good and comely for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy the good of all his labour.”
The simple things are often the most lasting. Let them be enough today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Ecclesiastes 5:18-19
Enjoy one simple thing today: a meal, a walk, or a view. Thank God.

pages.q: Joy is often found in the simplest places. If you take time to look.

269.pq: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

p: Repentance is not punishment. It is the way back.
God does not want to condemn you. He wants to welcome you home.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

pages.prompt: What step can you take toward sincere repentance today?

o.l: I can honestly acknowledge something I have done wrong
o.r: Honesty is the first step. Stop hiding the wrong, even from yourself. Acknowledge it fully and bring it to God.

o.l: I can turn away from a pattern I have been stuck in
o.r: Turning away is not easy, but it is necessary. You do not have to be perfect today. You just need to start moving in a new direction.

o.l: I can trust that God will forgive me
o.r: The hardest part of repentance is often accepting God's forgiveness. Believe that He has already made a way for you to be clean.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Wherever you are on the path of repentance, do not stop. He is waiting for you with open arms.

p: Repentance is not about earning God's love. It is about returning to it.
In Mosiah 26:29-30 we read: “Therefore I say unto you, Go; and whosoever transgresseth against me, him shall ye judge according to the sins which he has committed.”
Come home today. He is faithful, and He is waiting.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Mosiah 26:29-30
Write one thing you want to change. Pray for help to begin.

pages.q: Repentance is the path home. He is waiting at the door.

270.pq: But the meek shall inherit the earth; and shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace.

p: Humility is rarely rewarded quickly or loudly in this world.
But God promises it a lasting inheritance, and a peace that outlasts louder pursuits.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you trust the quiet path of humility today.

pages.q: But the meek shall inherit the earth; and shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace.

pages.prompt: Where could humility open the door to real peace today?

o.l: I can let go of needing to win an argument.
o.r: Let the argument go today, even if you could win it. Peace is often worth more than being right.

o.l: I can trust God's timing instead of pushing my own way.
o.r: Trust His timing today, instead of forcing your own. Humility often waits where pride would push.

o.l: I can choose peace over proving a point.
o.r: Choose peace today, even when proving your point feels tempting. It rarely delivers what humility does.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However humility shows up today, remember it leads toward a peace pride rarely finds.

p: The humble rarely make headlines. But they often find a peace the proud never do.
In Matthew 5:5 we read: “Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth.”
Choose that quiet path today, trusting its promised reward.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Matthew 5:5
Do one quiet act of humility today, like letting someone go first.

pages.q: The humble rarely make headlines, but they often find real peace.

271.pq: And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together…

p: Faith is not meant to be lived alone.
God places people in your life to encourage, challenge, and strengthen you.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another.

pages.prompt: How can you strengthen someone in your community today?

o.l: I can reach out to someone I have not seen in a while
o.r: A simple message can remind someone that they are remembered. You may be the encouragement they did not know they needed.

o.l: I can offer help without waiting to be asked
o.r: Waiting to be asked can sometimes mean waiting too long. Offer help freely and without expectation.

o.l: I can express appreciation to someone who serves
o.r: Service is often quiet and unseen. Let someone know that their efforts have not gone unnoticed.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Look around your community. There is someone who needs to know they are seen. Be that person for them today.

p: You are not meant to carry your burdens alone. God often answers our prayers through the hands of others.
In Romans 12:4-5 we read: “For as we have many members in one body, and all members have not the same office.”
Be that answer for someone else today.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Romans 12:4-5
Join with others today in one good activity or conversation.

pages.q: We are stronger together than we could ever be alone.

272.pq: Well, thou good servant: because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.

p: Great responsibility is rarely handed to those who haven't proven faithful in small things first.
What looks unimportant today may be exactly what's being tested for something greater.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you be faithful in today's small responsibilities.

pages.q: Well, thou good servant: because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.

pages.prompt: What small responsibility today deserves your full faithfulness?

o.l: I will complete a small task with real care, not just haste.
o.r: Give that small task real care today, not just haste. Faithfulness in little things is rarely wasted.

o.l: I will follow through on something easy to let slide.
o.r: Follow through today on the thing that would be easy to let slide. It matters more than it seems.

o.l: I will trust that small faithfulness is preparing me for more.
o.r: Trust today that this small faithfulness is quietly preparing you for something greater.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However faithfulness shows up in small things today, remember nothing given care is ever truly wasted.

p: Greatness is rarely handed out first. It is built, quietly, in how you handle what's small.
In Matthew 25:21 we read: “His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant.”
Be faithful today in the little that's in front of you.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Matthew 25:21
Do one small good thing today carefully. Treat it as important.

pages.q: What looks small today may be exactly what's being tested for tomorrow.

273.pq: For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:

p: Forgiveness is not just a gift you give to others. It is a gift you give to yourself.
Holding onto resentment keeps you bound to the person who hurt you. Letting go sets you free.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:

pages.prompt: Who can you forgive today. For your own peace, not just for theirs?

o.l: I can forgive someone who has not apologized
o.r: Your forgiveness does not depend on the other person. You can let go of the hurt even if they never acknowledge it.

o.l: I can stop expecting someone to be perfect
o.r: People will let you down. That is part of being human. Let go of the expectation that they should be flawless, and set down your own disappointment.

o.l: I can forgive myself for something I have been carrying
o.r: You have already repented, but you are still punishing yourself. God has forgiven you. Let yourself receive that forgiveness too.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Examine your heart today. Who are you still holding a grudge against? Choose to release them, not because they deserve it, but because you deserve to be free.

p: Forgiveness is not about forgetting or excusing. It is about releasing the weight you were never meant to carry.
In Luke 17:3 we read: “Take heed to yourselves: If thy brother trespass against thee, rebuke him.”
Let go today. You are the one who needs the freedom.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Luke 17:3
Forgive one small thing today and let it go completely.

pages.q: Forgiveness is the key that unlocks the door you have been standing behind.

274.pq: But the LORD is in his holy temple: let all the earth keep silence before him.

p: There are moments that call for words, and moments that simply call for stillness.
Standing quietly before God can say more than any prayer you could form in words.
Take a moment to actually sit in silence before continuing today.

pages.q: But the LORD is in his holy temple: let all the earth keep silence before him.

pages.prompt: Where could quiet stillness before God serve you better than words today?

o.l: I can sit in silence instead of filling every prayer with requests.
o.r: Try today sitting in silence before Him, without filling every moment with requests.

o.l: I can let go of needing an immediate answer to everything.
o.r: Release the need for an immediate answer today, and simply be still in His presence.

o.l: I can quiet my own thoughts long enough to actually listen.
o.r: Quiet your own thoughts today, even briefly, and make room to actually listen.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However stillness shows up before God today, remember silence can say what words cannot.

p: Not every moment with God needs to be filled with words.
In Zephaniah 1:7 we read: “Hold thy peace at the presence of the Lord GOD: for the day of the LORD is at hand.”
Sometimes the most honest prayer is simply standing quietly in His presence.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Zephaniah 1:7
Be quiet before God for five minutes today. Do not ask for anything.

pages.q: Sometimes silence says what words cannot.

275.pq: The just man walketh in his integrity: his children are blessed after him.

p: A life of integrity does not just protect you. It quietly shapes the people who come after you.
The way you walk today leaves a path others may follow, whether you intend it or not.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help your integrity today become a blessing to others.

pages.q: The just man walketh in his integrity: his children are blessed after him.

pages.prompt: How could your integrity today bless someone who's watching?

o.l: I will make an honest choice, even if no one would notice otherwise.
o.r: Make that honest choice today, even unseen. Someone may be watching more closely than you think.

o.l: I will model integrity for someone younger who looks up to me.
o.r: Someone younger may be learning integrity from watching you today. Model it deliberately.

o.l: I will choose the harder honest path over the easier one.
o.r: Choose the harder, honest path today, even when the easier one would go unnoticed.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However integrity shows up today, remember it quietly shapes more than just your own life.

p: Integrity is rarely just personal. It becomes a path others walk after you.
In Psalm 25:21 we read: “Let integrity and uprightness preserve me; for I wait on thee.”
Walk it faithfully today, for your own sake and for theirs.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Psalm 25:21
Choose to be honest today in one place where it would be easier not to be.

pages.q: The way you walk today becomes a path someone else may follow.

276.pq: By him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of our lips giving thanks to his name.

p: Praise is not only for the easy days. It can be offered as a genuine sacrifice, even in a hard one.
Giving thanks when it costs you something is often the most meaningful praise you can offer.
Take a moment to pray and offer God praise today, even if it takes real effort to mean it.

pages.q: By him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of our lips giving thanks to his name.

pages.prompt: Where could offering praise today feel more like a sacrifice than a habit?

o.l: I can thank God even in the middle of a hard circumstance.
o.r: Offer thanks today even in the hard circumstance. That kind of praise costs something, and means more for it.

o.l: I can praise Him before I see the outcome I'm hoping for.
o.r: Praise Him today before the outcome arrives, trusting He's already worthy of it.

o.l: I can make thanksgiving a deliberate act, not just a passing feeling.
o.r: Make thanksgiving deliberate today, a real act, not just a fleeting feeling.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However praise costs you something today, remember that kind of offering is exactly what makes it real.

p: The easiest praise is the kind that costs nothing. The most meaningful often costs something real.
In Psalm 50:14 we read: “Offer unto God thanksgiving; and pay thy vows unto the most High.”
Offer that kind today, and let it be genuine.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Psalm 50:14
Offer a short prayer of praise today. Use your own words.

pages.q: The praise that costs you something is often the praise that means the most.

277.pq: O worship the LORD in the beauty of holiness: fear before him, all the earth.

p: There is a kind of awe that comes from truly recognizing who God is, not just believing facts about Him.
That awe is not meant to push you away, but to draw you into deeper reverence.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you feel genuine awe in His presence today.

pages.q: O worship the LORD in the beauty of holiness: fear before him, all the earth.

pages.prompt: Where could a deeper sense of awe change how you approach God today?

o.l: I can slow down before prayer instead of rushing into it.
o.r: Slow down before you pray today, and let real awe settle in before you begin.

o.l: I can remember His majesty, not just His familiarity.
o.r: Remember today that He is not only familiar, but truly majestic. Let that shape your reverence.

o.l: I can approach worship today with genuine trembling, not routine.
o.r: Approach worship today with real awe, not just routine motion through familiar words.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However awe shows up in your worship today, remember it draws you closer, not further away.

p: Familiarity with God should never fully replace awe of Him.
In 1 Chronicles 16:29 we read: “Give unto the LORD the glory due unto his name: bring an offering, and come before him.”
Let today's worship hold both. Closeness, and genuine reverence.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in 1 Chronicles 16:29
Take a quiet moment of reverence for God today.

pages.q: Closeness to God should never fully replace awe of Him.

278.pq: And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.

p: Regret can keep you looking backward. God invites you to look forward.
Peace does not come from a perfect past. It comes from trusting a perfect God with your future.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.

pages.prompt: What is one thing you can release to live without regret today?

o.l: I can let go of a past mistake I keep replaying
o.r: You have already repented. Let the past be past. Replaying it over and over only keeps you stuck.

o.l: I can stop wishing things had turned out differently
o.r: Wishing does not change what happened. Trust that God has already used your past for good, even if you cannot see it yet.

o.l: I can trust God with my future instead of worrying
o.r: You cannot change the past, and you cannot fully control the future. But you can trust the One who holds both.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Give God your regrets today. Exchange them for His peace. He is not finished with your story.

p: Peace is not found in a perfect past. It is found in a present trust in God.
In John 14:27 we read: “Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you.”
Let go of regret today. He has already made a way forward.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in John 14:27
Let go of one regret today. Pray for peace.

pages.q: Peace is not the absence of regret. It is trusting God with what you cannot change.

279.pq: Be patient therefore, brethren, unto the coming of the Lord. Behold, the husbandman waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth…

p: Patience is not passive. It is active trust.
Just as a farmer waits for the harvest, you can wait for God's timing with steady faith.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: Be patient therefore, brethren, unto the coming of the Lord. Behold, the husbandman waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth, and hath long patience for it, until he receive the early and latter rain.

pages.prompt: Where can you practice patience with God's timing today?

o.l: I can trust that God's delay is not denial
o.r: A delayed answer is not a rejected prayer. God's timing is often different from yours, but it is always right.

o.l: I can stop trying to force a situation to resolve
o.r: You cannot force most things into being ready. Sometimes the best thing you can do is wait, and trust.

o.l: I can continue doing good while I wait
o.r: Waiting is not doing nothing. Keep serving, keep trusting, keep moving forward. The harvest will come in its season.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose to trust God with the timing of something important today. Your patience is not wasted. It is preparing you.

p: Patience is not about waiting passively. It is about trusting actively.
In Romans 8:25 we read: “But if we hope for that we see not, then do we with patience wait for it.”
The harvest will come. Until then, keep doing good and trusting God's timing.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Romans 8:25
Practice patience once today in a small, ordinary moment.

pages.q: Patience is not passive waiting. It is active trust in God's timing.

280.theme: The Strength of a Soft Heart
280.pq: Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.

p: A hard heart is heavy. A soft heart is open to peace.
Jesus Christ invites you to learn from His gentleness and find rest for your soul.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.

pages.prompt: What can help you keep your heart soft and open to God?

o.l: I can ask God to soften the hard places in my heart
o.r: You do not have to soften your own heart through willpower alone. Ask God to help you release what has made you hard.

o.l: I can release a resentment I have been holding
o.r: Resentment is one of the things that makes a heart hard. Let go of one grudge today, and let your heart breathe.

o.l: I can remain open to correction
o.r: A soft heart is willing to be taught. When correction comes, receive it with humility instead of resistance.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Examine your heart honestly today. Wherever it has become hard, bring it to Jesus Christ, and let Him make it soft again.

p: A soft heart is not weak. It is open. It can receive, heal, and grow.
In Alma 7:23 we read: “And now I would that ye should be humble, and be submissive and gentle.”
Bring your hardened places to Christ today. He knows how to make them tender again.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Alma 7:23
Do one thing today that shows a gentle spirit.

pages.q: A soft heart is not a weak heart. It is a heart open to God.

281.pq: And walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us, and hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour.

p: To walk in love is to live the way Christ lived.
He gave Himself fully, without reservation. That is the pattern He calls you to follow.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: And walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us, and hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour.

pages.prompt: How can you walk in love more intentionally today?

o.l: I can treat someone the way Christ would treat them
o.r: Imagine Christ standing in your place today. How would He speak? How would He act? Do that.

o.l: I can give without expecting anything in return
o.r: Love does not keep a record of who owes whom. Give freely, your time, your kindness, your help, and expect nothing back.

o.l: I can be patient with someone who is hard to love
o.r: Love is often most real when it is difficult. Choose patience and kindness today toward someone who tries your patience.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Let your actions today be shaped by love. Walk in the way Christ walked, giving, serving, and loving without limit.

p: Love is not just a feeling. It is a way of walking.
In John 13:34-35 we read: “A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another.”
Walk in love today, and let your life become an offering to God.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in John 13:34-35
Show love today by serving someone in a way they will not expect.

pages.q: Walking in love means living the way Christ lived. Fully and without reservation.

282.pq: Verily I say unto you, Except ye be converted, and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.

p: Faith does not need to be complicated.
Children trust without overthinking. They simply believe. That is the kind of faith God is asking you to have.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: Verily I say unto you, Except ye be converted, and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.

pages.prompt: Where can you simplify your faith and trust like a child today?

o.l: I can trust God without needing to understand everything first
o.r: Children do not need every detail before they trust. You do not have to understand everything to trust the One who does.

o.l: I can bring my needs to God with simple honesty
o.r: You do not need perfect words. A child does not prepare a speech before asking. Just ask, simply and honestly.

o.l: I can let go of the need to have all the answers
o.r: Faith is not having all the answers. It is trusting the One who does. Let go of the need to know everything.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Simplify your approach to God today. Come to Him as you are, without pretense, and trust Him with a childlike heart.

p: Faith does not need to be complicated. It only needs to be real.
In Mark 10:15 we read: “Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child, he shall not enter therein.”
Come to God today with the simple, trusting heart of a child.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Mark 10:15
Pray today with the simple faith of a child.

pages.q: Faith is not complicated. It is simply trusting the One who knows everything.

283.pq: The soul of the sluggard desireth, and hath nothing: but the soul of the diligent shall be made fat.

p: Good intentions are not enough. Real change comes through consistent effort.
Diligence is the steady work of showing up day after day.
Take a moment to prepare your heart, and pray before continuing.

pages.q: The soul of the sluggard desireth, and hath nothing: but the soul of the diligent shall be made fat.

pages.prompt: Where can greater diligence lead to a better outcome in your life?

o.l: I can continue a good habit even when I do not feel like it
o.r: Motivation comes and goes. Diligence is what keeps you going when motivation is gone. Keep showing up.

o.l: I can follow through on something I have been avoiding
o.r: Avoidance only makes the task heavier. Start today, even if you cannot finish it all at once.

o.l: I can give my full attention to one task at a time
o.r: Diligence is not multitasking. It is focused effort. Give one thing your full attention today and see how much more you accomplish.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: Choose one area where consistency matters. Make a plan to show up daily, even in small ways.

p: Diligence is the steady hand that builds a life of purpose.
In Colossians 3:23 we read: “And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.”
Keep showing up. Your efforts are accumulating into something good.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Colossians 3:23
Do one task today with steady effort. Finish it.

pages.q: Diligence is not about being perfect. It is about being faithful.

284.pq: Every purpose is established by counsel: and with good advice make war.

p: Important decisions rarely go well when made entirely alone, in a rush, without wise input.
Seeking good counsel before a major decision is not weakness. It is wisdom.
Take a moment to pray and ask God to help you seek wise counsel before your next big decision.

pages.q: Every purpose is established by counsel: and with good advice make war.

pages.prompt: Where could seeking wise counsel change the outcome of a decision today?

o.l: I can ask someone wise before making a major choice.
o.r: Before that major choice, ask someone wise for their honest perspective today.

o.l: I can slow down instead of deciding entirely alone.
o.r: Slow down today, and let a decision be shaped by more than just your own view.

o.l: I can seek God's counsel first, before anyone else's.
o.r: Bring the decision to God first today, before seeking anyone else's advice.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However counsel shapes your decisions today, remember wisdom rarely comes from isolation.

p: A decision made in isolation is often a decision made too quickly.
In Proverbs 24:6 we read: “For by wise counsel thou shalt make thy war: and in multitude of counsellors there is safety.”
Seek wise counsel today, and let your plans be established, not rushed.

pages.h: Here are some ways you can go deeper with your study of this verse:
a: Study related verses in Proverbs 24:6
Ask two people for advice today before making one decision.

pages.q: A decision made alone is often a decision made too quickly.

285.pq: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.

p: This may be one of the most familiar verses you know, and still one of the most reassuring.
It is a simple declaration of trust: with God as your shepherd, you genuinely lack nothing essential.
Take a moment to pray and let this simple trust settle over you before continuing.

pages.q: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.

pages.prompt: Where could you trust God's provision more fully today?

o.l: I can trust He is providing, even when I can't yet see how.
o.r: Trust today that provision is already underway, even before you can see exactly how.

o.l: I can stop worrying about something I don't actually lack.
o.r: Notice today what you don't actually lack, and let that quiet a worry you've been carrying.

o.l: I can rest in His care instead of trying to provide everything myself.
o.r: Rest today in His care, instead of carrying the full weight of provision yourself.

o.l: I can do something else
o.r: However trust in His provision shows up today, remember He has never once failed to shepherd you.

p: A shepherd does not abandon the flock partway through. Neither does this One.
In John 10:11 we read: “I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.”
Trust today that what you need, He is already providing.
